title: Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp Memorial Tour from Berlin
description: Get the most out of your visit to Sachsenhausen, one of the first concentration camps in Germany, by touring with a guide. On this full-day tour from Berlin, you'll listen to a historian detail the influence of the Third Reich and the timeline of how this camp came to be. Travel via train from Berlin with your guide (ticket at own expense) which eliminates the need to rent a car.

reviews.usertext: Xavier was an amazing host. He was really good about explaining every detail of the camp. Even the small stuff I would not normally notice he pointed out and told us the significance. He also knows a ton and was able to answer any of our questions. I’m not normally a tour person but I’m glad I booked this one because it taught me way more then I would of read on the plaques. Especially just the walk into the camp had history and relevance. I would recommend buying the ABC train pass ahead of time because you won’t have a lot of time before you leave. This also saves the tour guide frustration because he has a time constraint and if he misses that train you have to wait a while and it cuts time away from the camp tour. You don’t get a chance eat so make sure you have a good breakfast or snacks. Xavier walks fast but I think he is trying to give you the best opportunity to learn and see everything. He does wait for the whole group before talking so you don’t ever feel rushed. The tour starts and ends on the train. Xavier gave us details the whole way so make sure you are close enough to hear him. Ask him about his Grandpa because he has a first hand experience of what it was like to survive a concentration camp. This story was one one of the best parts of the tour.

Sachsenhausen concentration camp was a moving and I believe valuable experience for my wife and I. I would definitely recommend a visit to a concentration camp to clearly understand the depths mankind will go through for power and control over others. There was a logistical issue and a weather issue outside the control of our guide, however there were a couple things he could have done to make our experience better. First. There is about a one mile walk from the end of the train line to the camp entrance. Our group was very diverse with young and old alike. Our guide basically left a portion of the group that walked slower even after being asked a number of times to please slow down. Secondly, he seemed to not connect well with his group. If you weren’t able to keep up moving through the rain at the camp, you missed portions of his narrative which became rather frustrating. Overall his knowledge of the subject matter was very good and he projected when he could so that the group could hear him clearly. Overall the site was worthwhile, the tour guide should have been more responsive to his clients.

Irish Jamie was our superb tour guide in October 2022, extremely knowledgable with a lovely nature. It's unthinkable that this hell hole actually existed and the memorial gives a detailed insight into the atrocities that occurred there. Too much to absorb in one day but Jamie selected the 'highlights' and we were welcome to stay on to see more after the tour if liked. Although a large group, he was attentive and kept everyone together allowing time for browsing the exhibits independently. Yes a lot of walking and you need to take food, drink, and buy your train ticket beforehand. We were lucky to have beautiful warm, sunny, autumn day to take the chill off the ghastliness. I would say not suitable for children.

Great tour with Sarah, who was extremely knowledgeable and dealt with the difficult subject-matter in a sensitive and respectful way. This was a sombre day out but something that we felt we should not avoid while in Berlin. Our teen was worried that she would find some of the content too distressing, but it was possible for her to avoid the most difficult sections and was glad she had come.
One practical point, there is no official break for lunch during the tour. The museum understandably want to avoid the air of groups having picnics in the grounds. We had brought sandwiches and ended up eating them standing up while listening to Sarah explain part of the camp to us, which felt a little awkward. I'd advise eating an early lunch on the train before arriving at the camp.

This was a sobering and very educational experience. Our guide Ernestina was thoughtful, attentive, knowledgeable. I truly enjoyed myself. A few things to note:
(1) if you get the BVG app, it’s super easy to buy tickets (which is not included in the app)
(2) as of current time, you must wear a mask on the train
(3) pick up food (finger food) + drinks before the tour. You get about 10 min to eat during a quick toilet break before entering Sachsenhausen concentration camp. No food/drink allowed inside (although water is ok)
(4) during the first pee break at the souvenir store, just pee. You won’t get another chance till much much later.

10/10 will recommend

Excellent tour on 9/24 with Irish Jamie! He detailed the history from the formation of the Republic to the period discussed, specifically that of the 3rd Reich. He was very enlightening and covered everything that happened in the buildings of Sachsenhausen. He was very respectful to the memory of those who were in the camp and to those who never made it out.

Although Sachsenhausen was a work camp initially, many lost their lives within its walls. You will visit the area where people were exterminated but can ask to not see these particular rooms. The topics covered are very painful but extremely important. Jamie's tour was thought provoking and thorough.

He ends the tour discussing consequences and justice.

Good walking shoes are recommended as you walk one mile to the camp from the train station of Oranienburg and one mile back. At the camp itself, you walk for 2-3 hours. Bring snacks/lunch/drinks.

We did the 10-4 Saschenhausen tour in October 2022. We are a family of 4 (12 & 15 year old kids) and it was our first time in Berlin. Our tour guide Martin was easy to find at the meeting point and immediately began giving us the history of the camp. We were in a group of 18 People so not too large, and Martin looked after us for the train ride to the camp. He was very informative, patient and had a great loud voice for a tour guide. We were encouraged to ask questions and he was able to answer all of them. Easy to understand and a must for everyone to visit here. We would definitely recommend this company and our tour guide Martin
Sam, England

Our guide Ernestina (Tina) was amazing, she was so passionate in sharing her knowledge of the camp and the atrocities that happened.
I thought I understood what happened here, I was wrong -having a truly knowledgeable guide talk you through the build up of to the 2nd world war and the use of camps is a true eye opener.
I would highly recommend this tour for anyone visiting Berlin, the train journey and walk to the camp are all straight forward and ultimately poignant as you realise that some of those held in Sachsenhausen made the same journey.

Nick gave such good history and stories about what went on due to his background that I am not sure we would normally have seen. EVERYONE must see this. Only warning is its a 15 minute walk from the train station and then walking the camp (did 17,000 steps that day) so if you have trouble walking or keeping up would be better to go there yourself and tour rather than booking this tour through the site. One of the highlights of my trip

If you are visiting Berlin and wanting an expert view of history; I highly recommend the concentration camp tour with Martin. He’s is phenomenal and connects the dots of world events that lead to the Holocaust. Martin is a wealth of knowledge and really enjoys the many questions we asked. His passion for this topic is evident. You will not go wrong with having Martin as your guide!

This was the first thing we did on our 5 day stay to Berlin and I'm glad we started off with it. Our tour guide Jamie got us set up with public transportation tickets and guided us through the train system which gave us more confidence to use it later in our trip. Jamie gave a detailed overview of German history on our train ride to the camp memorial and did an excellent job of delivering some of Germany's difficult history is a respectful manner. We would definitely recommend this trip for anyone visiting Berlin.

We met near a train station. The guide provided an introduction to the tour. The train took roughly one hour to get to the destination and then we walked for half an hour more to get to the camp. The guide took us through the main landmarks in the camp and provided detailed explanations and answers to the questions. Definitely, he had very good command of history regarding this camp. There's only one con that matters for people who travel on a budget: you may buy your own train ticket (9 EUR for a one-minth ticket) and an audio guide (3 EUR). The entry to the camp is free.

Fascinating, sobering and very informative. Martin was an excellent guide with an obvious interest in the subject. He had lots of stories which made it feel very real. We went with 2 older teenagers and they said it was their favourite day in Berlin. A word of warning - the day involves a lot of walking (13K+ steps!) although I did notice some people getting a bus from the Concentration camp back to the train station (which would avoid a 2km walk) So come prepared with suitable shoes!

Nikolai was v knowledgeable & struck the right tone. He had an extremely tough job taking a tour out to such a destination in 38 degree heat but made adjustments & made sure to check in on everyone. He was a brisk walker which was required today to keep everyone safe & he briefed us carefully on what to expect before we left. The tour was detailed & interesting without ever feeling like it was sensationalising the events or site itself. It was an important experience & one we will remember. I am sure that Nikolai has a few interesting stories of his own to tell, given the initial ‘synopsis’ he shared of his life!

Nikolai was in charge of our lovely international group imparting his knowledge about the tragically sad tales of those who suffered there. He presented his tour so well and looked after us from the moment we arrived to arranging how we get back safely to wherever we needed to go. Kind, thoughtful, engaging and of course hugely knowledgeable about his subject, Nikolai demonstrated his passion and respect for a place that can educate those who were not witness to the atrocities committed and to make sure that such events should never happen again. The camp is enormous and having a guide really helps one pinpoint the significant parts of it as well as the chance to ask questions. I would recommend this tour to anyone who is interested in those troubled times of the 20th C.

It's possible to visit on your own but we had a guided tour with Jamie G from Insider Tours. I would recommend going with an accredited tour guide, as the site is vast and you may not get the essential context (especially if you can't read German) without help. Jamie was an excellent guide, I understand that the folk from Insider undergo training from the memorial authority and it does make for a better tour in my opinion. This is not a fun experience, and nor should it be. Make sure your grandkids don't forget - bring them on this tour.

We visited sachsenhausen concentration camp on Saturday 24th, Josh (Ohio) was our guide, we started from hackescher Markt just round the corner from our hotel, we had to get a tram which was directly at the Markt to central station and then a train from the station to Oranienburg and from there a 15-20 min walk to sachsenhausen. So quite a bit of walking but nothing which bothered us ☺️ Josh was very friendly and filled with a lot of knowledge he gave us talks and information from the beginning of our journey right through to the end, which some was of Nazi history and then once at sachsenhausen a lot of information on that too. Once you arrive at sachsenhausen you are on a schedule so there wasn’t a chance to visit all of the museum inside of the concentration camp but our guide gave as much information as he could on most of the history and stories behind it. But we did have the option to stay at the concentration camp if we wanted to spend longer there. Overall it was an excellent experience, highly recommend it being a top priority when visiting Berlin, gives you a complete inside of what really happened and such an eye opener. Glad we visited.

Campbell was our guide for our tour to Sachsenhausen. He was very knowledgeable and was able to explain the history of Germany and the camp in great detail, as well as answer all the questions that came his way. He clearly has a passion for history. The tour was very well organised even though we weren’t, we had forgotten to bring an umbrella but luckily Campbell had a spare which he lent to us when the rain came down. If you are in Berlin you should add this to your itinerary, you could do the tour yourself but having a knowledgeable guide is highly recommended

Our tour guide, Josh was excellent, he made the tour very very interesting by adding in pieces of history we had no idea about, some of this you would definitely not experience from other tour guides. Even while waiting for the bus or train he would give information relevant to the tour that you would not find out otherwise.

He had a great knowledge of WWII, the most I have ever seen. The facts he gave were all very interesting. Although the tour itself was very interesting, I couldnt recommend getting this tour guide enough just because of how much more knowledge you had on the camp while going through it with him.

Be sure to bring food and water as there is not anything there to get and the tour is long (which it flies!)

This place is an absolute must see. We had Maria as our tour guide and she was brilliant at giving plenty of interesting facts, information and history.

She was extremely knowledgeable and helpful. Admission into the camp is free, but I would 100% recommend going with a tour guide as I learned so much from Maria that couldn’t be found on a plaque or an audio guide.

This place isn’t gory or scary, but it is quite unbelievable to experience the true horrors that really happened. This tour is one we were really glad we did, if you’re considering going - definitely go! Wear good walking shoes, wrap up warm and take a bottle of water & lunch with you.

Our guide, Asaf, was great and knowledgeable! He made history come alive through his sharings. It's a pity though that some of the exhibits at the camp were closed. Please get your ABC tickets, or 24h ABC before hand so the whole group doesn't wait for you if you're signing up for this tour.

Fantastic tour, would highly recommend. Nikolai made the whole experience really easy. Tour was very informative and interesting. Nikolai really knows what he is talking about and was amazing at sharing the many horrible stories of life at the camp (much better than an audio guide!). He talked us through the entire day and made sure everyone knew exactly what was going on. Would definitely recommend, thanks again Nikolai for a fascinating and eye-opening day.

Our guide was friendly, informative and helpful. History of Sachsenhausen was really interesting and helps us understand how the Nazis started their campaign against others before the war. They just turned the dial up once WW2 started. Would definitely recommend this day trip to anyone, actually if more people went and understood why and how, perhaps we would rethink how we treat others today in 2022. Lessons from the past which are relevant today

We had our first and only tour arranged in Berlin (as we found it is better to have a tour guide to explain the stories to us). Our guide, Walid was very helpful and considerate. He looked after us by giving us interesting facts and also catered for the different physical abilities of the participants.

We met at Friedrichstrabe and we had a brief story from Walid about it... it was overall a very meaningful trip!

The trip lasted for 6 hours and do prepare some food and enough water. Sunscreen and hat are highly recommended.

We recommend this tour to those who are interested to know more about Concentration Camp history.

Would absolutely recommend this tour, very informative, powerful but not too long. Was succinct with Nick. Great history and stories of the suffering of the people but also reflective of human nature and human spirit. Would go again with this to a company. Would just recommend that travelers take a sandwich or something to eat before you start the tour or just after you end it.

Our guide Campbell was great! Very informative, patient and generous! There is a ton of information to take in and he was good to let us know that we would not have time to process all of the Camp history and information but he explained so much and gave us time to explore most of the exhibits- including offering to let us stay behind and take a later train if we wanted to see more. It is a long day with a 30-ish minute train ride at each end. Bring food and water!!! We didn't find out that need until we arrived. (We were able to grab things at the train station but would have liked to bring our own.) Hard subject matter covered very well. And at the end Campbell made sure we all got our correct trains/stops!

This tour was touching, amazing and mind blowing to appericate what we have today with the freedom. The tour guide was absolutely amazing, very knowledgeable with the history, compassionate about what he was talking about and humble. I highly recommend this tour for people to go and learn what history done and to respect for those who lost their lives.

Canadian Chris was such a fantastic guide - his tone, approach and knowledge about the area and it’s activity was superior. I will be telling everyone about the this tour and to make sure they get Chris.

Seriously superb, a must for any trip to Berlin. Thank you Chris!

We had a four hour guided tour of Sachsenhausen, leaving from Berlin. This was an outstanding guided tour, led by Martin who was absolutely outstanding.

The tour was sympathetically delivered by Martin, though he didn't avoid any of the 'hard facts' on the tour.

I would recommend this tour and especially Martin every and anytime.

The tour was well organized, and our guide, Chloe, was extremely knowledgeable and very passionate about the subject. With little comments and rethorical questions, it was not merely a recital of facts, but also a thought provoking process. The weather was wet and miserable on the day, which only emphasized the horrible conditions they must have endured during the war. Sadly, there was so much more to see and information to read than there was time for, but Chloe made sure we got the essential information about Sachsenhausen and the general back story around the camps. I would say that a tour of Sachsenhausen or any of the other concentration camps is pretty much mandatory when visiting.

Myself and my partner visited the sachsenhausen concentration camp with tour guide Chloe. Chloe really knew her stuff and fed lots of information to us throughout the tour. It was extremely cold at the camp so wrap up warm and take a bite to eat with you as there isn't much time to grab anything at the cafe. Chloe was both professional and friendly, even gave us a few pointers for places to eat and pubs to really get the feel of the real Berlin... Thank you pizza was great and pub you suggested wonderful ❤️

My husband, son and I went on this tour over Christmas break. It was excellent. Our guide was Julian and he really knew the history of the camp. We met at the Zoo station. The staff helped us buy the ABC tickets and we also bought lunch there to bring with us (we didn’t stop anywhere for food once we got going). We took the train to the Hauptbanhof where we met other groups, took the regional train to the town of Orienburg and then walked about 20 minutes to the camp. Spent about 4 hours at the camp and then took the train back to Berlin. We were back at our hotel by about 4:30. This was probably the best value we have ever had for a guided tour. I’ve heard the story of Hitler’s rise to power many times, in many settings, but Julien really added to my knowledge and gave a lot of perspective that made the story relatable even for the teens. Don’t hesitate to sign up for it.

To be honest, the weather was terrible. It was so cold, rainy and windy and me and my family was unprepared for the weather.

Despite the fact, our guide Xavier made everything worth it. He was passionate, knowledgeable and very caring. From the train Xavier started explaining all the basic information that helps us understand the history and the explanation lasted until the end of the tour.

My two children was listening and was interested. And they were opened to know more. He provided with more information for those who wanted further information and I’ve received it as he promised. I wish all the tour guides are like Xavier.

Didn’t have the opportunity to say goodbye as he had to jump out of the train on our way back to the city as he had to take care of one customer’s issue and he didn’t even hesitate to help the customer out. It that was very thoughtful of him and felt responsible.

If I visit Berlin again, I would like to go on a tour with Xavier and no one else. Thank you Xavier! Wanted to say that.

Paul was very knowledgeable and sympathetic to the subject matter. The tour was great if a little short. It would have been good to have been able to pause, process and digest the information. Given the site is free and we had to pay for our own transport some may prefer just to pay 3 Euros for the self guided tour when you get there.

Would very much recommend this tour. Swedish Maria was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about this subject. She was very attentive and went out of her way to ensure everyone was looked after. She dealt with what was an emotional trip in a respectful manner. Visiting Sachsenhausen is very much recommended as we can not forget the past.

Wow! Mike was unbelievably knowledgeable, not just about the tour at hand, but all things European History. My wife and I raved about not only his knowledge, but his enthusiasm during our tour. Everything Mike explained was fascinating. He was also able to cover an incredibly heavy topic with the utmost respect and grace, and made all questions welcomed. There was truly no question that Mike didn't know the answer to. Thank you, Mike!

Took a tour guide with Rob Shaw as we wanted to learn more about the history of the holocaust. Rob was very informative and knew this subject inside out. Made us feel welcome and the trip enjoyable with a great level of compassion for what occurred here

me and my partner decided to take the guided tour to sachsenhausen whilst in Berlin over the weekend, we met up with our guide Chloe who took us via train to the camp.

Chloe was not just very informative but she was extremely passionate about her job & answered all questions without ease or hesitation. We had planned on going solo before joining the tour and I’m very glad we chose not to in the end because without the knowledge passed on through Chloe I don’t think we would have experienced the tour in the same way. After the 3 hour tour we left feeling educated & further more curious to learn and have decided to visit further camps and can only hope that on our travels all of the future guides we encounter are just like Chloe! Once we arrived home we watched a film through our guides recommendation that really helped us to understand from the prisoners perspective what had happened in these camps, again a film we wouldn’t have encountered hadn’t it been for Chloe.

If you are planning a visit to Berlin, Sachsenhausen is a must see, giving a review on the camp alone isn’t necessary because I feel everyone will inherit it differently. I wouldn’t say you need to have vast knowledge in the ww2 before you visit because I’m positive if you use insider tours your guide providers will educate you along the way. Wrap up warm, take snacks & go in with a clear head. Big thanks to Chloe for taking our tour you have left us both eager to learn more and opened up new opportunities for us both to travel the world in doing so.

Took this tour with Jaime as our guide. really excellent both in terms of the information and the organization of the tour. Jaime is very knowledgeable about the subject and he was able to bring this dark chapter of history to life. Highly recommended.

Visited sachsenhausen concentration camp with insider tour. Our tour guide Ronan was great, very knowledgable, approachable and good fun. He dealt well with the different needs in our mixed group and took time to answer our questions fully. Would completely recommend- a really low price for the service and expertise given. Thank you Ronan!

We had Josh as our guide, and he was absolutely fantastic! He kept the information interesting throughout the 6 hour day, and really knew what he was talking about. The camp itself was genuinely amazing, it’s hard to believe what happened within those walls. It was interesting to find this site had so much history when Auschwitz is the more well-known site, puts into perspective how many camps all have their own individual history. We are so glad we booked this tour, it is now the highlight of our 4 week European holiday! If you’re in Berlin, you have to do this tour! (Make sure you rug up in the winter as we found it was very cold and windy and you spend a lot of time outside!)

Fantastic tour. Value for money, without a doubt. Jamie was our tour guide and he was very friendly, knowledgable and helpful. We highly recommend this guided tour if you want to make the most of your trip to Sachsenhausen.

Very informative and fun tour. Our tour guide (Walid) showed us a wide range of locations and gave a great background on the city which helped me make sense of the culture and history of Berlin, whilst also being entertaining a pleasant to all on the tour. We had the berlin welcome card so the tour was only ten euros. The east side meeting point was also super easy to find.

A fantastic tour and I would recommend it to anyone visiting Berlin. Sarah was our guide and what fantastic knowledge of the history of the camp she had. She was brilliant. She took us from Berlin city out to Sachsenhausen by train and gave us a lot of background information before we left the city. Her knowledge of the camp was fantastic. She answered every question that was asked of her and gave us a very real insight into life in the camp during the war. She even recommended movies that were based on the camp. The camp itself was cold but the way the memorial is designed and displayed gives a very good idea of how things were. Some of the original buildings remain but a lot is reproduced and we were made aware of this. This is to give us a better idea of how things were. Sarah also gave a great insight into how the camp was run, who was running it and how it was for both the prisoners and the guards who worked there.

Very interesting concentration camp. Focusses heavily on what/when/how and why.

Our guide was Ioana, who took the time to explain everything in great length and detail. How this camp came to be, how the SS and the inmates experienced it and what happened after that.

Some of the original buildings still stand, yet it matters not. You breathe the same air and walk in the victim's (and that of the perpetrators') steps.

25€ for this tour is really not much. Covers your entrance and the guide. Does not cover the train ticket to oranienburg and from Berlin!!!

Bare in mind, this is a full day tour so bring water or lunch with you.

A sobering tour from Berlin . A huge thank you to our guide Steve who gave us great information and insight on the tour while perfectly respecting the difficult subject matter .
A very emotional walking tour but I could not but highly recommend
If in Berlin it must be on the list to visit here

We were met with a very knowledgeable tour guide, Cian. He was engaging throughout the whole tour and explained the history as well as answered any questions we had. He also went above and beyond by giving us great recommendations of sights to see and restaurants to try out. Best guide I’ve had!

Martin was very knowledgeable about the history of the camp. Speaking from a local point of view helped a lot to put our feet in his shoes and immensely learn about all real-life stories and testimony during that dark time 1933-34. Thanks so much for the journey. Really unforgettable and a great educational experience 👍🏼

This tour was amazing. The highlight of our Berlin vacation. Our tour guide, Ariel was very kind, attentive and extremely knowledgeable. He seriously was an expert on all things WW2 and beyond. The concentration camp itself was very sobering, yet very interesting. We were completely taken back by what we saw and again- having a tour guide made the experience so much better because of all of the information that was shared about what we were seeing. After the tour Ariel even gave us some tips on great places to eat and see for the rest of our trip.

In short, we very highly recommend visiting Sachsenhausen and if you do, I even more highly recommend this tour. And if you are lucky enough to get Ariel as your guide, it’s even more of a bonus!

The guide was knowledgeable- take your own food/drink also a jacket very exposed no cover. Lots to read in the three or so exhibits, would have liked more time in them.
Guide very helpful with trains and tickets so don’t let that put you off. We had to walk from the station due to a public holiday so no buses about a 15-20 minute walk.

This tour was a life-changing experience for me. Plan to spend most of the day on this tour (6 or so hours). Nikolai, who is a very knowledgeable historian, guided our small group respectfully through this powerful memorial. Taking the tour means not so much time to look at the exhibits, but you make up for it with Nikolai's expert guidance around the former camp. The camp is also a short walk outside the town of Oranienburg, so having a guide made this so much better of an experience. There is also some time after the official tour ends to double back and view the exhibits if you feel the need. I am very happy I took this tour and recommend it highly. Make sure to wrap up warm if you visit in the winter months.

We done this tour on a cold sunday, our tour guide Walid(lovely english gentleman) was an amazing guide. his knowledge not only on the tour itself but Berlin overall was amazing. he answered any and all questions, got to know all the group and made sure no one was left out.

the tour itself lasts all day so i would come with snacks/water as it can be a long day.
it shows you all the original buildings and gives you a breakdown of the history on each one and also on all the camps and how they compared.

would defo recommend this tour if you are in Berlin as it shows you a side of history that should never be forgotten.

Visited here on the 8th March 2020. We used insider tours and our guide was Nickolai.
This tour involved using public transport and Nickolai made this very easy to use making sure everyone was in the right place.
The concentration camp it's self was incredibly insightful giving a massive insight to what happened in these camps. Nickolai knew everything you could possibly want to know about the camp. From the moment of seeing the headquarters to walking in this place has a very somber feel to it. The entrance itself is breathtaking. It really makes you think about what people must have though coming in here.
I would recommend this tour to anyone who has an interest in seeing these camps even as a small in comparison this place is very emotional and really hits home the conditions they would have experienced. As the camp is relatively intact.

Ioana was a brilliant tour guide. She gave a great mix of accounts from survivors as well as historical facts and timelines.
It’s hard to say you enjoyed something that was such an awful time in history, but it was certainly memorable in a positive way.
If you have a day you can spare in Berlin outside of the usual sights then definitely go.
Would highly recommend.
Do as they advise bring your own lunch and drinks and ABC transport tickets ready for the 10 am start, you will then have a seamless and lovely day out.

Had a very informative tour with Xavier who was fantastic and very knowledgeable and a really nice guy to boot. No time was wasted as on the way there he made sure to bring everyone up to speed with European history and the events leading to the birth of the concentration camps. The tour itself was very well planed out and definitely eye opening.

Maria was an excellent tour guide. She was very knowledgable and the time just flew by listening to her. Besides she was very helpful and gave advise on practical things such as the best way to get back to our hotel and son on. Highly recommended tour.

The tour was absolutely incredible. Robert was amazing, it was informative and respectful to the topics that were dealt with on the tour. The amount of walking was completely doable, and they were extremely helpful with all travel questions. Robert was very knowledgeable, he was equipped to answer any question but also made the harder subjects easier to digest with his good spirit.

Our guide Maria (from Sweden) at Sachsenhausen was amazing. She guided us with so much knowledge, passion and good storytelling that it became an unforgettable experience for me and my daughter. And we also appreciated the respect she showed all those who died in this horrible camp. I am 60 years old and have traveled a lot, Maria is absolutely the best guide I have ever experienced. She did an exceptional and unforgettable performance, a clear shining memory (although in a horrible place) for me and my daughter.

The guide (Swedish) Maria had a strong voice, knew her stuff and was friendly. The tour itself was interesting. The duration of the visit was perfect to prevent the tour from getting boring. I would recommend it if you want to scratch the surface of what happened in this concentration camp.

PAUL is an excellent guide; very friendly and informative. There was so much information to take in at the camp; you cd easily spend a lot more time there but Paul told us the main aspects. A bit more time with each exhibit would have been good but overall excellent. Paul was also very happy to give general tips on visiting Berlin and was really approachable.

The tour was very interesting. Like me I associated concentration camps with auschwitz. But that is not the case it basically means camp to concentrate prisoners. This camp was a testing camp. The story of the camp is interesting. One thing g I would say is take plenty of water/ drinks and maybe something to eat. You can fill water bottle up in the toilets if you need to. The camp is a bout 20 min walk from the train station, the same walk prisoners would have walked on their way to the camp. Although lots of the original barracks have gone there are a couple of buildings still standing. We enjoyed it although it ws a very hot day and there is not much shade around.

*Memorial tour not a tour of a concentration camp. 6 hour long day, food and drink should be brought with you as no time to pick these up during the tour.*

I've put all the important details that I think have been missing from the tour description first.

Met with our tour guide Gregory at the meeting point (very simple to find) and he took us on a little tour round Central berlin first give us some of the history building up to the camp. Had loads of picture examples to aid in his descriptions and was also keen to teach the difference between the 'factual' history and the realistic history. Think this is super important so we'll done. Really did go above and beyond with the tour, even at the end making sure each of us got back to the right subway station to get to out next destination.

The camp itself is a little underwhelming. I had higher expectations as I've been to auchwitz. However Gregory was keep to remind us that auchwitz was a death camp while this was began as a work camp. Also that during the de ryn of the Nazi, the camp was destroyed instead of reserved for educational purposes. Not a great deal to see however what was left is very interesting and probably wouldn't known about half the things if it hadn't been for the tour.

10/10 would highly recommend as its important to see from both sides and completely worth the money.

Went on this tour earlier this week. Our guide Walid was well informed about the history of the camp and of Berlin and was open for questions and discussion. He was friendly and fun!
The tour was most interesting and well-worth going on - highly recommendable experience.

We took this tour with Walid and he was excellent in sharing important information respectfully with a little lightheartedness that balanced the difficult subject. Really informative and we really enjoyed it. It is a eorthwhile daytrip.

I was very glad to attend this tour. I thought I knew a lot about the horrors of war, but this tour opens your eyes to just how horrible people can be to one another. The tour guide, was fantastic in sharing information and showing the most important aspects of the site. A caution for those that can’t walk well, it’s fast paced with lots of walking and standing and very few breaks for rest. Bring a snack and water since there’s little time for that. 100% recommend the tour and tour company.

Tour was very good and worth the time,=. Our tour guide Mikhail was very knowledgeable and provided a great deal of commentary and background knowledge on what occurred at this site. Very humbling day! Would strongly recommend

Our guide nikoli greeted us at friedrichstasse station. He was friendly and welcoming.
After a brief round table and tour overview we caught the train to the camp
He guided us to the venue and around the site.
It was very interesting and informative
He also added a few passed down stories which illustrated further the camps past.
I would certainly recommend the trip with Nikolai

Our tour guide Mike, was extremely knowledgeable and informed our entire group very well about the history and atrocities of Sachsenhausen. He provided unknown knowledge about the camp as well as Nazi occupied Germany and the years of the Cold War. I would highly recommend doing this excursion especially if your tour guide is Mike!

We recently visited Sachsenhausen using Insider Tour. The day was very organised, our guide Nickolai was fantastic. Nickolai was very informative and the tour went at a good pace. Having utilised this tour operator the prior day for a walking tour in Berlin we were not disappointed. All of the guides were friendly, spoke fantastic English, had a wealth of knowledge and the tours are very reasonable for the quality provided.

The tour guide is often a make or break with a lot of these tours, and from helping us organise our tickets for the day to organising our transport to our destination afterwards the whole day was organised amazingly. The tour itself was great, despite the large amount of groups there overall, Taylor made sure to get us to all of the places and provide background and explanations with such detail that it really made you feel the gravity. Couldn’t recommend this tour, and Taylor enough. Just for reference, Taylor is the guy on the left!

Would absolutely recommend this tour and Insider Tours. It was exceptional and thought provoking. Our tour guide Chloe was incredibly educated on the camp and the Holocaust in general, Chloe was able to answer all our questions and show us around the camp with huge insights. The camp was busy and Chloe was able to navigate the camp ensuring we saw the historically important sites. I’ve walked away with so much learning. 100% a must do in Berlin.

We had an amazing tour with Martin who was extremely knowledgeable and brought bold personality and personal connections to the tour. He has met multiple survivors from Sachsenhausen and heard their stories first hand and local knowledge as someone who grew up in the area. Lots of walking (about 2 km from train to camp following the same path prisoners would have taken) and about a 30 minute train ride.

One of the best tours I’ve ever been on. The guide Chloe certainly knew her stuff and was able to answer any question thrown at her. Would certainly recommend this tour to anyone wanting to keep the memory of the Holocaust alive.

Somber and important visit for us on our trip to Berlin. Yes, it’s a fair way out of the centre but the rail and bus system in Berlin we found was excellent overall. As a group aged 12 to 54, the youngest didn’t have any knowledge of the atrocities as she hasn’t started world wars at school yet. For the rest it was chilling being there and reading the information, seeing the conditions the prisoners had to live and unfortunately die in. Wrap up warm as it is a lot of open spaces and bitter cold in February. Each of the adults left with more understanding for having visited.

Tour guide and historian Rob was very informative and entertaining. He guided the group from Berlin via train and bus to Schasenhausen concentration camp.His presentation of the history of Germany during this period was illuminating.

Where to start!

Mike was an excellent guide, with passion, significant knowledge and insight into the whole period from the rise of the Nazi party to present day, as well as a great sense of humour which he used appropriately

The tour starts in central Berlin (where Mike gave background information) you then get a train (and a short bus ride) out to the camp.

We had a slight set of unfortunate circumstances when the train was cancelled - however, this didn't deter Mike who had a plan B as we went to the next station and got a different train.

Mike through the whole tour including on the trains provided commentary that was brilliant.

The camp itself is very sobering and we learnt what day to day life would have been like - Difficult to really imagine the true living conditions of the inmates.

What we found interesting and would not have realised without Mike was the 4 stages of the camp. How it was used by the Nazis, then the Soviets,, followed by a rewriting of true events by the East Germans and soviet bloc before being properly remembered for what truly went on in the camp.

Can't praise Mike or recommend the tour enough!

I had an experience that was very unique. The guide, Gregor, did a fantastic job of getting ensuring that the essential information was provided, whilst ensuring that respect was shown. He also gave an insight into Nazi Germany and why it is so important to learn about places such as Sachsenhausen. Value for money and an overall memorable experience.

"Swedish" Maria is a knowlegeable guide, and above all, speaks clearly and loud enough. The tour itself is OK content-wise, with interesting details and a good setting of the context. Sachsenhausen is not one of the 6 extermination/death camps, but an important labour/concentration camp focussed on other victims of Nazi prosecution, and reused by the Soviets in the post WW 2 era.

Went on the Sachesenhausen tour today, it was very interesting, thought provoking and emotional. Our tour guide Walid was excellent , making it interesting and informative. He was friendly and chatty and handled the tour in a compassionate way, whilst still getting across the terrible things that happened there.

Wonderful, informative tour of Sachsenhausen with a great overview of the history of World War II, Germany's rise to power and resulting events, including establishment of concentration camps. Irish Jamie was our tour guide and he was incredibly knowledgeable and a terrific teacher, going out of his way to present a balanced, detailed, historical perspective of the campaign. I am not a great auditory learner, but I was able to learn so much from listening to him because he is a good, clear presenter. Do not attempt to tour the facility on your own; you will get so much more out of it with this particular tour. Be prepared for a full day of walking, which I loved, and have a few tissues on hand.

The tour was in-depth, carefully thought out, and conveyed the gravity of it all to both children and adults. One site in particular was the one called Operation Bernard, where British currency was heavily counterfeited by the Nazi’s to finance the German war effort. Also, the prison within the prison, where the VIP’s were held was well documented. I’ve visited several camps in Poland however, the layout of the this one was on a grander and much more detailed l scale.

Fantastic tour guide, made the experience even more informative. Absolutely fantastic knowledge, the way the history of the camp was told by her was just faultless, I will 100% never forget it. Absolute must do when visiting Berlin.

Cian did a great job guiding the tour. He is very knowledgeable about not only the camp but also the whole of European history at the time, which added a lot of much needed historical context.He struck the right tone when explaining the stories from the camp which made the whole experience even more eye opening and very much worth while. Couldn’t have gotten a better person for the job!

Today we had the pleasure of meeting Chloe.
She was very knowledgeable and made time to answer any questions.
Great experience.
She even took her time to make sure everyone knew where they needed to go when we left.

The tour was well organized. Our guide (the Canadian :) ) Chris his stories were very interesting and he was open for any questions. He adjusted to the group if we wanted to know more/other things.
The view he had on Sachsenhausen and the second world war were refreshing and interesting. I would recommend taking this tour!

Literally nothing negative to say about this tour. The guide we went with (Martin) was super knowledgeable and knew something about everything there was to see and made everyone feel comfortable to boot! I would recommend this to everyone having taken this as a recommendation myself. Thank you Martin! A thoroughly educative tour!

Cambell was an amazing guide. Very helpful getting tickets, giving details before the tour. During the long day at an incredible location he was very knowledgeable and answered all sorts of questions. This is an all day tour he kept up the interred time. The sore is very somber as the history of it is terrible but interesting visiting such a place.
I strongly recommend this one of a kind tour and hopefully you get Cambell.

Enjoyable is not the word I would use When describing this tour. Informative, interesting, harrowing and excellent are words one could use. Chloe our guide did a great job of explaining everything from the beginning to the end of the Holocaust as it pertained to Sachsenhausen. Getting to the meeting point was straight forward as was getting to the site itself. She even helped us all to get back by making sure we new which stop to get off and where we get all of our various connector trains from. highly recommended.

This tour exceeded our expectations. Our guide, Brian, was very knowledgeable and helpful throughout the tour. The pace was also nice. Not too rushed but no wasted time either. Brian also made sure everyone had directions on the way back if they needed or wanted to go a separate way than the group. This tour is well worth the money and I would definitely recommend it.

This 6 hour tour was excellent value and very different from other Berlin tours. Peter our tour guide was extremely knowledgeable and an excellent communicator. He set the right tone for a memorial tour of a concentration camp. My two teenage sons and I learnt a lot. The whole experience is something I will never forget. I would highly recommend this tour.

Touring the concentration camp was a somber experience but the tour was still amazing. Ciaran was our guide and we could not have asked for a better, more knowledgeable tour guide. He provided so many facts, kept the tour group engaged and was overall terrific at his job. I would absolutely recommend this tour and Ciaran.

We probably could have figured out how to visit Sachenhausen on our own, but I am very glad we booked this tour. He was so knowledgeable and I could not imagine a more thorough way to learn about the horrible history of Sachenhausen. He made sure our group was respectful while we toured the grounds, which I appreciated.

Our tour guide, Chloe, was excellent and gave us a really good insight into the atrocities that took place at Sachsenhausen concentration camp. Could not have asked for a better trip, would insist anybody going to Berlin go on this trip. Went with a group of friends from university but there was a great mix of people on the tour. The quality of the tour was superb and our guide was extremely knowledgable about the camp. Thank you so much for the memorable experience.

First time to Berlin. Booked with Insider Tours with the excellent Xavier as our guide - he was highly knowledgeable and was a very interesting trip. Had only a slight knowledge on the history but came away with a much greater understanding. Would definitely recommend

Could not recommend Walid as our guide enough. We had been on another tour with Walid the day before so we knew it was going to be excellent. For me, this tour is a must if you are going to visit Berlin and a real eye opener. Walid kept the group in tact and provided us with great advice before departing from the station. This tour is great for US-American University faculty who want their students to study the history of the holocaust while in Berlin. Nickolai, our guide for the day, was absolutely wonderful, extremely knowledgeable on the subject, and professional. I highly recommend this tour.

This tour and the guide Mike were incredible. We had a bunch of people on our tour. Mike did a great job keeping everyone together and interested. His knowledge and the way he told the history kept us all engaged. My 2 young daughters even asked questions! The walk and the site itself is very solemn. Everyone in our group was very respectful of it's history. I am so glad I went on this tour with my family. Thank you for a memorable and meaningful experience.

A couple tips: wear comfortable shoes. It really is a full day. Bring snacks and water. I bought snacks for my family at the train station before we started the tour.

We had an unbelievable experience touring Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp Memorial from Berlin. Our guide, Cesar, was extremely informative and we learned so much in our short time from him. He also made the traveling by train from Berlin and back a breeze. He was so friendly and brilliant!

Our guide Jamie has a lot of knowledge and is a very good story teller.

Martin was brilliant and really passionate about providing a great tour. All the staff we met were very friendly and welcoming. Martin gave a great tour and was able to answer everything that was asked. Would really recommend.

A massive thank you to Phil, our guide, for an informative, sensitive, and confronting tour of the Concentration Camp in Oranienberg. Sarah our guide was excellent in conveying the horror that went on. Even though it was pushing 35 degrees. Definitely recommend. It's something toy will never forget.

Gabi was very friendly and very helpful. Showed us how to use the trains, made sure we were well prepared, and kept the group moving efficiently. Very informative tour, highly recommend.

Glad I had a chance to see the camp on my vacation however this is certainly a very somber activity.

Just went on the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp Memorial Tour from Berlin. Our tour guide was Chloe and she was fantastic. She gave some much colour to the tour. Nikolai picked us up as arranged and efficiently shepherded us from West Berlin to Sachenhausen. He was a font of knowledge on the camp, collaborating companies and individuals, and authoritarianism and fascism today. We’re very happy we chose this tour

Our host Steve from Australia was amazing. He was incredibly knowledgeable and knew how to lighten the mood in a respectful manner when needed. He told us how to get to our desired destination at the end of the tour as well, which was an added bonus.

Tour and guide Campbell were first rate. Very informative - very moving. Guide was extremely knowledgeable with history degree and interpersonal skills second to none. Excellent on every level (Bring a snack and be prepared to do some walking!)

Couldn't have asked for a better tour guide. Cian had all the information you could ever need about the camp, every question he answered in great detail. Swedish Maria was my guide, and I would give her 20 stars if I could. Her knowledge of history is fantastic, as is her ability to explain it. She brought the past to life for our group. This is such important work, lest history repeat itself.

Really good tour & well organised. Couldn’t of asked for anyone more knowledgeable than Mike Stack from Insider Tours. Outstanding tour with a superbly knowledgeable and informative guide (Martin). Not “fun” for obvious reasons, but something that will live in our memories for a long time.
Warning that it is a long and fairly strenuous day! 15,000 steps on our counter, but so worth the effort

Chloe was an excellent tour gude, from making sure the group were well prepared with drinks, food, ppe masks and train tickets to individual engagement. Her knowledge of Sachenhaussen Concentration Camp is exemplary. Very engaging tour. Highly recommended

We went with Rochele from SANDEMANs. She was excellent. She knew lots and communicated well. She knew when to talk and when to give reflective time. We reluctantly went on the half day tour. I’m not sorry I visited this historical site. I went with head knowledge and left with heart knowledge. The tour was well organized tour that portrayed an historical account of the events that happened and the people involved. I’m not sorry I visited Sachsenhausen Memorial and Museum.

Really nice to see, really gave context to Holocaust history and brought it to reality. Our guide Phillipa was excellent! Had great knowledge of the history and was so helpful and friendly. Definitely worth a visit and Would highly recommend and ask for phillipa !!

We had Walid as our tour guide. His perfect English Made everything understandable, great personality just made the tour fun in general, although keeping a serious side of how the concentration camp was used.

You will need to take water and snacks with you as it is a long tour without anywhere to get anything.

Highly recommend

Cyprus

We had such a great day. Martin knew so much about everything at sachsenhausen.
The things he told were so interesting. Enough space to ask questions. He guided us by train and foot to the camp. Everything was well organized by him. I really recommend him.

Comprehensive view of what transpired at the Concentration Camp predominantly focusing on the Nazi era but including the Soviet atrocities which followed after the Third Reich fall. Excellent guide (Maria B.) who was extremely knowledgeable and informative. Excellent value.

it was a very moving experience for my partner and i. Our guide john was excellent with his knowledge. It will be a tour that will be with you forever, truly heartbreaking, but a must visit. Cant recommend it enough. take warm clothes and a pack lunch as its a long day

This day promised so much of information and our tour guide John did deliver.

John that you for the detailed yet simple explanations and for answering all my sons questions.

Thank you Julian, for such an informative trip to Saschsenhausen Concentration Camp. It was an emotional, historical experience that I will never forget. I truly enjoyed what you said at the end about educating ourselves, traveling and voting, so to prevent history from repeating itself. Thank you again, my whole family will never forget it.

We decided not to get a guided tour as we didn’t want to be tied on times, we had read you can hire a listening wand which we did for €3 each, admission is free.

We found the easiest way to get there from Berlin was to go to the Berlin main train station and take the train directly to Oranienburg, this took just 28 minutes and only cost €3.40.

We walked from the station which was well sign posted and only took 15 minutes.

The experience was very good and I would definitely recommend a visit.

If you’re a history buff I’d recommend the day, but if you just want to see main buildings and information half a day would be fine.

We went on this tour today. A little bit of public transport and walking involved so be ready for that, but we knew that prior and it was no problem.

Wallid was our guide today and he was fantastic, very informative and accommodating to different interests and styles. I enjoyed the way he presented events - he was super engaging.
He also gave us a tip to bring some food with us as the food on site is expensive and not much to choose from. Thanks Wallid!

Some people might find this tour a little fast paced - I think if you are the kind of person to stop and read every sign in an exhibit you should give this one a miss. I certainly had enough time to take photos of key parts of the tour and the pace worked well for me and my boyfriend.

The site itself was of course interesting and sad. I recommend going even if you have been to somewhere like Auschwitz before because it is a different type of camp and very different / unique history

14/01/20

Met our guide Mike at Hakescher Markt station. He explained how to use the public transport - how to validate tickets and to ONLY VALIDATE YOUR 48 OR 72 HOUR PASS ONCE!!

We then took two trains to Oranienburg, passing through the largest station in Berlin, the Hauptbahnhof - a magnificent feat of enineering and well worth checking out if youre into that sort of thing. All along the journey Mike gave us more info pointing out landmarks such as sections of the berlin wall and Friedrichstraße train station where East German spies returned after trips to West Berlin.

He also provided us with information on the years leading up to WWII and the campaign of the Nazis to remove civil rights and liberties. His knowledge of the subject matter was immense and he had a real interest in the subject, regularly taking questions and adding further cultural context.

We got off the train in Oranienburg and took a bus to Sachsenhausen with Mike pointing out the local businesses who has uses labour from the camp or sold goods and services to the camp. When we got off the bus he pointed out the Police Training centre, once the barracks of the SS who gaurced the camp. He also pointed out the houses built for the officers near the camp.

The area is quite residential and the former administration building for over 1000 camps where the camp commandants were educated on how to run other camps across the country. It now houses the local tax office.

Passing through the camp gate was an eerie experience as you arrive in the camp devoid of trees, shrubs or grass and with no wildlife. We got to see several buildings including the barracks for the inmates, kitchens, infirmary and Station Z where the murders of over 45000 people was carried out. Mike always answered our questions and kept the tour moving whilst giving people the chance to break away and return if they preffered.

On our way back to the Hauptbahnhof Mike took the time to advise everyone - 19 people in total - on transport back to their hotels, where to eat according to their preference and what to do depending on their length of time in Berlin. You could tell he has become a Berliner even though he hails from New Zealand.

Although it was a cold day Mike's humour and enthusiam for the subject kept us engaged. The conversations around the context and its knock on effects today made the tour unique and Mike brought the innmates stories to life. It was a fantastic tour and I would highgly recommend it.

Gabriel and Gearoid
From Ireland

PS Your red welcome to Berlin booklet will get you a discount and your ABC ticket covers transport to and from the camp.

Coming to see a concentration camp is never going to be the most pleasant experience but it's necessary to see and learn about. Our tour guide Walid was exceptional and provided a wealth of information on the concentration camp, Holocaust and the rise of Nazism. I found it truly fascinating. Sachsenhausen is a very eerie place and it can feel quite grim at times however, Walid was able to add some light humour at times which is difficult considering the subject matter. On a practical note wear good comfortable walking shoes, your own lunch and water.

Went on Tuesday October 1, 2019. Stayed at Mitte and as a previous reader suggested, I booked the travel point from Hackescher Markt U-bahn station. Very convenient, just took the U-bahn one stop east from the hotel I was staying at.
Gabriela was our guide from Argentina. She did an excellent job and really knew her stuff. Very powerful, moving experience to be there. Highly recommend visiting Sachsenhausen to experience one of the darkest moments in history.

Here are some suggestions that I have that I wish I knew or would have made the tour better.

To future tour goers:
1. Comfortable Shoes: an essential as you will be walking from 10am to about 3:00pm before getting on the train at that time.
2. Bring liquids/water and food that is easy to eat/drink while walking: Gabriela gave us a heads up before we started the tour that if we didn’t have any liquids or foods that we quickly grab something because there’s no chance once we start. There was a “brief” time to eat while at Sachsenhausen while we were walking, but it was at one of the sites inside the concentration camp. Felt awkward to eat really while inside the memorial/concentration camp. Would suggest eating on the train or definitely after when done...
3. Small backpack: to carry your belongings, food, liquid bottles, etc
4. Check the weather: so thankful I checked the weather because it was raining and at times got soaked. I did bring my bring an umbrella but wish I had thought of wearing waterproof shoes as we were all dodging big puddles and walking around with cold wet feet which was not too comfortable

To the tour company:
1. Smaller tour group size: Gabriela did an awesome job managing our group of 30-35 tour goers. However it was hard to hear her at times when rows of us were surrounding her with our umbrellas all up.
2. Personal Head sets that tour goers can use with the tour guide speaking into wirelessly/blue tooth: I’ve been on tours with about the same size of participants and these headphones with this box that wirelessly connects to the box that the guide is speaking into made it so much easier to understand and hear what is going on (without us all needing to clutter together while Gabriela is doing her best not to lose her voice... which was happened!)

This was a great tour and our guide Sebastian was terrific. This is a hard place to visit, but I’m glad we did. Sebastian did a great job explaining the history and the importance of memorializing the events to honor those that suffered and to recognize those that fought to stop that suffering.

I recommend packing a hat, good walking shoes, sunscreen, your own food and water and make sure you have the C component of the Berlin AB travel card as Sachsenhausen is around 45 minutes north west of the city centre on the S-Bahn. That's followed by a 20 minute walk to the camp.

That's not the only walking you'll be doing. The site has no shops, no cafe, no chairs, very little shade or shelter and no rest area. If you need to sit, you'll have to do so on the ground.
The only restrooms are outside the main gate and that will be your last chance to use one.

Subliminally, I feel Sachsenhausen forces visitors to reflect and suffer.

There's few of the original blocks remaining as most were flattened by the Soviets. Some have been restored but the perimeter and shape of the camp remains intact. Every item, room, and every building has a story.

I hadn't been in long and I was already casing the walls and looking for an escape route.

The guided tour was well researched, factual, sobering and we were able to ask questions during our 3 hours or so. We had an outstanding guide who spoke both English and Spanish. Gabriela scored a 5/5 for the respectful manner in re-telling the history, forced labour, pain, forgery, human vivisection, prostitution, execution, and in a few cases, survival.

It wasn't only Jews who were imprisoned here. This camp was already in use for political opponents and communists during the 1936 Berlin Olympics.

To be frank, I wish I had never set foot in there. I hate it's very existence and have struggled to write a proper review without swearing.

Like all the concentration camps, they were an abomination and a shame upon humanity. Sachsenhausen has never known love or humanity.

This is a good tour, but this camp can overwhelm you. It was the only trip where none of our party took any momento photos. It just didn't seem right and I'm happy this wasn't the last trip we took in Berlin.

Booked onto the Sachsenhausen Concentration camp tour a couple of days before through Viator.

We met our group outside a central Berlin railway station at 10:00. We were introduced to our tour guide for the day, Walid, who was incredibly thoughtful from the outset. He made sure that everyone had got a packed lunch with them (nowhere to buy food at the camp) and that everyone has a zone ABC public transport ticket (not included in the tour price).

He led us through the railway station and directed us on to the correct train, after explaining where we were going. He even helped another tour group get on the right train as he heard the change of platform announcement in German over the station tannoy system.

The walk from the station to the camp took 20-30 minutes but Walid kept us all occupied by taking a genuine interest in where we were from and how we were finding Berlin.

When we entered the camp, his commentary was insightful and he obviously knows so much about the history of the subject.

The actual camp was somber with preserved inmates quarters and remnants of the guard towers and morgue. The written information was fascinating.

We arrived back in the centre of Berlin and still Walid was taking care of us, answering our questions and giving us directions to where we wanted to go.

It was a great tour and an interesting day spent just outside of Berlin. Walid really made our day with his kindness and his expertise. He was such an interesting guy and it was a pleasure to meet him!

Absolute must if going to Berlin. Easy to get there but felt booking a tour was worthwhile, learnt a lot from the guide. Booked via trip advisor and our guide Phil was brilliant. Really knowledgable and friendly. He also took the time to go round everyone on the train back to advise on places to go or how to get back to various hotels which was really helpful. Highly recommended.

We took a tour of Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp with Maria (in English) through Insider Tour, and really appreciated her insights! Highly recommend going on this tour, as you get much more in depth knowledge and context - rather than going on your own. Maria was incredibly knowledgable, pleasant and an absolutely wonderful guide!

it was interesting, but there's very little of it left, so if you like structures and buildings to give you a feel for the horrors of the place, you wont get it, 3 left. It was an early experimental concentration camp, not one of the gas chamber nightmares. They shot and cremated 15,000 soviet soldiers. Another 150,000 were starved and worked to death, a mixture of German political prisoners, comunists, homosexuals, Jehovah’s witneses and not so many Jews as they were moved on to the far worse camps in the east.

My sister and I really enjoyed our tour with our guide Maria. She knew her way around the large crowds, and had an incredible knowledge on the history and every question I asked. The experience is without a doubt very chilling. Just imagining that in the very grounds we stood, so many things happened that changed the course of history. I am very happy with this tour. If you do book, please wear comfortable shoes because you will get tired (they told us before the tour about the shoes, so you'll also get the memo). And if you go during the winter, which we did, dress very warm because the camp is located in such an open and exposed area that you'll be freezing your butts off. If you go in the summer (which we did not go), our guide Maria says it gets very hot, so keep that in mind. You do have to buy your own food before you go. Keep in mind it's a long tour so you should pack something that will keep you satisfied during the day. Overall, I highly recommend! Also please respect the space! It's a memorial with an abundance of history.

Great tour experience of the history of Sachsenhausen concentration camp. The tour guide Alaria was very informative and ensured we had a smooth travel to the camp and back. Our guide met us in central Berlin and guided us to the camp 30km outside of Berlin and gave us the full experience of what travesties occured. I'm happy to have gone on this trip as it has given me a deeper understanding of what really occured during the war. It is important to remember and understand these brutal events as we must continue to educate future generations so we never forget.

Walid was our tour guide for the tour. Met us at train station and helped buy our train tickets. Very informative tour from Walid who had a wealth of background knowledge on the concentration camp and Germany. Would highly recommend the tour and we were impressed with Walids helpfulness and knowledge.

Maria our tour guide gave us a deeply insightful tour of the concentration camp. She gave us a very detailed insight into this chapter of dark history. The camp itself still has many parts that are original and in tact. Parts that are reconstructed still give you that very real feeling if what it may have been like for the people who were living there. Maria our guide took us in directions were we always avoided big crowds and got a chance to have a proper look. Only thing is it’s advisable to bring your own lunch and drink as the cafe at the camp is very slow service and sometimes the break time has finished by the time your order is ready. I would definitely recommend this tour to anyone going to Berlin.
WOW mike is good. So smart and such a great tour guide. He is easy to understand and doesn’t use crazy language. He’s super awesome. The tour was moving and I highly recommend. Ask for Mike!!!
Fabulous tour with Nickolai. He was extremely knowledgeable and happy to answer any questions. I would highly recommend this tour. Wrap up warm as the site is very open.

Excellent informative tour by Walid - easy meet up at east collection point & train to Sachsenhausen. Although annoying that people turned up without train tickets or lunch/food - as it specifies you needed these for the tour. It was a 10-15 min walk from the train station to the camp - but Walid stopped at various points on the way to the camp to explain various aspects. Very knowledgeable on the camp and the Nazi regime.

I had visited the camp once before on my own, but I am really glad I decided to take this Insider Tour when I brought my sons to Berlin. Mike is a very knowledgeable tour guide and his guidance and insights really put everything into perspective. He also really took care of everyone on the tour. He even offered to carry some books I had purchased in his shoulder bag.

We needed to take two trains to get out to Oranienburg, but Mike shepherded the group well and made the process very smooth and stress free. I did not even realize that the current Finanzamt building was an administration building for the concentration camp system. So getting to tour this building was a great benefit of taking the tour, because I did not see it on my first trip to the camp.

Mike really knows the history of Nazi Germany and this camp in particular. I was really impressed with his detailed knowledge and the facts and statistics he had at his fingertips. It was like being give a tour by a professor. He was careful to include everyone and answer the questions that everyone had.

Definitely worth it to experience the camp with a an excellent tour guide like Mike.
Wallid's tour today was nothing short of amazing. He's super knowledgeable about the camp but also friendly and engaging. I would do this again. 10/10

This tour is incredibly emotional and educational. Our guide Chloe was friendly, informative and gave us time and space for personal reflection and thought. This six hour tour was an amazing value for money. It was a day well spent. 10/10 would recommend.

An amazing tour guided by Jakub. Very helpful and informative from start to finish. If you’re like me and haven’t a notion how to use public transport they help you with tickets and give time beforehand to ensure you know how to get to and from the camp. Jakub was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about the history. He was very respectful in his descriptions and the tour itself was touching and heartbreaking. I definitely recommend!
Jakub was an excellent guide. This is tough going but a really important and informative tour. Highly recommended

Found it really great! I didn't know much about the history of Belin/Germany but our tour guide, Walid, explained everything so clearly I came away from it really informed and got a great insight into Sachsenhausen. Would reccommend!

The tour was very well organized and planned. Our guide Nickolai obviously has read a lot on the topic beyond what is required and provided individual stories as well as overall important information.

This place really left a mark within me. It is every teaching and interesting. You don't need to book a tour. It is very easy reachable by train from Berlin at a cost of 3,40€ per person one way. The entrance is free. You should rent a Audio guide for 3 €. Notice that you need to take bus from the train station (fair is included in your train ticket) It says Sachsenhausen at the bus stop right outside the train station.

We have just finished our trip with insider tours and we loved it. Ronan was our guide and he was so informative giving us detailed information. He made a very emotive subject easy to listen to. It is a long day with plenty of walking so comfortable shoes , plenty of layers and waterproof coats are a must. A great job has made done at preserving what is left and highlighting what was there. If anything this tour has left us wanting to visit again!!! Ronan helped us all back and gave us pointers for places to eat etc. Ronan yer a legend you should get a raise!!!! And if your mum is reading this (We know she does) your boy is lovely x
Ps remember and take food and drink with you.

Our tour guide - Phil - struck the right tone on this tour. He had an excellent
knowledge of history and details which gave colour and flavour to the experience. Would highly recommend. There is a considerable amount of walking, but the pace was very manageable. It should also go without saying but be respectful - keep your voice down and rethink taking smiling selfies; in short, remember where you are.

Our tour guide Phil (October 14th tour) is a true historian who did an excellent job during his presentation of this terrible time in history. Phil had a way of bringing me into the life's of the innocent victims of Sachsenhausen, truly feeling their horror, helplessness and both emotional and physical pain. Any "problems" that I encounter in life moving forward, will truly be dealt with in a new light. I learned more from Phil during this afternoon in all of the years combined of history education during my school years. Phil was also a very courteous and helpful person, welcoming any questions about not only the tour but other nearby museums or excursions as well. Phil was also very helpful in assisting everyone with specific train transfers for the trip back from the site. We road back with Phil, but were welcome to get off at other train stops in lieu of returning all the way back to the original start up place. Phil went above and beyond making sure Everyone's return trip needs were met. I will also mention that it really is best that you bring bottled water and a snack or lunch with you during your tour. We began at 10AM and with all of the walking we did, I was grateful to have water and a protein bar. The Sachsenhausen site does not have any vending or refreshments for sale, so come prepared,

Myself and my family ( including a 11 and 18 year old), went on this deep and dark topic of a tour. I found there to be so much to learn, however Walid managed to explain the history of the concentration camp, drawing on recent history and thoughts. This kept myself interested throughout, and not too depressed by the topic by the end. A recommended day out.

Had a great tour with Nicolai (hope I spelt correctly).
The knowledge was amazing. Lots of stories. Enjoyed.

My Mum and I did this tour a few days ago and it was incredible (very sad, but amazing).

Taylor was our guide and he was incredible. He gave a great and balanced overview of how the Nazis came to power and the history of the camps. It was really really interesting. Taylor also gave us lots of great tips on transport and general Berlin stuff.

Highly recommended!!
Thoroughly enjoyed our day visiting Sachsenhausen. Chloe was our guide and she was lovely, very knowledgeable and made this a worthwhile tour. A very moving experience.

The Camp is a "must-see" while in Berlin. It is extremely informative and a real "eye opener". Very sad that this occurred, but it was a part of history which we should all see so that the poor people who suffered and died here are never forgotten. That being said, I would suggest you go to the Camp yourself and take the self-tour. They provide a audio device that explains everything. This way you can take your time and really digest everything.

We took the organized tour, which was very disappointing. I would not recommend it and would use our guide (see below).

First off, the tour was very rushed. Our guide Josh (from Ohio) did not take the time to walk through the various museums and explain things, like the way I saw other guides from other tour agencies do. It didn't help that the tour did not leave Berlin until after 10 AM; it should have started way earlier. Our guide spent more time giving us a "lunch break" and sitting around with us, when we could have been touring. I did not go all that way to sit in a cafeteria and eat lunch; I went to tour the Camp. He was very rushed throughout the entire tour, and I felt we did not see half of what we should have seen.

Second, on the train trip back to Berlin, Josh abandoned us. He said he had a festival to attend and would be leaving the train at the first stop. He verbally gave us instructions on where to exit the train we were currently on, and how to catch the next (transfer) train.
