Well, our transfer occurred at the Central Station where there was a multitude of trains and train platforms, thus making it very difficult to find the correct transfer. With help from strangers, we were able to find the correct transfer train. I felt that "Josh" abandoned us for his own personal benefit. As our guide, he should have stayed with us until we returned to our original starting point. This was his responsibility, and he chose to himself over his group.

I would rate this tour and our guide Josh a "1" star, but because the Camp itself is a "5" rating, I gave the whole experience a "3", which is the average of the two marks.

It was myself and my boyfriend’s first time in Berlin, so fancied taking a tour as part of our sightseeing around the city.

We choose the Sachsenhausen tour and I have to say, it exceeded our expectations.

Walid was so warm and welcoming! He helped everyone with their train tickets and gave us a run down of what the day would include before we set off. He made sure that we were all happy and introduced each of us to any new guests that turned up.

The tour was very informative and Walid made what could have been a very long day, very interesting and up beat. He answered any questions that our tour had and was more than happy to find out something that he wasn’t sure about.

Everyone loved the tour and I felt that I learned so much about the history of Germany and the concentration camps in general, as well as the specific camp we visited.

I would highly recommend one of these tours! Especially with Walid 😊

We did this tour with Maria and she was an excellent guide. She was very patient, helpful and very easy to listen to. We found the tour extremely informative and interesting, if at times quite emotionally challenging. I would say this tour is definitely a must do. Thanks again Maria.

The tour is great because the guide explains everything about the Holocaust and the camp and the camp details, but it is not the best one to go, when comparing it to Auschwitz-Birkenau, because many structures are gone and most of the ones still standing were remodelled.
Roman was a really great guide - he is so knowledgeable about the concentration camp and relates the information in an interesting way. So glad we booked the tour rather than organising ourselves...

I typically read books in advance and do self guided tours everywhere in Europe with the Rick Steves app and guidebooks. This is the ONLY guided tour I took in 5 days in Berlin and I’m glad I did. Our guide, Taylor, was friendly and knowledgeable, and his insights added so much to the visit. From the time we met in Berlin, Taylor provided the narrative that immersed us in the tour. As we got off the train in Oranienberg from Berlin, we walked through the streets to the camp following the route typically taken by prisoners. Once at the camp Taylor distilled what could have been an overwhelming amount of information into a tour that hit all the major sites in the camp. He gave us time to spend on our own where appropriate, but was able to ensure that we saw and understood the key components of the camp. To be clear, this is not a tour for children or the faint of heart. The camp, storyboards, and Taylor’s explanations tell it like it was, sparing no details of the brutality that took place there. It was an emotional and worthwhile day. Logistics were easy. We met at Hackescher Market, took the S to Hauptbahnhof, joined others, and took the 40 minute train ride to Oranienberg. The walk to the camp was about 20 minutes. On the return Taylor walked through the group on the train and made sure we each knew how to get back to our respective Berlin destinations. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.
Great trip - Ronan was our guide and he was really knowledgeable and informative. The time went really quickly and he made sure we got back to the right stop on the train.

We had Xavier as our tour guide and he was great! He had so much knowledge and kept the tour interesting. We felt bad that we couldn’t think of many questions to ask but he covered everything we could think of! Overall a brilliant, emotive tour with an interesting and passionate guide.

Xavier our tour guide was excellent-his knowledge and compassion left us emotionally moved.Looked after us in every aspect from start to finish.The tour involves a lot of walking but well worth it .The Concentration Camp itself was thought provoking and it is hard to believe humans could commit such dreadful atrocities.
Ciaran was a really great guide, knowledeable and friendly. This tour was just enough time and a good level of information, would recommend!
Excellent tour with a very knowledgable host. It was well organised. Overall a very sobering experience from start to finish.
worth visiting. our guide Brian was knowledgeable. only if I could stay longer in the exhibition venues.

Had tour guide mike, Went with girlfriend and had really good time was given a ton of intresting information and had some problems with trains last minute cancellations which didnt slow him down straight to next available train which ended up getting delayed aswell (not mikes fault), plenty of light heartedness shown and explained in detail everything we came across and were given good photo and opportunities to have extra time wherever we wanted didnt feel rushed although we were behind schedule, on the way back dropped train ticket under the train and mike replaced it with his own one for us, saved us at least 6 euros, very friendly and a great tour highly recommended!

Amazing. Our tour guide was JOSHUA from the Insider Tours
He was just fantastic. He was like a historian with all his knowledge. Fantastic but extremely sad.
Nickolai was an amazing tour guide. Very informative and friendly! Although it was cold outside, he offered us his gloves.

The concentration camp tour is educational and brings an understanding to the brutal horrors of Nazi Germany. Our guide, John, was excellent and was able to relay the history in a respectful and thought provoking way.

Highly recommend seeing this camp. There is a lot to see there. Make sure to wrap up warm as it was freezing out there as it is in the countryside and out in the open. The tour got us familiar with public transport which was handy.

Would recommend this to anyone visiting Berlin , was such an emotional and interesting experience , our tour guide Chloe was amazing and made our tour great , we never lost interest and would advise everyone to take this tour
Walid was extremely knowledgeable and really assisted us to get a full picture of the horrors of the camp as well as the events leading up to its crea6and subsequent use.
Very good, educational tour. Wallie was a good knowledgeable guide. A lot of information and artifacts.

If you’re going to head to Berlin the main sights you should see are The Laboratory (Male only) nightclub and Sachsenhausen Concentration camp.

The latter being more family friendly than the former.

The directions given in the email to get to the meeting point are perfect and the guides who meet you there are friendly and extremely engaging.

My guide was Martin who was a gentle giant. His beard as large as the warmth he emits.

It shocked me just how knowledgeable Martin was about history in general and not just the concentration camp - he clearly has a passion and thirst for history.

It was fascinating hearing about his own family’s experience with the Berlin Wall on the train to the camp as he pointed out interesting locations to take note of and really set the scene for what we were about to experience.

Taking us around the small town the camp is located in and then around the camp itself he was open to questions and really did a fantastic job at painting the grim picture which was Nazi Germany during the Third Reich!

I would highly recommend this tour if you’re a fan of history, have family ties or are just morbid - it’s extremely important to remember that we’re all just one bad decade away from finding ourselves in similar situations - and the more we know about the conditions Germans found themselves in during those times that made them not just allow this, but sometimes support it, the better - as we will be better equipped to avoid those mistakes ourselves.
Highly recommend this tour. It was really harrowing to visit but a must see for all. Maria was a fantastic guide, really friendly and knowledgeable!

We did this tour with our tour guide Campbell of Insider Tour. He is a History Major and we have never ever had such a fantastic and informed guide. It was a sombre, insightful, soul searching trip and Campbell’s philosophical words hit hard of our duty to know of Mann’s cruelty to man. Would strongly recommend this trip and if you get Campbell as your tour guide, you are on a winner !!

An excellent tour that was worth every penny! The day was very organised and our guide Phil provided us with an in depth history of Sachsenhausen Camp and was more than happy to answer all questions asked by the group.
Highly recommend factoring this tour in to your plans if you are visiting Berlin!

On a very cold day Phil gave the group an interesting tour. He was knowledgeable and helpful ensuring we got the most from our trip. Well worth the money. I hope you get the chance of having Phil take your tour.

Martin out tour guide was amazing the tour was emotional and thought provoking I doubt anyone left unchanged by this experience, good mobility Is a must and very warm clothing was needed for the tour on the day we went

We were very impressed with this tour. Very informative and tour guide Brian Bell was very friendly, knowledgeable and willing to help with purchasing tickets and informed others that there would be no opportunity to buy food at the concentration camp. Well worth the price as otherwise you walk around with a recording which looked confusing.

We visited Sachsenhausen yesterday and we were confident the tour was going to be great from the start. Our guide Maria helped us with train tickets and ensured the group had food and water for the day. This is essential as the tour starts at 10am and finishes at 4pm. Dress for walking and extremely cold weather as the camp is very cold.

The tour itself was amazing and Maria showed passion and real knowledge about the concentration camp and the history of the holocaust. She was very open to questions and made sure everyone was included.

This is a must see for anyone visiting Berlin. I would thoroughly recommend Insider Tours and Maria to guide you.

Collins Family

Traveling to Berlin was amazing, booking this tour was a must! Our tour guide was Brian and he filled us in with so many facts and made our day super interesting considering the nature of the trip. Couldn’t of asked for a better guide! Highly recommend.

This was a very informative, excellent tour. Our guide Gabi was extremely knowledgeable and her presentation and information was excellently presented. The tour proceeded exactly as was explained at the beginning. This tour provides information of a time in history which we should never forget. Thank you Gabi for your very important work.

We enjoyed the trip with our tour guide Gabi. She was very informative & knowledgeable. Whilst there we heard a very loud bang close by & found out a bit later (after one of the people on the tour googled it) that it was actually a bomb from WW2 that was detonated (a planned detonation) in the town about 5km away. So that was quite exciting in itself having been hearing all about WW2 horrors, then a real bomb goes off. It is a fast paced walk & alot of walking (we walked about 12km).

I wavered between 5 stars and 3 stars, but this is not because of Insider Tours or the memorial.

First, Insider Tours and our guide, Chloe, were excellent. Five stars, for sure. Chloe was tasked with having to manage a large group and share a lot of heavy and emotional information. She was clear and concise, engaged the group with thought provoking questions and facts and handled the information in a very respectful way. My ONLY criticism of the tour was the size - due to unforeseen circumstances, our group was combined with another group and we were over 30 people. I wish it had been half the size, it would have made for a different experience.

Second, the memorial is a sobering reminder of the worst of humanity and a warning bell for the future. Critical information is conveyed through photos, narratives and representations of living conditions for prisoners. It is a place that made me feel very uncomfortable, as it is supposed to. There is no easy way to recreate and depict these horrors, but they have done a good job. Definitely a place to visit and pray respects to those who’s lives were brutally taken.

My wavering on the rating, however, is more to do with how one absorbs information. If you absorb information purely through a guides narrative, without much opportunity for extensive engagement, this is a great tour. On the other hand - if you’re the type who spends time wandering through exhibits, this is probably a good idea to plan to stay for a few hours after the group departs to take time to walk through the exhibit. Note: this makes it a very long day. If you like extensive engagement, this tour is probably not for you (unless you’re sure it’s a smaller group).

My personal reflections: I found the tour rushed, and that I didn’t have a chance to reflect on the space or information. This is not a criticism of Chloe or the tour group - just information for folks who may want more time to reflect. Again, I also think the size of the group played a part in my experience.

Additional note: you can also go to Sachsenhausen on your own, without a group. I am not sure I would have done that as a solo traveler, but would go back on my own if I had time.
Jamie was an excellent guide. Very passionate about the history which was well conveyed to the tourists.

An excellent, informative and poignant tour of Sachsenhausen. Martin was just fantastic. Having worked as a tour guide for the museum itself he brought with it a deep understanding of it's history. From the moment we met at the train station he was giving us a huge amount of background history leading up to the time of the opening of the camp. No question went unanswered. Highly recommend to see the camp with a walking tour. You will get so much out of

Our guide, Maria, was outstanding. She was extremely well informed, very engaging and very well organized. I would rank Maria, and our visit to Sachsenhausen, among one of the best walking tours anywhere and deeply memorable. Maria ensured that each participant had a personal experience including making sure that we all knew exactly which train we needed to get back to our respective hotels once we had returned to Berlin.

Our tour guide, Sarah, met us in Berlin and was immediately helpful showing us the correct travel ticket for our day tour. As a group of approximately 12 people Sarah ensured all of us stayed together during the tour but allowed time for people to visit the exhibits alone too. Sarah was extremely knowledgeable and able to answer questions with no hesitation.
The place itself is a very sad place but due to the historical importance it is worth a visit when visiting Berlin.

Martin is a very friendly and knowledgeable guide. His passion for the subject led him to talk to survivors of the camp and enabled him to share knowledge that you don't find in books. Besides all the walking that was tiring and freezing, we had an enriching and fruitful time.

Martin also made sure that we knew how to get to wherever we wanted to go after the trip. Thanks, Martin!

Somber and distressing, but so important. Our guide, Martin, did a great job. He grew up in the area and provided interesting information about that as well as from his parents who lived there when it was East Germany. He was very personable and willing to answer all questions. He was particularly good with the younger (~16 yrs) members of our group.

A sobering tour, but certainly a must do to remind us that we must not allow a repeat of history. Our tour guide Sebastian was fantastic. Well spending the 5-6 hours doing this tour which went very quickly.

Julian our guide was excellent. His knowledge and delivery was first class. He made sure that the travel element was seamless. Just to have him navigate Hauptbahnhof was priceless. It is clear that this tour company hires the best talent. Did the Third Reich tour today with John. Both of these guys are entertaining, college educated historians. They can discuss topics on an entry level, or converse with experts equally well. We aren’t tour people, but at times it really makes sense to take part in a high quality program. Highly recommended and likely the best money spent in Berlin.

The only reason I did not give this tour a 5 star is because of the long and brisk walk to and from the train station to Sachsenhausen. Our tour guide (Phil) was great and shared so much information about Sachsenhausen with us. I know we would not have gotten as much out of our visit without a tour guide.

People need to see Sachsenhausen. It is a grim reminder of an awful time in history. Although there is not much standing there anymore, one can see where all the barracks (and how many) were, a recreated barrack showing how awful the living conditions were.

Phil also helped everyone with what trains to connect to to get where they were going after the tour. This was really great.

A must do experience with a great tour company.
Martin was a fantastic guide, very engaging and knowledgeable.
We visited a large part of the camp with in depth information at each area, Martin shared many stories of the torture and bravery - it was a great educational experience.
My tips include wearing good walking shoes and don't forget your water.

We learn a lot of this concentration camp, the guide was fenomenal, he born in the city, so was special. All persons should go to this tour, is just amazing see this camp and with the an expert like Martin was just perfect.

We were two mums visiting Berlin with 16 year old boys to support their GCSE history syllabus. Visiting Sachsenhausen with Insider really helped them to get the most from the visit and understand wider contexts for what happened here. Our guide Martin’s vast knowledge was invaluable, but he also shared the stories with empathy and genuine commitment to the importance of educating new generations about the history of the concentration camps. The boys were captivated and have since reshared many of the details they picked up on the tour, which proves how memorable and moving a visit it was for them. Massive credit to Martin for making this difficult subject matter so engaging for a diverse visitor group.

The tour was very informative and interesting. If you love history and are versed in most of the concentration camps and have background information it makes it even more interesting because you learn other important things and details from these tours. It’s a different experience because it allows you to understand even more what the poor prisoners had to endure and go through. I have always felt so much compassion and love for all the Jews and the innocent children that also suffered so much in concentration camps. Thanks so much to Martin, our tour guide who was very well informed and most importantly very passionate about history. He kept the whole group very interested the whole time. There were even 2 teenagers and they seemed very pleased with the tour. If you attend one of these tours, please remember this is not the place for selfies or posing inappropriately on some of the areas. This is a memorial and tourists should show some respect. Please note the tour involves quite a bit of walking. From the train station, it takes about 25 minutes to get to the camp. There are lockers there if you need to leave your items there so you’re more comfortable walking around the camp without having to carry stuff you won’t need. This tour really touched my heart. Make sure you add this to your list of sites to visit while in Berlin.

We visited on a sunny Tuesday in October 2019. Sebastian was our guide. He was very knowledgable about the history and painted the picture before we arrived. Vivid commentary on how some of the human race de-humanised others. A powerful presentation full of details.
The meeting place was easy- the guides were helpful and we were escorted on the train and walked to the camp.
The camp itself is a memorial so no one forgets the evil that happened.
Both teenage children listened uncomfortably but it was important part of history gcse work.
Recommend this trip.
Sebastian was approachable and knowledgeable. Asked lots of questions.
Escorted us back to train- and spoke to us all individually to find out where we wanted to be directed to at the end of the tour.
It’s an important tour well presented

As a new Berlin resident, I wanted to see this and I decided to do this tour by myself when my family was travelling. Walid was an uinbelievebly informative guide. I had visited some other concentration camps before, but on my own. This was a much richer experience with a ton of background information.

We were so lucky to have such a wonderful guide on this tour, a sombre visit but Martin really made it come alive with his almost encyclopaedic knowledge of Sachsenhausen. He gave us so much information but it was never dull, he managed to keep my 15 year old son engaged for hours, never easy, and we came away with so much learnt. Thank you, Martin, it’s people like you who will make sure we never forget. Highly recommend this tour.

This is a prison camp from before the WW2 era that evolved to be a concentration camp then post war prison.

We took the self guided audio tour which was extensive with loads of main and supplementary information. Allow yourself plenty of time (2hours plus) to get around the site at a steady pace.

Whilst much of the former barrack buildings have gone they are clearly outlined. Some have been rebuilt to show what conditions were like.

The camp is a little way from the station at Oranienburg and took us about 25-30 mins to walk. There is a bus service (804?) but only every 2 hours on a Sunday.

Definitely worth a visit to experience to put history into context.

Our tour guide Sebastian gave us what we call the “Coles notes” tour of the camp. I listened in on other tour guides to get more info. I found him not very approachable on our tour until it came to the end when he was looking for a tip.

Thank you to Ciaran our guide for an informative, fascinating tour. The context and background thoroughly explained, much appreciated. Ciaran had a warm and engaging personality and made sure everyone got the most out of the trip.
Met at Zoologischer Garten train station outside McDonald’s. Buy a Berlin ABC train ticket €7.70. You can buy this before the actual day and validate it on day of travel.
Sachsenhausen is a fitting memorial to those who lost their lives, were oppressed and persecuted.
Definitely worth a visit and the information shared by guide made the cost well and truly worth it. Thank you

Yan was our guide for the day, he was fantastic and we couldn't fault the experience! Good value for money for a day long tour. Yan really knew his stuff and was engaging throughout. It was informative, respectful and well organised. Everyone should visit and learn about what happened in these camps, it is a tragic part of history. Fully recommended.

This is a very moving trip to remember what people are capable of. Our tour guide Chloe was outstanding. Very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject. Lots of walking but well worth it. This tour will stay with me for a long time.

Just finished the Sachsenhausen CC tour with Martin, unforgettable experience, with an extremely knowledgeable guide who went above and beyond to help and create and enjoyable, info loaded experience.
Cheers!
Brooke & Deek, New Zealand

Martin our guide was excellent. The tour lasted a little longer than we expected, we met at 10am and arrived back in Berlin approx 4pm.
I would ensure that you grab some drinks and some lunch before you go, although Martin ensured that we had 10 minutes at the train station to get something to eat to take with us, depending on train timetables that may not always be possible though.. The trip was well organised, and as Martin was brought up in the area he gave a great insight into the small town.
The camp wasn't too crowded so you could easily move around and see the memorials etc. There is a 2k walk from the train station to get to the camp, however as long as the weather is dry then the walk itself isn't too bad.
The camp itself was quite windy so even if it's a nice day, take a jacket/jumper with you.

Met our Guide, Jim, at the designated meeting point and took the S Bahn to Orianenburg. On the way Jim set the tone, complimenting the tour party for taking on this type of tour. 40 min train and probably 15 minute walk, stopping as we walked through the town, Jim pausing and sharing his knowledge on the background to this camp. Sufficient group discussions but also enough time to talk in small groups to Jim. Truly enlightening and informative. Jim knew his subject matter very well.
Excellent tour

We had a great host (I’ve forgotten her name, but she is half Japanese and half Swedish). You could tell how passionate she was about the story of the people here. It was absolutely unfathomable the amount of wickedness that went on in this place. So sad and shocking. I would recommend this tour.

We had an amazing day with Taylor. We ran into some transportation glitches but he overcame them quickly and made sure that everybody stayed with the group and we got where we needed to go. Unfortunately it rained all day. However it gave us a good experience of what the people went through that were marching to the concentration camps. Of course not as bad but you get the idea. We learned many things and it's true that we did not spend a lot of time at each individual section of the memorial but at the end of our tour we were given the option to stay to look at things more extensively if we wanted. Because of the miserable whether we chose not to but Taylor made sure that everybody knew where they needed to go to get back home. It was an amazing day and I highly recommend the tour.

Martin was amazing during this tour. The concentration camp was held in his HOME TOWN! You don’t get any closer to the truth and authenticity than this. Fact aside, Martin did an amazing job explaining everything. This tour had honestly exceeded my expectations. HIGHLY recommend. It’s definitely worth it. Once I came back to my Airbnb from the tour, I immediately started researching more about the concentration camps and about that time. This tour made me want to learn even more about the history of the Holocaust and the Concentration Camps. Thanks a million for such an incredible experience.

Our tour guide was Julian. From the off he was attentive, friendly and knowledgeable, able to answer questions quickly and clearly from some of the more learned members of the group, never seemed stumped by the queries.

As well as making sure everyone got to hear him and, learned things during the tour, he made sure everyone knew how to get back to where they were staying upon our return and, even recommended places to eat and drink around the city.

All in all, 5 stars, very good.

I would recommend this trip to anyone interested in history. It is very informative and interesting to learn more about the life in the camp. I also would like to say Big Thank you to our guide Ariel who was very kind and answered all of our questions.
This was a guided visit which is advised as you get the true information....be aware in hot weather as this is an open air area

Our tour guide, Jakub, had a very good approach to talking about what had happened at the camp. I was concerned that due to the subject of the tour I would leave feeling very upset, but the way that Jakub guided us stuck to the facts whilst being respectful.

I would suggest this trip to anyone travelling to Berlin, as of course it is an important part of history to remember.

Similarly, our guide certainly deserves further praise for navigating us through the station and on the train on a very very busy day!

This is a must see if you are in Berlin. There is public transport involved and lots of walking so be sure you're relatively fit and wearing appropriate clothing. Our tour guide was Phil who was a fantastic tour guide. You could tell he had passion in the history of Berlin. He was happy to answer any questions anyone had and helped us with many other queries we had as tourists in Berlin. Thank you Phil for a memorable tour.
He gave us a lot of information about the camp and you really got a feel for how life must have been for those poor people.
This tour is fast paced but you are given the opportunity to stay after if you want but no one did, I feel we had all got enough information from Phil.

Very informative tour. We find the meeting point easily. Our guide sebastian was very good and knowledgeable. He gave us a lot of information during the train trip. This is a must see to remember what happened.

Yes it takes over an hour to reach on public transport but this is a must do. It's very sobering & sad to remind yourself of the horrors associated with this place. However in age where we take everything for granted, its good to be reminded of what can go horribly wrong if evil is not thwarted.

It's worth making the effort to visit the Sachsenhausen concentration camp, especially if you have a well prepared guide like Jakub. The Nazis dehumanised prisoners from the moment they set foot in Sachsenhausen, one of the earliest camps. During over four hours Jakub conveyed not only the ever present fear and oppression of the place, but also the astounding scale of the operation and its impact on individual lives. You won't come away with anything much more than a partial understanding of the motivation behind the madness, but it's frightening enough to make you want to keep a wary on any contemporary form of ideological racism.
During a break in a business trip schedule, we went to visit. It's a must see! Our tour guide was excellent and made sure we saw everything. Very emotional yet very educational.

I would have to recommend this trip to anyone visiting Berlin and looking to extend on some of the information they might have read in any number of museums around museum island, on the subject of the early concentration camp used by the Nazis.
Our guide on this trip was Taylor and he was so careful to talk the group through so much of the build up to arriving at the Sachsenhausen camp, that you understood who was likely to have been walking the route you took to the camp, what lead to their incarceration and what was the chance of surviving such a place.
With so much background being shared with you as you move around the grounds, you can easily experience the emotions of many of the personal and camp stories.
This is a fantastic way to spend a day understanding and experiencing German and world history.

Both Roisin and I had a fab time on the trip. Apologies we couldn’t say thank you at the end face to face! Really informative, engaging and well worth seeing. Ronan was a star throughout in giving us as much information as we wanted. Very knowledgable.

We wanted to go to the camp me and my 15yr old son who has just come back from the flanders and the somme,And he is mad on war history so we booked before we arrive in berlin as my other son did the tour in may,We was met at the meeting point at 10 by the lovely walid who told us the get the train tickets first plus water and food then other group arrived where we then got on the train to the camp,We then walked another 20 minutes to the camp with stops for usefull information from walid,as we arrived at the camp we where all given a information leaflet about the came the tour lasted about 2 hours in baking sun but was given loads of storys about life in the camp walid goes above and more as a guide asking about everbody on the tour about there lifes hes a great guide and top bloke credit to the company overall well worth to book the trip.
Was a very impressive tour, tour guide was very friendly too 😊 Walid was his name, knew a lot about the camp

I'm so glad we STARTED our tour of Berlin with this site and with TJ Travel. I had never heard this site mentioned before, but its importance is not to be overlooked. Our tour guide, Kathinka, was excellent? I would love to have her on any tour in Berlin. She was so easy to understand and was able to set up each place we viewed with background history that really enhanced our tour. I highly recommend this site AND TJ Travel.

Julian was our guide. He was very good and informative. Highly recommend this activities. It takes most of the day but it is well worth it. Recommend packing some snacks for the trip as they don't have a snack vending place at the camp. Also if you are going to get one of the tourist passes for Berlin that include public transportation make sure that you tell them that you are going to Sachsenhausen so they sell you the right pass with the right zone for transportation.

Really glad to have went on this tour, the guide Phil was excellent, friendly and took great care of the group in 34 degree heat, making sure to stop for talks in any shaded areas available.

For what is a very difficult subject to cover Phil was extremely knowledgeable and answered any questions fully.

At the end of the tour he took the time to help with any travel issues or questions and suggestions for the rest of the trip.

Would highly recommend this tour and guide company.

Our tour guide was EXCELLENT! She was fun, knowledgeable and so kind during the tour and ensuring everyone knew how to use the train system to get to where they needed to go once the tour was completed. The tour itself was outstanding, breathtaking, and sobering, but an educational experience absolutely worth experiencing!

Very glad that we set aside a day of our time here in Berlin to do this tour. Our guide Jamie from Insider Tours was great. He was able to tell us so many details that I am sure we would have missed if we had chosen to just tour the site on our own. Some of the stories he told us were fascinating. There were a few museums/exhibitions there that I would have liked to have more free time to look at and read about, but due to the schedule of the group tour, we had to keep moving on. There is a lot to see there, and it can be a bit overwhelming to process it all in just a few hours.

A few tips...

- Make sure to pack snacks and water bottles for a full day. There is not ever really a break for lunch or anything like that, but plenty of opportunities to eat snacks along the way.
- This is a walking tour (with LOTS of walking!). Definitely recommend wearing comfortable and good walking shoes. There is about a 20 minute walk once you get off the train to get to the actual memorial site. And then about 2-3 hours of walking/standing during the tour itself.
- Bring sunscreen! I also wish I had thought to wear a hat. Most of the walking you do is out in the open under the sun.
- You can get your ABC Zone day train ticket on your phone with the BVG app. This is often easier than getting a paper ticket and validating in the station. Just make sure you get ABC (not just AB) and chose the correct date that you will be traveling on before you purchase it.

This is a crucial and very timely trip for everyone to make to remind us all of what can happen when we are not paying attention. I strongly suggest getting yourself to the memorial (which takes a while but is not difficult) and taking a tour with the "Public Guided Tours by Friends of the Memorial" as advertised on the site's website. You can take the bus there if no one is there to meet for the tour--there is a little placard in the circle directly outside the bus station telling you which bus to take. It's about a 1.5-2k walk (the signage was confusing...) Once there, our guide Leah had a degree from University of Haifa in Holocaust Studies and was very knowledgeable. She was able to answer every question authoritatively and sensitively. I actually can't imagine anyone dealing with this subject matter in a better way. These tours currently run Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday at 10:50 (definitely) and 2 (I think) but I suggest emailing to confirm the afternoon times. At 14 EUR per person (12/student) the tour was excellent value. It isn't fun necessarily, but do it anyway. It is important.

Our guide Jakub was the most knowledgeable, helpful and intelligent guide ever! All day he kept 20 people organised to a tight schedule without being harsh or pushy, and we had so much opportunity to learn! It’s definitely better to do this trip with a guide who can spend all of the time on the train stations, train trips and walking along telling you the overall history and then the specific details. We got so much context for the events of the time. Jakub was incredibly knowledgeably and personally-connected with his material as most good guides are. He was also keen to learn from his group members, which was refreshing. We went around in an ordered way and saw so much. We all particularly enjoyed his discussion of the metalanguage of remembrance: who made each memorial sculpture/item and why, and what impact does that have on what we see now? Or who took each photo, and what was their worldview? How can this be seen in the photo itself? For people keen to pursue these topics of representing history and memory and experience, much opportunity was available throughout the day to talk to Jakub.

Warning: buy your ABC ticket in advance as it saves time, take plenty of water, and quick snacks to eat as you go. No shops as such and NO LUNCH BREAK to sit down. Lots of walking, obviously, and pretty emotionally/intellectually draining. But a complete highlight for all 6 of us!

The tour was great but I would like to commend our tour guide Jakub. He was so knowledgeable and was all round a very nice guy to have as our guide. He helped all people of our group to find their way back home and informed us on a spot to eat for dinner that night. The tour was made even better in my opinion having Jakub as our tour guide. Thank you Jakub!

If you want a guide that cares about German history then you should pick Julian. He knows more than most Germans (and he’s Canadian, I know crazy right? 😉)
Apart from that, it’s just a mind blowing experience to see such horrible things and to be confronted with how evil some people were. I think this should be part of any Berlin trip as it reminds us just how cruel some people were and still are. Use this as an incentive to never let anyone do this again.

We were fortunate enough to have Nadav as our guide. He was able to recreate the atmosphere and experiences of the camp through powerful and personal stories.

On a practical level, this tour is long without a meal break. Be sure to have an ABC travel ticket, snacks, and plenty of hydration, particularly if visiting in the summer.
Excellent trip to Sachsenhausen with an excellent guide named Sebastian. Great history teller and enthusiastic conveyor. We highly recommend this trip with him.

Very well organised tour, Phil was fantastic and extremely knowledgeable- he was able to provide lots of additional information and answer all questions. Really appreciate the extra effort he went to ensuring that everyone got to their next destinations.

We did this tour on our last day in Berlin and recommend it to anyone that wants to get a better understanding of the how and why of the Nazi Germany era. Brian our tour guide provided us with so much information and delivered the tour with passion and enthusiasm. There is a lot to take in and a lot of time on your feet, but came away with so much more.

Jakub was our guide for this central part of our recent trip to Berlin. Needless to say, it is not easy to revisit the horrors of Nazi Germany, but it is necessary to know this history so that we are not destined to repeat it. In this regard, Jakub was incredibly well informed and articulate in presenting his extensive knowledge of this period in history. It was a six-hour tour from start to finish, but one couldn't imagine it being any shorter. Jakub's passion and devotion to his subject captivated everyone in the group. It was a stifling hot day, but Jakub's manner of presentation managed to keep everyone alert and engaged. In my book, this is a must-do when visiting Berlin!

On a recent trip to see my daughter in the fabulous city of Berlin, I had the opportunity to visit Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp. Since my daughter had to work that day, I located an Insider Tour on TripAdvisor. A group of sightseers from multiple countries met up with our tour guide, Taylor, at the train station. where we proceeded out of town to the camp. Arriving in Sachsenhausen, our guide led us through the town pointing out landmarks and vital information related to the camp. Upon arriving at Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp, we walked the entire camp, while exploring the various structures, displays and museums housing pertinent data and artifacts. Though you can view the grounds on a self-guided tour, it was gratifying to have Taylor available to answer any questions, which he was quite proficient on answering. I also felt he was instrumental in giving us the "inside view" of the camp, relaying valuable information you wouldn't get from taking a self-guided tour. It is important to note that since this is a walking tour, plan on doing some extensive walking, wearing your most comfortable walking shoes.Would highly recommend taking the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp Memorial Tour from Insider Tours, and if you land Taylor as your tour guide, all the better!

As expected the tour is somber, but accurate and super informative. Our goal was to get as much history as possible. Our guide Sebastian was very personable and knew an extensive amount which, overall highten our experience. He was well spoken, answered any questions asked and really gave us a detailed perspective. This tour is very well put together and worth the money.

I visited Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp on May 11th and had Chloe as a tour guide! The whole experience was done very professionally and Chloe did a fantastic job as our guide! She made sure everyone was prepared for the day ahead before we even got on our first train! On our way back, she went to each group of travellers ensuring that they knew how to get back to where they wanted to go. I thought the tour might seem long at times, but that was not at all the case. She captivated us the entire time and found a good balance between giving facts and telling stories to really let you take in all the information. If you’re making a trip out I highly recommend this tour! Great value for money and Chloe went above and beyond!!

Getting there may sound a bit fiddly, but it's really not.We met at the Hackescher Market location, which is at the base of the stairs to the train station. So, go up & get your ABC ticket, back down the stairs & check in with the tour guide. Wait there until everyone assembles. Meet your guide, walk together up the stairs & all ride the train together, so there is no confusion about where to get off. Walk the 15-20 minutes together to the camp. Tour the camp. Ride a bus from the camp back to the train station. While riding, the guide will make sure you either get off at the same place you got on or give you recommendations on what to do next & guide you where to get off. It really couldn't be easier. As far as the tour, excellent, you won't see it all, but you'll spend a decent amount of time seeing lots of it. We got a sandwich for lunch at the bakery at Hackescher Market but we didn't have a chance to eat it until we were waiting for the bus on the return. There are no brakes. The area is windy & dusty so bring a beverage, too. Great tour, great way to see it. Passionate guide.

A very interesting detailed tour of the camp. So much history of the horrors dealt to the inmates. A lengthy tour that involved taking a train journey of about 40 minutes from city then a BRISK walk through the town of about 20 minutes until you reach the actual camp. You need to take drink and food with you as tour is intense but you do get opportunities to use the toilets and buy books etc from shop. Also wet weather gear or appropriate clothing as tour is out in the open for most of it. You need an ABC train pass as one of our group only had an AB (ticket lady had misheard her request) and she got fined 60 euro. On the check to camp she was ok as had not entered C area but on the way back check was made early and her ticket didnt extend to that area. Also important to validate ticket before boarding train. Still a tour worth taking if you want to understand the living conditions and horrors administered to the inmates. Our tour guide was very informative.

I would recommend this tour to everyone, the tour guide Sebastian deserves top marks he did a great job organising us on the right trains to get to site and back, Sebastian knowledge was top class and the way it was delivered enabled everyone to understand and contemplate. Would not recommend to do this tour independently as this tour is great value for money and Sebastian shows all the camps exhibits and gives you all the facts
Would like to thank Sebastian for the day

We met our guide Walid at the zoological garden train station (outside McDonalds) at 10am. He was amazing from the start, helped us buy a train ticket (which we found a little complex). Walid made the whole group feel at ease and asked us what our background was. The train journey was easy and we chatted with Walid and our new companions on the journey which took about 45 mins. Walid's knowledge of the camp and life in Berlin during WW2 was incredible, he is obviously well read and passionate about the subject matter. It also really helped that my teen thought he was cool. It was a tough experience, but with the knowledge and passion that Walid brought to the whole experience we didn't feel anything other than well informed & educated about the camp. Going with a guide gave the experience a different perspective, which I wasn't expecting, but would not have done this any other way. Walid was compassionate and sensitive about the truly awful subject matter, and made the whole experience worth while.

Spent the day with our tour guide Campbell, met us at the meeting point at 10am. I would advise you to get your ticket and something before meeting up, however if you forget there is a Starbucks there you can grab some water and a sandwich.

About the experience, I would highly recommend doing it with a guide, as there was so no much information provided and throughout.

The trip is well organised from start to finish, the tour guide will stay with you and if you have to break away from the group you will not be left behind as headcounts are taken before moving on.

This trip is a must when visiting Berlin, there were young children at my visit, I would caution this as it's clearly quite an emotional topic and may cause upset.

A great experience!

I took my two children 12 and 17. Very informative trip. Very knowledgeable guide JJ(John from Cork)
Would really recommend trip.

This was brilliant. Very easy, We went to the meeting point outside of Mcdonalds and paid the operator and they sorted our train tickets. Yan was our tour guide who we met at the 2nd station. Very knowledgeable and knew everything they was to know about the history etc. Very interesting and highly recommended!!!!!! 5 star!

This tour was phenomenal beyond all expectations. Our tour guide, Taylor, was truly incredible, We learned so much above and beyond the history of the camp itself. Taylor gave one of the most concise, effective explanations of Hitler's rise as a perfect way to set the stage for the tour. We walked from the train in Oranienburg to the camp and Taylor stopped along the way to explain the surroundings and how a town could have seen prisoners walking down their street to the camp and done nothing. His commentary was thought-provoking, comprehensive and so helpful in understanding the full scale of the camps in Germany. The camp tour was very, very informative and we learned more than we could have imagined. Cannot recommend it enough.

See what happens a great country falls for "Pie in the sky" politics...I wish ever one could take this tour...It is really amazing to see what happened to a great country like Germany...and sadly is still happening in other countries....This place was real..this isnt some made up story...

Ronan was our tour guide with good personality and funny and lots of knowledge we very enjoyed the tour, Its a long day and walking all day , provide your own meal and drinks and don’t forget to buy ABC transportation ticket buy all day ticket , wear walking shoes and bring sunglasses.

Outstanding tour of the concentration camp the knowledge that our tour guide Ronan has is amazing, even though the tour is a full day you will not get to see everything as it would realistically take you around 3 days to look at all the exhibitions and read all the info , that’s why the best way to get around etc is by a tour guide & also you can ask them questions, put some comfy shoes on by the way. This tour is a must when visiting Berlin.

I went on the day trip to Sachsenhausen Concentration camp today with Insider Tours and I would highly recommend.
Booking was super easy and Mike our guide was very helpful explaining which trains and buses we needed to get to get to the camp and he had extensive knowledge on the camp, the second World War and the later Soviet activity at the camp and was happy to be asked questions throughout.
Whilst I believe it's possible to visit alone I think it's well worth paying extra to go with Insider Tours as I would not have learnt as much as I did if I had gone on my own.

When our tour guide Phil first addressed our group, I knew it would be a good day. He was engaging and extremely knowledgeable on his subject.

I can’t fault the tour, which we did with our teenage sons. The history of the camp was fascinating and it was an experience to visit and understand what went on inside its walls.

The tour is 6 hours including travel time by train to the camp. It did not seem a long day but we dressed warmly for the bitter cold at the camp, and took a small lunch with us which was eaten outside.

I thoroughly enjoyed this tour. The things we saw at the camp were very serious and sobering. Everyone should take the time to take this tour.

Maria was an awesome guide. She made sure our group of about 20 got on and off at the correct S Bahn stops and made sure we all kept up with group. She knew her stuff and made tour fantastic!! I highly recommend her as your guide.There is a LOT of walking...especially between the Orienenberg Train station and the camp. Nearly a mile.

This tour started at 10 AM and we arrived back in Berlin about 4. Plan to spend most if your day on this tour.

The day trip to Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp is a good experience. Phil took care of our little tour group and made sure that we made all the train connections and were prepared and comfortable throughout the tour. He gave us a lot of background information pertaining to the time and events leading up to beginnings of the Nazi camps. Phil also gave us information on making the correct train connection after the tour was completed. I think the tour is a good value. If taking this tour in the winter be sure to wear layers, heavy hooded jacket, scarf around neck, gloves, and a good pair of walking shoes.

Walld is an energetic guide with lots of passion for doing his job! Will definitely recommended. The only thing is as a student, you can actually get a reduced price (14 euro) in person instead of full price (17 euro) on TripAdvisor. So I will pay in the meeting point by cash next time.
Amazing tour. So informative and well organized. Appropriate for all ages too. I was travelling alone and did this tour alone. I loved every minute of it

This was a really interesting day trip. George was our guide for the day and we couldn't have asked for better. His knowledge and passion for this era of history was unbelievable. So informative. We got back to Alexanderplatz about 4.30pm and George went to everyone in the group to help with directions to their individual destinations. The tour itself is really worth doing. You get to relive a part of history that should never be forgotten. Many thanks George. Wendy and family from Ireland

This is an easy day trip from Berlin. Met the guide at Hacksher Markt as planned. He was punctual and very helpful making sure all guests had the proper tickets etc. We took the train to the camp - about 30/45 minutes. Unfortunately we had to make our way on a bus because of work on the tracks (more on this later). There is a 20 minute walk from station to the camp - at a brisk clip. The walk is on flat paved terrain - but be advised. It is actually the walk many prisoners took to Sachsenhausen. Once at the camp Campbell guided us through many of the 'sites'. Of course a lot of the original camp was destroyed but there has been some thoughtful reconstruction. Campbell did is best to give a lot of detail without sensationalizing the more gruesome aspects. At the end of the day I felt we got a good feel as to the daily life of the prisoners, and the arc of those imprisoned at Sachsenhausen . Little to no amenities at the camp as to be expected. Be sure to pack a lunch and water. There is no stopping for lunch just eat while you are walking on the grounds (not in any structures). Remember you have a 20 minute walk back to station after 3+ hour tour. The track repair and bus to the station made our return difficult. We ended up getting separated from our group and luckily found a cab to take us to the station about 10 miles away for 28 Euro for 6 of us. - almost incredible as it was Sunday and Oranienburg is virtually shut down.

Also remember to tip your guide! Especially if you get Campbell. He is terrific!
Fantastic informative day! Excellent, knowledgeable and very interesting guide Rob Shaw! Highly recommended! Really enjoyable!

I came away from this tour having learnt so much more. It was very eye opening and sad but our guide Campbell was fantastic and gave such a good background to everything and I learnt so much. I would 100% recommend.

One of the best tours we've had till date! Our tour guide was Phil who took us through the historic stories and scenes of the Sachenhausen concentration camp. Our tour began at 10am and we returned back around 4pm. The tour takes you through the deeper / dark aspects of German history showcasing the Nazi era which led the concentration camps and prisons at Orianenburg. Phil is a highly knowledgeable tour guide who's understanding of the German history is vast. He not only spoke about the camp specifics but also gave much more insight in terms of related books, museums, places to visit, etc.

A place everyone should visit and take time to think of those that suffered here. The camp has easy to follow directions and plenty of information boards to paint a picture of what life was like for those incarcerated here. It is easy to get to the camp from Berlin by train and walk and can be done independently and you don’t have to go on an organised tour. The organised tours go the same way.

We took the tour with Maria just some days ago. Though physically demanding (Berlin blessed us with some sunny and hot days, but there is almost no shade in Sachsenhausen and there's hardly a place to sit, so think about it carefully before planning the tour), it's a remarkable experience that should not be missed. Our guide taught us a lot about the camp, those who operated it, and some of the most important prisoners held there, in a very straightforward but sensitive way at the same time. She did her best to give us some time to rest and have a quick lunch and break and appeared highly professional and well informed. Though there were no babies nor kids in our group, I'd suggest not to visit the camp with young children (we saw a couple of them in the camp, one in a stroller), as the experience may just be demanding and perhaps less educational for them. I'm sure there is a suitable way to introduce children and kids to the topic, as it is an important yet sad and mad part of our past that needs to be known to be better people in our present. We were highly satisfied with the experience and would certainly recommend Maria as a guide!

The tour was very good. The subject was of course hard to take but Maria did a great job of explaining what we were looking at, gave stories from things that had happened. Not too much remains but it is still a crucial part of history we should never forget.

Our guide told us when we arrived at Sachsenhausen that he admired us for deciding to take this tour during our holiday. The things you see during this tour are not pretty, but I think it is crucial to visit, as it is a very important piece of history.
Walid was a great guide, you could tell he knew a lot about the subject. He also did an effort in communicating and getting to know a little about each person in the group. Absolutely lovely!
If you have time, do not miss the oportunity to go on this journey. It really makes you think.

We took the Sachsenhausen Camp Tour from Berlin and Chloe was our guide. She was amazing -- really enjoyed the tour. She is very enthusiastic about the topic, and a wealth of information. She made getting to the camp and touring the camp really easy.

I was also very impressed by how she was very vigilant about keeping a headcount of everyone with her so that no one got left behind. She assumed that everyone there didn't know their way around.

I think that she did a fantastic job of handling the delicate subject matter and can highly recommend her and her tour company!

Worth every penny. Our tour guide was Cesar and his knowledge was amazing. You need a guide to really bring the buildings and camp to life. Don’t hesitate to book this trip, by the look of it all the guides are great.

You really have to think carefully before visiting a concentration camp. In the case of Sachsenhausen near Berlin you have to do a lot of walking and you need to have your own food and water. There is nothing available there but the tap water is potable.
Thank goodness for Nickolai, our Insider Tour guide who shepherded us from Berlin to the camp on the train. He was very knowledgeable and kept our spirits up in a place that is profoundly disturbing. Nickolai was also a master of finding shade for us to stand in while he addressed us. Remember to have an ABC zone transit pass before joining the tour. This will not be supplied.

It was touch & go as to whether to visit here but so glad we did. Our guide was Phil who did an incredible job filling us in with all the history of this camp. So much so that we went on to book a further tour knowing his knowledge would give us just the best taster of Berlin. The camp was a very humbling place to visit. Its an eye opener to what went on during its occupancy but this trip is a must do & worth every penny. Not much shade here and plenty of walking so dress accordingly.

With such a sensitive subject, Wallid gave an excellent tour of The concentration camp. Even when the weather turned horribly cold & rainy, he kept us all as warm as possible, while filling us with his knowledge and facts of what had occurred here.

Highly recommend doing the tour with Walid. Did the Sachsenhausen tour with him Saturday and it was brilliant, could have gone on our own but Walid made it so more interesting, from when we left Hackersher markt to when we got back again he was explaining all about the camp and Berlin, than and now. I haven't really done tours like this but and definitely going to consider them in future trips. Walid wasn't just teeming off a load of facts, it was very informal and friendly and I actually learned so much that I wouldn't have if I just went alone.
We took this tour on one of our last days in Berlin. Mike was an incredible guide, incredibly knowledgable and helpful our entire day.

Campbell was our guide, excellent guide. Kept everyone together manoeuvring our group in/out of Berlin on the trains, very very knowledgeable about everything he talked to us about, was engaging with the whole group and gave us lots of opportunities for questions. Great job Campbell!
The concentration camp itself had a lot of reading material on the various buildings and spots around the camp, with the chambers as well in tact as they could've kept them, which was interesting to see.
What made the excursion that little bit more special was being able to be there on the 73rd anniversary of when the camp was liberated. It gave the visit that little bit more meaning of being there for me. Overall, highly recommend this Insider Tour and I plan to book another tour with Insider again on my next visit if i get the chance - organised, friendly, easy to book and budget friendly.

So let’s say my family over slept the morning of our walking tour( late arrival from Paris the night before)... although we were semi on time after a little direction from the Insider company, we managed to meet up with the group. Our guide Walid did a fantastic job bringing the group to and from the camp, explaining the importance of each building with much respect. He made it a point to engage everyone in the group remembering most of our names and where we all were from. I highly recommend our guide Walid as Insider tours has a gem of a guide!

We took the tour with Taylor and it was a great tour. It was a smooth start with an easy meeting point and full assistance at the train stations. He gave excellent information regarding the camp and was great to talk to in general. It was a heavy day but well worth a visit to get a better understanding of the horrors that took place.

This tour is a "Must Do"' in Berlin if you want to know more about the horrors of concentration camps during Wold War II. It is emotionally draining but worth it to realise what so many innocent people went through. Our Guide - Taylor- struck the right note between giving us the history and details of the camp and being most respectful to the memories of those who suffered there.

My granddaughter who is twelve said she felt traumatized as she read the history I knew the history and still wondered why we humans never learn from the past. I found the trip tiring and hot but well worth the visit

We did the Sachenhausen walking tour with Insider Tours on Friday. We hadn't booked in advance so just arrived at the meeting point in Hackescher Markt in good time and had no problems identifying the staff and buying tickets. Chloe was our guide and she took the time to introduce herself to everyone before we set off. The tour requires a train journey and Chloe helped to make sure that everyone had the correct ticket and something to eat with them etc. Once we met the second group (from the West of the City) we were on our way!
We had a great time - Chloe had no problems looking after our group of 27 and was very knowledgeable on all aspects of the camp. Although the tour takes something like 6 hours the time went very quickly and we felt as if we had learned an awful lot.
Sachenhausen, although much changed from it's original state still provided enough of an insight for an informative and enjoyable day out, albeit on a range of difficult subjects. I'd recommend this tour to anyone and thought it was excellent value.

Chloe did a great job. She is knowledgeable, sensible and shows and induces a respectful attitude concerning the site. The camp is conveniently close to Berlim but most of its buildings result from restorarions. Even so it does a decent job of showing what the hollocaust has been, especially to new generations.

Mike Stack knows what he is doing. Seriously you will get the best tour of your life. There is no room for doubting. He knows tons about the history of nazi germany but, on top of that, he has gave a good thought ot it and he gives room to analyze the facts and discuss them. Amazingly he does all of that with a lot of respect and including humor. Overall, you will end your day knowing a lot about nazi german history, having a wonderful time and getting emotional engaged with this tragic events of history. When he asked as to review his tour on tripadvisor I told him that he deserves to own tripadvisor! And he actually deserves it.

I had Brian as a tour guide. His depth of knowledge is unbelievable and his passion for history is truly amazing. Our group met in town before heading off on the train to the Sachsenhausen Camp, and straight away we were given lots of information on Berlin and Germany and how Hilter came to power. Brian gave us an in depth tour of the camp which was quite harrowing, what those people must have gone through is mind blowing to me. I cannot imagine what it must have been like, but walking around the camp, listening to Brian and reading all the information I have a pretty good idea.
I would highly recommend this tour, if only to see how we must not let history repeat itself!!

Our tour guide Pip was extremely helpful and very knowledgeable. It was a great (if not harrowing) experience about an important part of Berlin's dark history, and it was very informative. I would recommend this to anyone visiting Berlin, particularly if you're coming for a historical endeavour.

My wife and I toured Sachsenhausen on our recent vacation in Berlin. We were very fortunate to have Nicholi as our guide. He was able to tell the story of the camp and identify historical events that happened there. We were very glad we took this tour.

The insider tour of Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp was one of, if not THE best, thing we did in Berlin during our trip (other than eating Currywurst).

For those who have an interest in WWII and Cold War history and want to learn about it in more detail, this is the tour for you.

Note: I would not recommend this tour to those who have trouble walking.

Our tour guide was Walid, who absolutely knocked it out of the park. The tour was neither a crawl or a sprint but very well paced.

He also found a great balance between his talks throughout the tour and letting us discover the details for ourselves. He intrigued us with facts and knowledge at each part of the tour and gave us time to study the landmarks further on our own. He certainly didn't sprout elongated facts all day which was a great touch.

With the dark history of the camp, Walid also balanced the hard hitting facts with some light-hearted and uplifting spirit. It's difficult not to feel sensitive and upset during a tour like this considering its dark past, but Walid did a great job of identifying the moments of sulk between the group and bringing us all back up with an amusing tale.

There was plenty of time to ask Walid further questions which he was very happy and enthusiastic to answer.

Would recommend this tour to anyone visiting Berlin for the first time.

Also, if you go...please don't whip out the selfie stick. It's just plain disrespectful.

Our tour group was bigger than we expected, over 20 people, but Phil made it feel like a smaller group. He was very professional, personable, and clearly has an outstanding body of knowledge regarding 20th century German history in general, and Sachsenhausen in particular. Phil was more than willing--and well-prepared-- to answer any questions regarding the camp. On the way back on the train he gave us two restaurant recommendations: Clärchens Ballhaus and Prater Biergarten, both of which we enjoyed. He also told us about the "Alltag in der DDR," a free and very interesting museum. Highly recommend this experience.

I booked tickets through TripAdvisor for Insider Tours. From start to finish the tour was excellent. Our guide, Ronan was full of knowledge and really brought history to life. (We were saying we learnt alot more today about the concentration camps than we did for our Leaving Cert (school exams).

There is too much to cover in this review but whether you have an interest in European history or don't, the tour is worth it!
The tour is outdoors so make sure you check the weather and wrap up if needed!

I am the first to admit I am very ignorant when it comes to history and was not really looking forward to this but my other half was so off i went ... grudgingly. We met our guide Mike at a central train station and he gave us a history lesson on the 45 min train journey out to the camp and from the minute he started talking I was hooked , he was so enthusiastic and knowleagable and I enjoyed listening and learning to everything he has to say. The camp itself was an experience and whilst it is quite emotional again our guide Mike made it a wonderful experience. To anyone who is not sure about doing one of these tours please put your fears aside and do it. You will not be disappointed.

A fantastic enlightening trip! Our tour guide Ronan was extremely informative and went above and beyond when answering everyone's questions. He made sure everyone knew how to get back to their destination and took the time to sit and chat with everyone on the way there and back. A must do for everyone!

Fascinating trip to the concentration camp. Very well organised and very punctual trip. The guide Jamie's was very interesting and friendly who really added to the trip. His knowledge was really impressive and he delivered this information a really interesting manner. I learned a lot and really enjoyed the trip which I would highly recommend. Jamie answered loads of questions and even made sure everyone knew where we were catching onward transport links from. A superb guide and tour. Thanks Jamie!

Jamie guided this tour in a very knowledgeable, and insightful way. His approach is not only factual, but he is open as well to share his own view and interpretation which brings another human dimension. I am usually not a fan of guided tour, but had not time to organize on my own this visit- I am really happy I did it, and challenged at the same time my perception.
Anyway, I highly recommend this visit..and wish you to be able to get not one of Jamie's group!

I would highly recommend this tour. Our guide was Mike and not only was he extremely knowledgeable about Sachsenhausen, he was also very friendly and personable. I did the tour with my friend and he met us at one of the stations, then we met up with the others. From start to finish he was full of information.

Absolutely brilliant tour of Sachsenhausen. Well worth taking a guided tour and I recommend Insider Tour. Jamie was extremely knowledgeable, informative and passionate. He helped us get our rail tickets and helped us get back to where we were going in Berlin. He even gave us advice on where to eat and drink in the evening, which proved to be spot on.

We recently took this tour with Jared and could not recommend it enough. He was passionate and obviously very knowledgeable. He gave us some background on the train journey to the camp and was more informative than any audio guide or book would have been. Despite temperatures of around -5 Jared kept everybody interested and was happy to stop and answer questions along the way. He even went out of his way to make sure everybody knew how to get to where they wanted to be on the train back to the centre. If we had more time in Berlin we would have definitely gone on another Insider Tour.

Our tour started in the morning where our guide, Jared took us from central Berlin to Oranienburg and then onto the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp. Jared’s knowledge was amazing and you could tell he had a clear passion for these type of topics, yet he spoke about it in such a way that it gave the topics the respect they deserved. These were topics such as torture, suffering and mortality alongside many more. I could not recommend Jared as a guide any more. The information he provided was just as, if not more insightful than the sort of information you could take from reading the boards at the camp itself.

The tour itself lasted for several hours and our interest did not wane at all (despite our feet getting severely cold towards the end!). There was a short lunch break and we were back in Berlin at a nice time ready for dinner.

For the price of this experience, I would thoroughly recommend doing something like this. Not just because our tour from Jared was great but because I feel it is important to learn about these aspects of history and humanity.

After the Berlin trip we were surprised to see the same guide, Brian Bell, was going to take us to Sachenhausen. It turned out to be a great day and Brian's knowledge and his manner of imparting information really added to the experience. It was a long day and I got a sense of what inmates may have gone through. There was no lunch break but we were given time to organise food and drinks before we left Berlin. It was good advice and having to eat on the run (walk) added to the sense of hardship of the place. The intensity of the information grew throughout the tour and we had time to reflect on what we had learnt. The day we toured was cold and this was also a part of the experience. Checking the weather before hand would be helpful.
This is definitely a tour my wife and I would recommend.

Although an intense trip due to the subject, it was incredibly helpful and interesting to listen to our our guide Phil go into detail regarding various areas and elements of the camp. He certainly came across very passionate about the history and myself and my partner learned many new things. If you're visiting Berlin for Historic reasons then I'd definitely recommend this trip.

Went on the Sachsenhausen Concentration camp tour with Walid, he gave us a great insight into life in the camp while not reeling off the usual spiel some tour guides would and was very helpful even in the horrible wind &rain!!!

This is a very organised, and thoughtful trip. Insider tours do a great job in shepherding you through the Berlin public transport system and out to the camp. Walking from the station as the prisoners did. Our guide , Taylor was informative and engaging, passionate without being preachy and managed to engage all of us.
The camp itself is sensitively done, quite understates at times.

I would highly recommend doing the concentration camp tour to Sachsenhausen from Berlin. Our guide, Phil, was entertaining and extremely informative. I do feel that going to the concentration camp is something everyone should experience. Definitely wear good walking shoes and bring a bag lunch/bottle of water. Phil also gave us an awesome recommendation for local places to eat and helped us figure out our train tickets for the next day. Thanks, Phil!
Excellent tour of the Concentration Camp. The tour guide, Taylor, was very knowledgable and passionate about the subject

Our visit to Sachsenhausen with this company was first class; our guide Walid was very informative and charismatic, which made what could have been a morbid day into a fascinating one. I definitely recommend booking with Insider Tour Berlin and hopefully you will get Walid too.
An overwhelming but necessary educational experience led by a phenomenal guide Martin, who grew up in the surrounding area and was beyond an expert.

Our tour guide was Gregor. He was absolutely fantastic! Gregor told us he was born in East German and he gave us a very interesting insight in what it was like growing up in East Germany and what his family went through. It was very beautiful, especially as he went through the tour and its history. He was very passionate and engaging, and he gave my husband and I alot of very thought provoking questions. The tour was very organized, very informative, very easy to follow, and very special.
Don’t hesitate to book this tour, you won’t regret it.

Very engaging and informative tour guide! Walid was both thorough and entertaining! Very attentive to detail and was very much aware of the high temperatures. We were enduring.Really interesting tour and a valuable experience.
Easy to locate and travel together and had an awesome tour guide who gave tons of information, highly recommend.
This tour was informative and thought provoking. Our tour guide Walid was very knowledgeable would definitely recommend if you are interested in this history.

Xavier was a great tour guide, so friendly and knowledgable. Would recommend this tour to anyone, you can learn so much. Even if you’re only in Berlin for a few days, this is a must! Thank you Xavier!

This was a really interesting and informative tour! Xavier was amazing and gave a very educational tour from start to finish! He was always happy to answer any questions that the group had. Overall an extremely interesting tour and friendly tour guide!

Such a great experience and our guide Gregor was very friendly. He provided such a personal experience making us think about different perspectives of the memorial site. Highly recommend if visiting Berlin.

Visited with my 23 year old daughter and wife. Both apprehensive because would rather be shopping instead. They were bowled over by the experience. Real view of atrocities perpetrated by man not so long ago. Learnings for the future. Sad thing is there are similar concentration camps in China where muslim uighers are interned and the world watches!

Nickolai was the best tour guide I’ve had to date! His tour was filled with the general history and also individual stories that helped you really understand what it would have been like to be there. He also gave the perfect recommendation for a sports bar and ensured everyone knew where to get off the return train and what connections to make.
Tour wise I would recommend taking food/drink and be warned there is not much chance to sit down!
Incredible day, thank you for sharing the knowledge.

I booked this tour through viator (a trip advisor company) who sublet to Berlin walks.com.

You meet at 1000 outside a train station, it takes about an hour to get to the concentration camp itself.

Our guide, Nickoli (i hope I spelt it correctly) was very knowledgeable, you could tell he knew his information and was always to take questions or have some debate.

The day we went it was very busy due to school trips but it didn't impact us a great deal.

You must take your own food and water with you as there isn't chance to stop to get some..the tour is continuing throughout the day and there is no "lunch rest" as such.

The tour itself was very interesting! I would really recommend this tour, just to see what happened and original buildings remain is both pivotal to remembrance and education.

I would say though, that if you have any issues with walking and standing up all day do not do this tour.

Unfortunately we had a really nice lady who was struggling with her knee, we slowed down for her but eventually it was too much and she had to go sit and wait for us.

Otherwise it is long days returning around 1630. I would make sure you check the weather forecast as you are outside all day.

Highly recommend this tour!!!
