Tour Guide Martin was a local who seemed to know everyone. He gave us a behind the scenes look. We missed out on some of the inside exhibits due to social distancing requirements.
Maria our guide was very good, knowledgeable, but I wanted to see more of the exhibits to understand the history more. We look through the windows because there was not enough time.
Amazing experience, very sad but so important to learn about what happened and remember the victims. Martin our tour guide was so friendly and knowledgeable, very happy to answer all questions :)
The tour guide was extremely kind, helpful, and insightful. Super engaging and interesting tour - highly recommend.
Nickolai was our tour guide and he was great. Love everything about his attitude and commentary. Everything was perfect :)
I went on a tour yesterday to Sachsenhausen and it was such an insightful experience. My groups guide was fantastic, thank you Chloe!
Excellent. Jon our tour guide was so knowledgeable and charismatic. We learn so much. Would highly recommend.
I went on the Sachsenhausen tour a few weeks ago and loved it. Our guide, Nikolai, was one of the best I have ever had on tour!
Our tour guide was called John. He was excellent! This tour is very informative and well planned from start to end.
Despite of the weather we loved the tour. Wahid, our guide is very kind, helpfull and is very enthusiastic. We want to recommend this tour to everyone.

11/10 - Couldn’t recommend it enough, if you are in Berlin this is a must do! Our tour guide Jamie (Irish) was brilliant, made the excursion that bit better as he is suited to this tour with his knowledge of the topic. Also listen to the advice and bring a packed lunch as it’s a long day.

Everyone will benefit from visiting a Concentration camp, particularly this one which helps you understand how they evolved to the final solution. Our guide Chloe could not have been more helpful and thought provoking.

We took the tour with our guide, Ariel. The tour itself was very memorable, and Ariel was amazing at answering our questions as well as giving us a clear picture of what life at the camp was like. A truly unforgettable experience, showing the very worst of humanity. A definite if you are in Berlin and have a spare day to do something.
Mike was an excellent and knowledgeable guide for this tour. It is a MUST do when travelling to Berlin.
Sebastian was wonderful. I learned more in those 6 hours than I did seeing any museum by myself. Highly recommended!

This experience is a must if you visit Berlin! Our tour guide Chloe was extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the content. She did a wonderful job of really contextualizing the experience for everyone.
Well worth going, so interesting, a must when coming to Berlin. Our guide was really good explaining everything in detail.😊
Visited this site today with Yan. We found him to be great. His knowledge was exceptional and he was a friendly fellow. This tour was very educational and would thoroughly recommend it.

We definitely had quite an emotional experience visiting the concentration camp! It was very somber to be reminded of the horrific history in Germany in the past, however, we are glad that the concentration camp is still here to make sure history does not repeat itself in the future! Thanks Nicholas, for a very thorough journey to the past!
...Vivien

Thank you to Mike, our guide, who ensured we all walked away with a better understanding and appreciation of what occurred in this location. He was knowledgeable, the tour was very informative, friendly and above all ensured that this sensitive subject was discussed with dignity and respect for all those who lost their lives during this period in history.
Fantastic tour. Chloe was an amazing tour guide. She made it very interesting and easy to follow. Would definitely recommend and great value.
What a tour . Our guide Chole had exceptional knowledge of the camp and I really enjoyed it . She was a brillient tour guide !

It was interesting and sobering to visit this site and to learn the details of life in this concentration camp and what happened there. After this visit I have definitely come away with more knowledge on this topic.

Brian was amazing! How he can remember so many facts and statistics I’ll never know! Very informative and sobering experience, would definitely recommend. The tour is a lot of standing/walking so bear that in mind.
Just phenomenal. Brian Bell’s commentary was unbiased and unfiltered. Great to get a true sense of the historical context as we perceive it today. Truly enjoyable. Thank you Brian.

What a fantastic day and tour. Julian was excellent from start to finish and his knowledge on everything from Berlin, Germany, ww 1 and 2, the cold War, politics, and obviously concentration camps was impeccable. Not a question asked that couldn't be answered. A very sombre place that gives you perspective. You can really grasp the suffering that went on here in these times. Also showing the hope that can rise up from the darkest of times and places. Highly recommended while in the city

Our guide Julian made an excellent job telling the historical background and explaining everything we needed to know. Walking around this place without a guide would not have been close to what we experienced. A bit cold and long day however, and pretty crowded in the exhibition rooms but would recommend everyone to go.
Our tour guide Nickolai was amazing and so knowledgeable. Really interesting experience and would definitely recommend this tour!
Nickolai is pure class, would highly recommend! Tour group was easy to find and we were expertly guided from start to finish!
Our tour guide was Nickolai, The trip was very informative, and was very easy to get to. The walk there is pretty lengthy (25mins) but other than that a great trip!

Chloe was all around great!!!
From helping us buy our day pass train ticket, customizing the tour to fit in as much as possible (as there are lots of other tour groups there), knowledgeable & passionate about the history, and helping us with directions on how to get back to our individual chosen final destinations after the tour...all while keeping track of 30 people the entire time!
Julian was a very informative guide, who took us with great sensitivity, on a journey through a difficult period in history. It’s a very worthwhile experience and one we can highly recommend.
Many thanks to John who was professional and sensitive to the subject. He had a lot of knowledge about the camp and ww2 in general. We’d highly recommend this tour and John.

I had an incredibly moving experience during this tour. Our guide was well educated and gave us many (horrifying) details of the concentration camp. I learned a lot! Would recommend if you're passing through Berlin!

Our guide Phil was very knowledgeable and did a great job of storytelling as we moved through the concentration camp and bore witness to the atrocities that took place there and what remained. We were also able to ask many questions throughout the tour about how the history related to events in more modern times and I appreciated that Phil also discussed the more recent use of the camp by during Berlin’s communist period. It was a very holistic and well thought program.

December was very cold here, but I appreciated that it made me realize how much more the camp victims suffered in the bitter Berlin winter without proper attire. (Note to other, pack warm gloves, scarves and warm boots if you visit in December).

Our tour guide (John) was fantastic, his knowledge of the camp was excellent and no question was left unanswered. He was very polite and courteous and made sure we all reached our required destination. As a fellow Irish person I would highly recommend him.

Anne. (Limerick)

Our tour guide John ( Irish) was EXCELLENT ! He was polite, attentive and very knowledgeable.Studying German history at uni and living here for almost ten years he has a wealth of knowledge. I would highly recommend this tour . Thank you John you’re employers are lucky to have such a wonderful employee ! Harry and Diane
Sebastian was an amazing tour guide! Definitely recommend this tour! It is a lot of walking but worth it!

Chloe provided us with an amazing tour that gave us a true insight into what happened in the war and the events that took place in Sachsenhausen. She is highly knowledgeable with a great attitude and friendly approach!

Highly recommend!

Our tour guide Campbell had loads of knowledge, and made the trip very interresting.
I will reccomend this trip.

This tour was very thought provoking it was a very solemn experience.
Chloe was an excellent guide who was very knowledgeable she was also very smart as she took us in the opposite direction to the other tour operators so we had no waiting. She was very helpful as well. Would recommend this tour

Jamie was our guide for the Sachsenhausen concentration trip. He did a great job explaining the history, the current situation and alternative theories and stories. He also patiently answered all our questions.
Jamie is also a super friendly person. Enjoyed the trip, highly recommend.

The tour was amazing. The amount Of information given by the tour guide was incredíble.

Martim, our guide, is an excelent professional and a really nice guy. He knew everything about the camp’s history and was always ready to answer any question.

The tour is really interesting and I think everybody shold do that.

Marcelo Lessa

This is a long and hard day, but one to do. Easy to reach from central Berlin. The walk from the station was about 15 mins, then the whole day is walking and reading. Take some food and Fri k, limited available at the camp.

This was a very informative tour and a must to anyone trying to get an understanding of this dark place in history. Our tour guide Chris Canada taught us so much and is an extremely knowledgable historian who treated this horrendous subject with sensitivity.
A very interesting part of Berlin. We recomand to go to this tour to learn a bit about Berlin history. Leard a lot from our guide Gabriela.

Sebastian, our tour guide made this trip. He was very knowledgable and informative in how he guided us through the trip. His talk about the history leading up to the Nazi regime was full of passion.
We would maybe have liked a little more time to explore some of the sections of the camp.
Would highly recommend this.

There is so much information to take in that I think a tour guide is the best way to see Sachsenhausen and have the elements explained within their contexts.

Our tour guide Sebastian was fantastic. Extremely passionate, animated, respectful and knowledgeable about the subject and period (his 15 minute summary of a 60 year period before the Second World War was very impressive!) and I liked the way he strove to explain the aspects of the camp within their historical context. He was a credit to himself, Insider Tour, and the memorial.

As difficult and horrifying as this is to try and understand, it is well worth it.

Travel to and from the memorial was straightforward and the guide actively sought to help people find their way to their desired destination after the tour.
Nickolai was an amazing host so attentive. Hard subject to discuss but he did an amazing job. I had to count my blessings after seeing what those poor souls endured. A must see for all in this area.
Our guide from Colombia was wise beyond his years and handled this challenging tour so sensitively and passionately.

Martin was an amazing tour guide, easy to find meeting point and travels with you for the tour and guides you around the camp explaining everything, very informative and educational, we had a great tour experience
A fantastically enlightening tour with a highly knowledgable tour guide with the informative and friendly Martin

Our tour guide Josh was exceptional, his knowledge on both the camp and this period in history was excellent. He started the tour by giving a background to World War 2 which then set the context for the visit to Sachsenhausen, the camp was sobering, Josh added lots of context which you wouldn't get without a guide. If you are only going to do 1 tour I would definitely recommend this one, it will leave you thinking about the world we live in today.
Walid our tour guide was extremely knowledgeable about the history of Sachsenhausen and conveyed the information in an engaging and compelling way. We would definitely recommend this tour.

Walid the tour guide was great and had brilliant knowledge of the history of the camp and gave great insights into the social impact of the Nazi reign of terror . Also very informative regarding east and West Berlin and the Cold War

Wickedly funny dry humour by Walid made the trip. Be prepared for lots of walking - there is no other option to get from the train station at oranienberg to sachsenhausen. Plenty of stops along the way where walid titilated us with factoids and history in his own particular manner. Walid was very helpful and really open to questions. Informative and gave a context to the story of saxhsenhausen. No fun tonne had in the story but still had a Great time hearing it from Walid making it real for us. Wicked trip. Defo reccommend if you got a day to spend on this trip. Good mix of peeps on our trip too. USA, Spain, English, Belgian, Irish, Australian. Also helped us buy train tickets at the station which was also very helpful. ❤️

Our guide Mike was absolutely superb - can it recommend highly enough. He knew so much and was able to present it in manageable chunks so it didn’t become too overwhelming. He took time to make sure every single person was engaged and interested. The tour was harrowing (how could it not be?) but it is all extremely well done. The camp has been sensitively restored and it is chilling. With Mikes narrative the horrors were retold and we were reminded what happened in one of our darkest periods of history. Everyone should be made to do this tour and remember what can happen if evil is allowed to flourish.

This is certainly worthwhile visiting if you are in Berlin. There is so much to see and learn about and our tour guide Sarah was really informative. The day was really moving and shocking but it was an experience we will never forget. It is quite a long day and can get very cold so be prepared with comfy footwear and lots of layers.

Mark Curtis was our guide. He was kind, funny, caring and super bright. He really had his facts, history, and had his act together. He kept our group on their toes, on time, and knew more than we had imagined. He made us think about human beings and the phenomenon of the Holocaust . He really cared out making sure that we understood everything. I highly recommend this tour and what it felt like walking from the train to the concentration camp.

This tour was well very good.
Our tour guy Walid was excellent. He was very knowledgeable and informative.
I would recommend this tour to anyone who is interested in the history of Germany
A group of five of us visited the camp which was very thought provoking and really brought alive how horrendous the conditions were at the camp. Sebastian was incredibly informative as host.

Josh was the perfect guide. During the entire 6 hour tour there was not one moment of boredom. He is so engaged with the history of Sachsenhausen and it really came through in his tour. We learnt a great deal during the tour and would thoroughly recommend it to anyone who wants to learn more about Nazi Germany.

Very historical and educational tour. Our guide Mike was very well versed in the history of all the camps, not just this one. He more than met our expectations. He was very reverent of what we were seeing. I wish all our tour guides were at his level of expertise on his subject. We would be pleased to have him as a guide again
Thanks to susan for an amazing tour of the camp. Made a really emotional day interesting and dynamic. Would recommend the tour to all ages. Thank you
Phil was super awesome! He’s a historian and knows his content immensely. ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ ⭐️ He’s also a kind bloke who was quite thoughtful of the people on his tour.

Booked this before we arrived in Berlin, the meeting point and times/info was very clear and easy to understand. We met our tour guide and straight away he made us feel comfortable and knew it was going to be a very good day. We already had a train ticket however you need one covering the ABC routes. This is all easy to do and explained by the guide they make sure you have the right ticket. The tour guide takes the trains with you. Of course there is a lot of walking on the tour so wear comfortable shoes and also take food and drink for the day you will have multiple occasions for it. Definitely worth the money, couldn’t recommend our tour guide John enough, he was great! It an eye opening experience which is definitely worth doing to understand more about the German history. We left at 10am and returned to station at 4pm.

Certainly a sobering place to visit. Well worth visiting on the guided tour. Very informative about such an awful time in history. After meeting at the Brandenburg gate, it’s almost an hour on the train to Sachsenhausen, certainly worth the travelling though.
Very moving memorial tour with such a fantastic guide (New Zealand Mike), who was extremely passionate about the history behind it all.

Guide was very knowledgeable and easily heard / understood. Walking was fair amount for the trip. Travel time was long! Very sad and tragic history. Guide was very articulate and provided additional insights not attainable in books or research, some insights word of mouth. Thorough and very educational.

I had never been in a concentration camp before, and although many of the buildings here have been demolished, the feeling when visiting stays very dark. Because the camp was used for 2 causes, it has a very big history. This history however, is somewhat unclear in the audio tour, as it quickly jumps from the history regarding it being a Russian camp, and it being a German camp, which is sometimes a bit confusing.

My wife and I did the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp tour with Phil from Insider Tour Berlin as our guide. What a great tour. Highly recommend it. Try to get Phil as your guide. He is so knowledgeable about the history of the camp and shares all his knowledge to make the tour a ‘must do’. Easy meeting place. Phil will also answer any other questions you may have about Berlin. Highly recommend this tour. An unforgettable experience

We did the tour with Gaby. She was extremely knowledgeable about the site and very helpful with all of our questions. At the end she even took the time to address us individually to make sure we knew where to get off the train for our next activity of the day. Would recommend it for anyone!!

The rainy weather added a gloomy element to this heavy tour. Our guide Nickolai was great. He was very knowledgeable and personable. We had a big group but Nickolai was able to effectively manage us and keep us all engaged. He certainly went above and beyond in his role.
The hours just flew by.
Our tour guide John from Ireland was fantastic. This tour is a must see whilst in Berlin. Also did the Berlin walking tour which we would recommend.
A great tour and guide Simon. A very good, knowledgeable, informative tour. Tour guide friendly and helpful delivering a difficult and sensitive topic

Our tour guide Maria is very knowledgeable and showed us everything worth seeing and knowing. Time control was amazing cause I was originally planning to stay longer if there’s anything too crowded or not able to see with others on the tour, but turned out I don’t needed to. Highly recommend to join this tour to understand more about this camp.

Nickolai the tour guide was very knowledgable and informative. He relayed the information with confidence and expertise. Answered questions fully, even unexpected ones. Pace was good and we saw a lot in the amount of time we were there. Excellent value for money, if you’re visiting Berlin make sure you do this tour. Danke Mark and Donna
Martin was engaging, knowledgeable, personable and treated a sensitive topic with such professionalism. I wish all tour guides were like Martin!

We knew this would be hard. To be among the evil that perpetrated the mass genocide in Europe during WWII. But needed in this time of rising populism and declining community and empathy for our fellow human. Our guide was educated with a Masters in History and extremely thorough when it came to detailing exactly what each prisoner experienced on a daily basis. If you are in the area, you must go. Take your kids....show them what will happen if we allow these populist governments to have absolute power.

We enjoyed our time with Jamie(Jim) a soft spoken Irish gentleman. He explained many sensitive things with tact and knowledge.
He made certain we were well informed as to the agenda and technical details of the day.
The tour itself was very interesting. Not too much time to spend at each exhibit, which would have required more time/a longer day.
Bring sufficient drinks/ snacks/lunch for the day. Wear comfortable footwear as it is a lot of walking, including the 20 min + walk from/to the train station in Oranjieburg to the camp itself.
In all we would recommend this tour.

We had Maria as our tour guide , she has a sense of humor and was very informative and helpful despite not being born in Germany , learned a lot abt Berlin and the camp
Highly recommended

Visiting the camp and what they have put together to educate people on what took place is worth doing. This I would give a five star, as the German people have worked to preserve what was left.

I was a bit disappointed with the tour guide, a lovely man but not a local or German, and his knowledge of war history was amazing but when we arrived at the camp he spent over 1.5 hours talking to us, then let us go into the first section for Jewish people and said we could have 15 minutes inside, it took 5 minutes to get in and there was so much, it was such a shame to rush through it. I would have preferred to spend the time inside seeing this memorial than sitting outside in the cold wind for over an hour. This was the pattern for the day.

I would have liked to had more time to look and read what was in each of the sections.

Worth going to the camp so we never forget these people and what they suffered is unimaginable.

Despite being a tragic event in human history, the use of concentration camps is central to our understanding of the Nazi ideology that rose to power in 1930s Germany and Sachsenhausen certainly didn’t disappoint!

Our guide, Taylor was extremely knowledgeable, effortlessly listing off facts and dates. He gave us detailed information on the background of how the Nazi party came to power before any camps came into construction which was useful. The tour of the camp itself was just as enriching, though the pictures of the prisoners (the Jews in particular) and the rooms more or less kept in their original states were disturbing to say the least.

The weather was miserable: you could say it accurately set the mood and as a result, we were always trying to get to the next building for shelter. However, the tour was fascinating nonetheless.

Having a guided tour, especially in a place of such historical significance, is so important in putting facts and figures into perspective. As Taylor said, humans need to learn from their mistakes in order to prevent history from repeating itself.

Great tour from start to finish. Sebastian knows his history and explained it all so well. Lots of walking on this tour but loved that as got to see parts of berlin that didnt expect to see. Highly recommend this tour.
Chloe was a great tour guide. Very knowledgable, friendly and paced the day very well. Difficult topic, but important tour to go on.
Our tour was led by Ronan who was very knowledgeable and sensitive. The trip was very thought provoking and hard, but I would recommend to anyone visiting Berlin to take the time to visit.
Phil was a great guide - very knowledgeable, respectful and interesting to listen to. A very worth while experience.

Very well organised - wonderful guide.

There is a lot of walking and isolated from shops for most part - wear good walking shoes.

Take water bottle and snack food.

Toilets are on site.

Some of the stories and scenes are very confronting.

Not suitable for young children.

Real modern history about the camp, how the local township saw the camp, the Russian occupation of the camp after the war and East Germany propaganda of the camp.

We took this trip with Ciaran and he was very good at helping people get the right train tickets and making sure everyone was in the right place!
At Sachsenhausen, he was very informative and always gave people the chance to ask questions. He also allowed the group to have time alone in each of the points of interest.
It was a very hot day and he took this into consideration when telling us information as he always looked for the shade so no-one was uncomfortable.
It's a good trip to do but it involves a lot of walking so be prepared!
We took food & drink as there is no real time to stop for lunch

Our guide Josh had plenty of information to share. He was very informative and kept our group together easily (about 21 people total).

Also be prepared and bring snacks/lunch and water (there are no water fountains). We walked approx 8.5-9km according to my Fitbit so good shoes are recommended!

Had a great time and glad we booked, thank you :)

Today we had John J. as our tour guide on the concentration camp tour. We are a family of 6 and we enjoyed the tour guide. We met at a location right outside the train station and took a van to the site. There was around 15 people in our group. John always waited for everyone to get there before speaking. He gave us great knowledge on the camp as well as info on some of the prisoners. This was a very informative tour. Would highly recommend!
Thanks to Jakub our tour guide, we could not recommend this tour more. Very informative yet engaging despite the long day. A must visit to this extremely important part of Berlin history.
Great tour, very informative. Pace was a bit fast and didn’t allow for pics and just absorbing all the fascinating displays and exhibits.
Very good guide who explained clearly throughout and gave us full history before the tour. Well done Phil
Gabbi was excellent tour guide. Very knowledgable. Wear comfortable walking shoes and take something to eat and drink. Excellent tour.

From start to finish our tour guide Phil provided us with a wealth of information and made the tour so interesting. He even recommended future places to visit which we included in our trip. Thank you Phil

What a memorable day we spent with our guide Nickolai at the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp, he was so clear and informative as he took us through the timeline of the camp's shocking history. He also took the time to make sure that everyone got their train connections back to their hotels which was much appreciated.
Highly recommend
Incredible tour. Very happy that we did the tour and that my son could also have the experience. The guide was extremely knowledgeable and competent.

I booked a last minute tour, literally 45 minutes before it starts, and couldn't be more delighted. I had a very informative and well described tour with Nickolai. His knowledge and professionalism is impressive! Well recommended!

After taking the free Berlin tour yesterday, we signed up for the Sachsenhausen tour with Chris (the Canadian). It is an intense, thought-provoking and educational day but well worth the time. Chris offered great insight and answered all and any questions. If you have the chance to visit Sachsenhausen, I would highly recommend it.
The tour we went on was incredibly informative and managed to be quite interesting without keeping the mood sombre for the entire day, and I'd certainly recommend others to visit.

An excellent tour, fast paced yet required due to the sites needed to cover.
Ronan was a great tour guide, with his vast knowledge of the site and his background in archeology kept us well informed whilst keeping a respectful and sensitive feel to the nature of the topics. He kept the group together and navigated the transport part well, getting us a bus to the camp.
Make sure you get an ABC day ticket, lunch and a bottle of water before you set out, and stretch/sit when you can, it is a day tour.
Highly recommended.

The scale of the camp is much more manageable than Auschwitz, Birkenau... However, being so close to Berlin, this working camp that later became a extermination camp. Our guide Chloe was knowledgable and acknowledged that the behaviour of the perpetrators was open to interpretation.

Overall worth it.

The tour makes one consider many issues; the rise in power of the Nazi party to the 3rd Reich and the systematic way in which they treated those who did not deem worthy. The camp has been preserved and/or restored appropriately to provide context without being too macabre. Our tour guide, Pip provided good historical context and was respectful of the relevance of the site

Excellent trip that catered for a variety of levels of knowledge and age ranges of people. The guide was extremely well informed and helpful, taking time to provide more clarity, extra information and even restaurant recommendations on the way back.

Did the tour to the camp with my thirteen year old yesterday. We had a sobering but good experience. Our tour guide Sebastian was brilliant, loads of stories of little know history really brought it the tour to life. He even had some nice words for my moaning teenager!!
I would highly recommend this tour, it is a lot of walking but definitely worth it

Loved this tour! Super well organized and they make it safe and convenient. Josh was super considerate and knowledgeable! Appreciate the information considering the sensitivity of the place. Thank you Josh!! Highly recommended!!
Coming back to learn more with the Third Reich tour.

My family and I had the pleasure of touring the camp with John today. John was friendly and super informative. He handled every question with ease and displayed an impressive depth of knowledge. I felt that I learned a 100 times more than I would have if we had done a self guided tour. John really knew his stuff and was a great guide from the moment the tour started. To grasp the significance of this important site and the history of the era - do this tour!

Did this tour the day we were due to leave Berlin - got back to hackescher market for 4 (our departure point that morning at 10)
Our guide Sebastian was absolutely excellent. Obviously it’s not a tour you necessarily “enjoy”, but it is a very worthwhile “experience”

Our guide was Josh. He was brilliant. His knowledge of the subject was very impressive. Yes, you could say it was his job but you could tell he had a genuine passion for the subject. The tour was informative and interesting while maintaining the dignity and compassion it needed. Well worth a visit as it brings home the atrocity of the concentration camps.

Our guide was Sebastian, who told the stories of the German culture around World War I and II as well as dived into the personal stories of some of the heroes and victims who perished at Sachsenhausen concentration camp. The whole thing was done in a very respectful and tasteful manner. Sebastian made an effort to make every single person on the trip seen and welcome in between bringing history to life.

HOWEVER, the reason we do not give 5 star to this trip was the lack of transparency of Insider Tours. A large number of the group was not aware that additional train tickets had to be bought. This is an easy fix on the shopping page we hope they will correct shortly. Therefore, be aware that extra costs for transport must be factored in.

We had John as our guide. He essentially made this trip amazing! Having studied German history at uni, John had a wealth of knowledge to share during our visit to the camp. John was super helpful (even buying train tickets for late comers so they could purchase food and drink for the trip) and went out of his way to make sure we all enjoyed the experience and went home knowing a few bits of knowledge that we wouldn’t have obtained from the mainstream literature. The camp itself is a surreal experience; well worth a visit even if you’re not that interested in history. In terms of practicalities, the walking was reasonable (though we ended up taking the bus from the train station to the camp, losing about 2 km round trip in walking). You also need to take sufficient water and food for a 6 hour trip.

Really interesting tour, there were a lot of surprising facts about this place that we had no idea about even with prior knowledge of WW2. Big thank you to Walid for an informative, engaging and occasionally humorous insight into this place! May he always find a free train seat.

Many thanks to an exceptionally knowledgable guide walid .
He made the tour. from the beginning of meeting me , his communication skills encouraged questions and made me feel welcomed. He looked out for everyone on the tour to even guiding us onto the right trains at the end. Preparing us before the tour re food and appropriate rail tickets . Many thanks

We learned so much during this tour. Our tour guide Maria was fantastic. There's a huge educational benefit to going on a tour. Who would have ever thought that Hugo Boss manufactured the SS officers uniforms??

We went on the Insider tour to Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp with Maria. She was an excellent guide who is very knowledgeable and informative. She has a lovely manner and presents the information very sensitively. This was truly a very memorable experience. We would highly recommend this tour.

We visited on a 38 degree C day...the hottest our guide Pip had ever seen. It seemed fitting to be uncomfortable while we were there. It is not a happy place of course but important to see. Pip was outstanding. Very knowledgeable about the camp’s history and also went above and beyond finding us shade and places to sit down while she spoke. Directions to get to the meeting place were good. There were only quick breaks during the tour so have a good breakfast before you set out. A thoughtful day.

This tour was so much more than I even thought it would be. Phil (our tour guide)knows his subject and answered all our questions. Provided other tour suggestions as well as books to delve more into specific topics. Be prepared to walk (did over 7 miles) but nothing compared to the shoe testers (you'll learn on the tour).
I had a great time on this tour! My tour guide, Maria, was extremely knowledgable about the history of this camp and was also very time efficient. Definitely recommend!!

Phil was a fantastic guide. He was so knowledgeable and did not mince words. He even gave us lovely suggestions of places to visit once we returned to the city. The tour was highly emotional and even overwhelming at times. But it was more than worth it.

Our guide, Sebastien was able to distill important areas to see to make the most of our visit. He was also very knowledgeable about the rise and fall of the Weimer Republic and the economic conditions that led to Hitler's emergence. Top rating and a must see to remind ourselves that it can happen again if we forget.

My travel partner and I went on the tour with Chloe and she was an incredible tour guide. She made sure to answer all of our questions in depth.
Something very important to me was the ensuring of respectfulness white visiting the camp, including making sure we avoided standing on indistinct grave sites, which not all tour guides we saw pointed out.
There was a lot of sobering information to take in and I definitely wouldn’t recommend for children, but I’m so glad that we included activities like this rather than a trip solely for leisure.
A must-see at least once in visits to Berlin. Thank you Chloe!

An emotional walk through this memorial with our very knowledgable tour guide Nadav. Thankful he is willing to share his personal story with us. There were only bathroom/water breaks so bring snacks since it is a 6 hour tour.

Definitely a must see/do for anyone that goes to Berlin. Our tour guides name was Sebastian, and he was fantastic. He was so knowledgeable with all the historic information and context, and didn’t just say the facts as it is, but genuinely wants to provide you a deep understanding of what occurred.

You could also throw any questions at him, and he’ll most likely know the answer! Very engaging presenter, and also ensured group safety in terms of everyone getting to the correct places, head counting etc.

Makes you want to find out more about history!

Our tour guide, Phil, was so knowledgeable and friendly and respectful. This is by far the best tour I’ve ever had for anything hands down. Not only was our guide amazing, but we missed the original meeting point and by calling insider tours and talking to Mike we were able to easily meet with our group. Thanks so much Phil, Mike, and Insider Tours!

Phil was fantastic! The trip was exactly as described- a guided trip through the camp that picked up and dropped off at the meeting places. In addition, Phil took time to direct every individual party to their correct train at the end of the trip. Phil was clearly extremely knowledgeable about the subject matter and was approachable for questions. Phil stopped frequently to explain everything behind and in front of us- mindful of finding shade and thinking of each patron. He was an engaging speaker and kept a brisk pace without rushing anyone. Bring your own water, snacks, and bus ticket to zone C and be prepared for an informative and transformative tour. If I could have Phil direct more tours in my future I would!!! Also, I wrote down many things e.g. books, movies, etc. while walking- I suggest you listen to Phil’s suggestions if you are a WWII buff and if you miss something make and a note and he will write it down for you on the train back. Also- Phil kept his cool even after herding the most stray guests back, even when language barriers or other cultural aspects came into play, etc.- I would suggest him on an international project.

We had a wonderful tour guide Campbell, who was extremely knowledgeable and able to answer any questions anyone had. We decided to take another tour with Campbell the next day knowing he was going to be the guide. Although an extremely
Sad sight, this tour was very interesting.
We enjoyed our tour very much. Lots of walking as the train did not take us all of the way. It was worth the walking!

Nickolai's deep historical knowledge and seriousness of purpose made this tour powerfully moving for us. It brought home the horror of Naziism that mere reading can only approximate. He was an excellent tour guide and we feel fortunate to have had him as our leader on this excursion. --Greg and Suzanne E.

Pip was our guide for the day who was just brilliant.
The tour started by us getting the train followed by a short walk to the camp itself. Pip was really knowledgeable about the history of the camp and was showed real empathy and sensitivity. I knew nothing about the history of these camps and how they came about (my husband who i was with is into all that) but I left the camp feeling quite emotional and found myself reading up more about them when I got back to my hotel. Highly recommend this tour.

We were so fortunate to have Brian Bell as our tour guide. We went in May while the weather was perfect for this longish tour. I could not say enough good things about our guide, he was very personable, informed, unbiased, patient and very well spoken. Great that he was tall too, hahaha, we could easily follow him. Although the content of this tour is understandably disturbing, Brian had a lovely way of helping us through the backstory of how this part of history came about. SO well worth the time.
Maria was a great knowledgeable guide. Joining instructions were very easy. Would book with her again.

Must see whilst in Berlin. Our tour guide was Maria. She was very informative, and very knowledgeable about Sachsenhausen. She was great help getting to and from the concentration camp and then helped people navigate how to get back to their hotels on the way back. Sachsenhausen is definitely a must see on your trip. Make sure to bring lunch as there isn’t anywhere to get food while you’re there.
We had a great day out with insider tours. Phil our tour guide from Dublin was great, really friendly and really knowledgeable. Great day out would recommend

We did the tour with Brian who was the perfect guide for this tour.
Day was organised well and Brian's knowledge made the whole day faultless and very informative
Would recommend this tour for anyone visiting Berlin.

Organization of the whole tour was excellent. We purchased our tickets for the camp at Berlin Central Station. We were told exactly what type of ticket we would need to get to the Concentration Camp, what train to take to get to the meeting place for the tour and recommended to bring a sandwich and drink.

When we arrived at the meeting spot, we were greeted by Phil. Phil did an incredible job communicating to ensure the whole group was aware of the stop we would take to get to the concentration camp.

Once we arrived at Oranienburg, we all walked together to Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp. Along the way, we were able to ask questions & were provided information surrounding the area.

Phil walked us around the camp and throughly explained everything. Out of all the different tours we reviewed, we were extremely satisfied we booked this tour.

We spent the day out at the concentration camp, we opted for the audio guide which was €3 each.

The audio guide was really detailed and took us around the former concentration camp. There are loads of exhibitions and different buildings to see so would suggest spending a day here.

The camp is a short walk from Oranienburg railway station and it is free to visit.

It truly is an eye opener about the horrific crimes committed here.
Campbell took us for a tour and he was incredible! All the information was clear and he gave attention to everyone inside and outside of the camp.

This tour is a great option if you don’t want to have to navigate your own way to the camp, and you want some good content.- but being part of a tour didn’t mean that rune was wasted. The group was larger but still workable.
Most importantly, Julian our guide was very knowledgeable and personable, which made a real difference. My only hesitation was that the time to see some things was too brief- but I still felt as though I had a sufficiently comprehensive experience.

The tour was brilliant and 100% was down to Whalid our guide. He’s so good others stopped to listen to his commentary.

Somber experience and cruelty beyond measure. But the story told is one you would never forget. You have no idea how cruel humans can be and to this day nothing learnt ..... nothing gained. Do the trip with a guide you will get so much more out of it.

Taylor provided an insight to the evolving national mentality during this period. The tour moves moderately fast. If you want to stop and take photos of things of interest you will be way behind. This tour is designed to give an in depth picture with a fast pace to stay within the time allotted.

Campbell was an amazing tour guide.
Studies history, politics and international studies so most if not all the questions that were thrown at him he had answers for. He went through the thought process, reasoning and ideas for every decision each of the governments who were in-charge of the camps at the time made and not just recounting what was done to the prisoners at the camp.

And like any tour you are moved around quite quickly but after this tour you are given the choice to either go back on the train with the tour guide or stay and wonder around the camp a bit longer.

For me, having a tour guide was great for this place because there was a lot to read and go through but at least with the tour guide we felt we got the most important information and history. Instead of walking around reading random bits of information or having to hold up a little speaker to your ear for however long you're there for.

We met our guide Phil at the train station and we proceeded by train to Sachsenhausen with the tour group which took about an hour.

The fee included entrance into the camp and tour guide. A day ticket for zones ABC is also required.

Phil was very knowledgable in the history of the concentration camp and had answers to everyone's questions as he lead the group through the key aspects of the camp and its history. Excellent tour guide.

Very insightful tour overall if somewhat disturbing at times. Expect to do plenty of walking. Would definitely recommend to those interested in gaining insights into German history.

The knowledge and understanding that Phil brought on the subject made us understand the history of the World War II like never before. We go back now with a better understand which was very vague in our minds and something that is not written with such compassion. Must do visit with PHIL.

We would not have undertaken the journey out the camp alone and thank Insider Tours for making our trip possible. Phil was a helpful and informative guide and we learned about camp life and some of the truly horrific things that happened there. It was interesting to hear and see the differences between this camp and Auschwitz.

Phil was a great guide, very knowledgeable but didn't waffle. Very well looked after on the journies to and from.
The Sacsenhausen site was much more moving than I had expected, as it was both a forced labour concentration camp but then also became an extermination camp. It was a cold day, but this added to the understanding of what the inmates went through. We have to move on, but must never forget. Thanks Phil for helping a 68 year old understand what my parents were fighting for.

I had thought of doing this trip on my own, but so glad that I didn't. Our guide was Taylor and he was so knowledgeable, but it wasn't just spouting off facts and figures, he made it so interesting and gave you just enough information for you to take it all in without being overwhelming. He also came into his own on the return journey, as there had been a fire down the line and all trains had been cancelled until we didn't know when. If it had been me, I would have panicked, but he dealt with it professionally and managed to shepherd us all onto a bus that had been laid on for waiting passengers, that we would probably been unaware of. Thank you Taylor for making it such a memorable and extremely interesting day.
Sebastian was engaging and very knowledgeable of the historical context. He is an excellent and resourceful guide. He made the experience that much interesting. Thank you!
We were very fortunate to have Phil as our guide on this tour. He was informative, knowledgeable and passionate about the subject and I thought showed the right level of sensitivity throughout.

Jaime was our guide and made us feel well taken care of from the moment we left. He even got our group on the "sneaky bus" that saved us some walking. It was eye opening with so much horror to take in but so important to remember. My 14 year old got a memorable history lesson that she will always remember. Well worth it, A ++

I cant find the link jusg to review the camp on its own. But 150% its worth a visit, its a must see when you visit Berlin - we booked a tour however oncr we turned up and waited over an hour then we got told it was cancelled dus to minimun numbers not met... so annoying as we would of left way befofe that .
Any how you dont need a guide, ae used google and got the underground plus a train and then a bus, it was quite an adventrue actually, theres madonalds and bakerys all over on your way!
we paid for thd ear phone sets however there is soo much information & numbers yoy dont even need them. But yes most worth a visit, you can take your own food and drinks or there are cafes, sites & toilets all around.... good prices and clean

so imprezssed by all of the originals and storys, really and over whelming placd to see.

Had an amazing time on this tour. The tour is 6 hours including a short train ride. There is plenty of walking but it’s definitely worth it. Our friendly warm and welcoming tour guide Walid made the trip extra special. Walid’s vast knowledge of the site and history made it an invaluable experience. Highly recommended if you have a day to check it out.

This is worth the time and effort if you have any desire to broaden your understanding of the holocaust. The remaining buildings are basic, it's not a horror show, but our guide made it come alive (Martin Lange). A true revelation of the depths of darkness that can take place.

We spent the day with our tour guide, Walid. He is very knowledgeable and definitely made the tour more interesting. He also showed obvious concern to the group. We were a rather large group so we had to split up our group into 3. Walid was our guide. From start to finish, he made sure the group was together and safe. He even made sure everyone knew what train track each was taking to bring them to where each needed to go after the trip.
The whole tour will definitely last at least 6 hours. It took us about 45 minutes to reach Oranienbutg where the camp is. Then we walked about 2.5 miles to get to the camp itself. Trusty footwear is a must! Also, make sure you have food and drink with you as there will be no time to stop for lunch. You eat as you go. The camp itself is a sobering place to be. You would not want to miss the facts about the camp and the inmates so lean in. It is a sure way to fire up your interest in Germany History if you have not already. The youngest person in our group is 10 years old. It could be a long day for them so consider this if you have younger member of the family you consider bringing along. Also, be prepared for the weather. It was sunny and a bit warm when we did it. Shade may not always be available as there could be many other groups touring that day. Glad I brought a hoodie. Someone in our group had an umbrella.
Overall, this is an excellent tour. Great tour guide, too! Highly recommend it.

Campbell was brilliant from start to finish. Was there early ,had every one primed with their train tickets and got us on the road in time. He had a great knowledge and a super delivery. Very patient and answered all questions posed. Made sure we all got back to our starting destination. Well worth a tour
Phil made the visit there very interesting and was very knowledgeable about the camp and the people within. Well worth the trip out.

Your guide Maria was excellent,informative and compassionate as this must be a difficult tour to guide,transportation instructions were easy to follow all in all well done.James Mitchell & Mitchell Hawes

I had a few days on my own in Berlin and decided this visit was essential given the history.
I booked with Insider Tour Berlin and met at a very easy to find location.
Our tour guide was John (from Ireland) and extremely knowledgeable, friendly and helpful (thanks John)

The group was 18 in size and never had any issues hearing all the details of the visit.

I would recommend you take snacks and water as this wont be available once you arrive at the camp. The tour took approx 6hrs (from meeting to arriving back)

Would highly recommend this tour.

Met our guide Ronan for the trip to Sachsenhausen concentration camp. The trip took about 6hrs including the train journey to and from the camp.
Ronan was excellent full of information and happy to answer any questions it was quite a large group but it was always easy to hear him.
I would definitely recommend this trip, there is quite a bit of walking involved but a lady in our group was in a wheelchair and managed it with her friend.
Also recommend taking a snack and drink with you.

We could not have wished for a better guide. Mike arrived as a late addition as the group was so big. He was incredibly knowledgeable but also incredibly passionate about the history of the camp and the context in which it operated in the different eras. He was also very helpful and made sure everyone was OK throughout the whole six hours of the trip. A kiwi who knew far more about European history than we did. Excellent!

This is an important place to visit if you get a chance. Our guide Nikolai was outstanding he was a great story teller, he was informative and showed the utmost respect for a camp with such significance. Although it was a rainy and windy day Nikolai tried to make sure we were indoors as much as possible whilst not sacrificing the importance of getting to walk the camp. Would highly recommend and not too far to travel from the city. Book with insider tours if you do

Defo a must do in Berlin! £15pp for a full day from 10am-4.30pm! Taylor was our guide, he was so informative and friendly. He was opened to questions around the tour and at the end he made sure to get everyone on the correct train they needed to get back to their hotel or recommended places of interest near by if that’s what you wanted. Very informative tour and we hope you get Taylor as your guide!! :-)

The tour commenced at Berlin Zoo Station which is easy to get to. Everything was well organised and the joining instructions sent out upon booking were detailed enough to ensure we were where we needed to be with what we needed.
The first thing to know about this tour is that there is limited food and drink available, if any, so ideally make use of one of the many sandwich shops around the station or the Spa shop and take some supplies as you can expect to do quite a bit of walking.
You will travel on the train to the town/city of Sachsenhausen were there is then a short walk (10/15 mins) to the actual memorial, the walk itself is interesting as you approach up a little street of houses that were build for SS Officers and learn about the site. Although not all of the original camp is still there, what is left is still fairly vast and very well preserved to give a fascinating, and sad, insight of what this place was about.
We were so pleased we had joined a tour group for this as our guide, Brian Bell, captivated us with interesting history and facts throughout the entire journey there and back, as well as the tour, and there was no question left unanswered.
Be prepared to do a quite a bit of walking, but I would recommend going with a tour as you will learn so much more and this really was quite an insightful day. Allow a good 6 hours in your schedule to and from Berlin.

Our guide Pip was an extremely knowledgeable historian with regard to Berlin. The site had changed immensely since it was an active concentration camp, with very few buildings remaining. Pips commentary brought the site to life and allowed a vision of what life was like for the orisioners in the concentration camp. Thank you Pip for making the tour so interesting. Definately recommend insider tours, especially if you are English

Chloe was our tour guide on a phenomenal, eye-opening tour of Sachsenhausen. In addition to sharing the brutal realities of life as a prisoner in a concentration camp, Chloe also shared the history of the SS and the quick rise of Hitler to power that led to such mass murders. I highly recommend a tour of Sachsenhausen with Chloe. Her passion for sharing history was appreciable. Not only will you learn newly discovered details from research of Holocaust Museums, but you will also be asked how much did folks outside the concentration camp walls know? Critical thinking required in times such as now.

One of Berlin's saddest stories from WWII, it's not a glamours/fun tour like most others, but full of informative facts about Concentration Camp. Our tour guide Phil is great, he provided a good summary of the camp and hit some notable exhibits during 3-hour walking around. Entire tour was about 6 hours, but transportation took about half of the time. There weren't specific time scheduled for lunch, so we ate our snacks during the walking which wasn't fun in winter when cold wind blew on my face but was OK. Phil also provided additional helpful suggestions for us after the tour, very nice guy!

A concentration camp tour may not sound like a "must do" trip but I would definitely recommend this activity.

It was very informative and our guide, Sebastian, gave us an educating and engaging tour. He presented what is a very emotive topic in a very level and non-judgemental way which is essential for this type of activity.

Meet up was easy outside the U-Bahn station.

If you're staying in Berlin and already have a zone ABC travel pass then that will cover the train trip of around 40 mins each direction from Berlin centre. If not the tickets are really cheap at €3.50 each way anyway (02/2019)

It's about 4 hours of walking at the site with a 15 min walk each way from the station so wear your comfortable walking shoes. It's a very open site so bear in mind for the weather.

There are shops in Oranienburg to buy food/drink but better to come prepared... no shop at the camp.

Definitely recommended and goes well with other activities around Berlin that inform about the Third Reich/WW2/Holocaust.

I have been on a couple of similar tours of other sites that were arranged through TripAdvisor and would definitely say that all have been very well presented and well organised.
We took school children on a trip. This is haunting but worth a visit. How this was allowed to happen doesn’t bare thinking about but the memorial is worth a visit.

Firstly the experience is not to be missed as we are duty bound to reflect on how in reasonably recent history these unsavoury acts could be carried out on fellow human beings.
As you may have read in other reviews, you can easily get to Oranienburg using the S-bann easily and take a 15/20min walk to the Museum. Audio is available to hire on site however I don’t think you will beat the knowledge imparted by our guide.
It is a whole day trip from Berlin but would strongly recommend booking with Insider Tours if their guides are like Maria our guide for the day. Very knowledgable without lecturing and able to inform clearly on a sensitive topic.
Take drinks and food as facilities are not available.
Having walked about the camp today in sub-zero temperatures helped imagine how intolerable it was for those unfortunate enough to have found themselves in the Camp.
‘Lest we forget’

A friend and I did this trip together with not a lot of background on the camp beforehand, which was definitely not the case when we left. We had Campbell as our guide and he was amazing! The weather was cold and rainy but he did his best to keep us dry and warm when navigating the camp and was so knowledgeable. His approachable nature also made it easy to ask questions and he even made the effort to make other recommendations for us for our remaining time in Berlin. The camp itself was very sobering and well worth the visit to learn from the past.

This tour is well worth the money, you have an escort there (which is needed, we would have got lost) and then Phil who is clearly passionate about the subject walks through giving information when needed.
Wrap up warm if you’re going in winter, we froze

This camp is a little different from the big name ones you hear about in US history class. It was one of the first ones built and kind of a prototype to see if these would work to hold prisoners and such. Very educating but also still solemn to hear of what all happened. I did learn some new aspects of camp life and after liberation life there.
Pip was our guide. Very knowledgeable and would answer our questions of different but related topics. She walks at a good pace so have your walking shoes on. It's a 20 min walk from the train station alone, and then you walk around the camp. Be prepared.
I honestly prefer these type of tours than going and listening to the recorded tapes as you walk around. Different little facts are shared and you have someone that you can ask questions who is trained and studied in this particular area.

This trip was so knowledgeable and informative. Cold, sun, rain or shine definitely go on it and for English speakers 150% request and make sure you get Phil. His historical prowess and the way he articulates and illustrates all relevant tidbits relating to Sachsenhausen is nothing short of masterful. He’s a true historian. This is the greatest tour I’ve ever been on and I’d 100% recommend it.

Pip was a wonderful guide for this very interesting tour of Sachsenhausen concentration camp. As a guide she was engaging and informative throughout and very knowledgeable about the camp and its history. The tour was thorough and she allowed us plenty of time at each stop to take in the exhibits and read the plethora of information on offer. I'd highly recommend taking a tour with her if you are interested in history.
not much left of the original structures... lots of stories and pictures... our guide was great at explaining the horrors of what went on here.

First our tour guide Maria was amazing. She had so much information about not only sachsenhausen but the surrounding area and struggles of the people involved. Very informative trip and I would recommend to anyone interested in the history or ww2. Again a big thankyou to Maria who made the tour special

Went on this tour today with an amazing and knowledgable tour guide Campbell. He was very helpful on meeting at the East side meeting point informing us that there was nowhere to get any food or drinks when at the camp and told us where we could purchase some before leaving the train station. He was also extremely helpful with booking the train tickets. All through the tour he would give us useful and interesting information that we would have missed had we gone alone to the camp. We were able to walk the route the prisoners walked to get to the camp from the train station which was interesting in itself. The camp was extremely interesting to tour. Was very thought provoking looking at the history of the camp along with the conditions the prisoners were kept. The harrowing stories of the daily lives of inmates made the camp that much more real even though lots of it has been destroyed.
This concentration camp is a must see when in Berlin. Would recommend to anyone. But remember to wear comfortable, appropriate clothing (was very cold today, could have used more layers) and there is a lot of walking involved.

Our guide was Campbell from Australia. What a knowledgeable person! As other reviewers have commented be prepared for walking; wear comfortable shoes and make sure you pack a light lunch and a drink. This is not a fun excursion but one for you to take time to consider a dark and terrible point in the history of humanity. You will also meet people from all over the world who like you felt it important to come to such a place.

Most importantly, our guide, Phil (from Ireland) was magnificent. He is a graduate of Trinity College in Dublin and is passionate about history. Anyone taking this tour should request Phil. How anyone could know more than Phil about this camp and the politics that led up to it is beyond me. People should also be advised that there is a considerable amount of walking on this tour. After meeting at the train station at the Zoological Garden in Berlin, the train trip took about 45 minutes. Then there was about a half hour brisk walk to get from the train station in Oranienberg to the concentration camp. Phil’s lectures started while we were waiting for the two trains we had to take. In the winter, dress warmly.

This is not an easy place to visit, in any sense of the word. The journey, by public transport, takes about an hour and there is a fair amount of walking. But it is something everyone should do, to appreciate the true horror of the Nazi concentration camps.
Sachsenhausen is a bleak place, colourless and eerie. The buildings that remain have been arranged to show the visitor the history and operations of the camp. There is also information on the post-war East German use of the camp and their re-writing of history.
To stand in the very place where prisoners were worked to death or murdered was shocking and horrifying. But I'm glad we did it.
Our tour guide, Brian Bell, was fantastic. He had a wealth of knowledge and presented many different aspects of the death/work camps in an enlightening and impartial way. He really opened my eyes to many previously unknown (to me) aspects of 20th century European history.

I found this to be a very surreal place, very little wildlife about also. On the day we visited, the weather was -1 and we Scots, could even feel the coldness though our clothes. How the prisoners survived this cold with the thin clothing they were given on their arrival and the food they were given to eat is unbelievable.
The tour of the whole camp was excellent due to our guide Ronnan took us through each step the process of the prisoners would have been made to take. My only fault was not enough time to read all the information that was on show though out the camp.

Marie showed us around and although it was a large group of 16 it was easy to hear all the details. She took us to the most significant parts as the site is too big to cover all in one day. She was very knowledgeable and keen to answer all questions.

It takes great skill to summarise such complex history, and deliver such an emotionally loaded part of history with passion and neutrality...Phil at Insider Tour did exactly that on a recent trip to the Sachsenhausen Camp. It was a sobering, sombre experience yet he guided us with respect and warmth. I am so happy I went and I highly recommend Phil and Insider Tour.

It sounds strange to say 'I enjoyed a trip to a concentration camp' but I did, it was very informative, mainly due to the guide, Campbell, an Aussie guy who's studied history and who was extremely well informed. He was very articulate and addressed the controversial issues well.

To see where these attrocious acts occurred was very sobering, we set off from the train station in Berlin and travelled by train to the concentration camp, following the route the victims took. Once there you get a real sense of how awful it was. This is the only camp I've been too, I think it will be the last.

It was a full day almost, make sure you take food and drink as there's no where to buy anything there, you'll also need a train ticket which you buy on the train station platform. Get an ABC standard return (e7,70), this will last you all day.

Definitely worth the time and effort to travel out there, if you can get on Campbell's tour he's brilliant.

AMAZING! AMAZING! Our group of 6 toured with Mike and we all enjoyed every single moment. He had great stories to tell and get recommendations on what to do next in Berlin. Mike made this difficult tour an eye opening experience. He was VERY informative, patient, passionate and helpful. He answered all of our questions and always had a story to tell. I Highly recommend taking the tour with Mike. He even guided us home and to other fun places after our tour. THANK YOU MIKE!

This is a 5-h trip to Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp (north of Berlin). I always wanted to visit it. However, having Mike (our guide) along with us made this trip even better. He gave us details on the history of the camp. He was definitely one of the best guides I was ever with. If you are in Berlin or plan on visiting this town, this trip is a must.

We had a nice tour with our guide Phil who shared a lot of history and details so we could understand better what was happening on that territory during ww2. Overall a great experience and an excellent guide.

We had the pleasure of attending the Sachsenhausen tour with Taylor as our tour guide and it was a fantastic tour. I cannot speak highly enough of Taylor as a guide; he did a truly fantastic job painting a clear picture of what the camp was like and walking you through the progression of it over the years without losing you among excess information. He was also able to distill a lot of information into just a few hours without losing any of the importance of the site. It was a really powerful tour and one we won't soon forget and it was in large part due to the excellent job of Taylor. I would highly recommend him to anyone wanting to visit the camp.

If you visit Berlin because of the city's history, then a visit here is almost compulsory. It is a 40 minute train ride from Berlin city centre, then a short bus trip. Very easy to organise yourself on public transport. The entry is free, but I thoroughly recommend an audio guide if you do not have a tour guide to talk you through your visit. You can just walk the site and read the exhibits, but for 3 Euros, the audioguide gives an amazing insight to make sure you miss nothing.

Words cannot begin to do justice to the feelings you encounter when visiting here. I recommend a minimum of four hours so you get the full experience. Even then you probably only read a small percentage of the exhibits available. You will leave with your emotions pulling in all directions, but with an over-riding feeling of shame that human beings behave in such appalling ways.

This is a great tour, very informative, thanks to Julian's awesome knowledge of the subject matter. The trip is also very well organized. I highly recommend it. Thank you Julian for a very successful tour. From Elpida, New Jersey

We met our guide Ronan at the station as arranged, he was very good at warning us about validating tickets, how many stops the journey would be etc. The journey involves 2 train and a bus journey there and back .
At the camp there are no original barracks however there is a reconstruction . There are watchtowers ,prison block ,doctors block , execution trench and foundations of extermination room and furnaces .
Having a guide who is obviously really interested in history meant he was able to concisely tell us the facts about the camp .
There is a Jewish museum and another in the kitchen block but unfortunately there was not enough time to pay these justice . The trip did feel a little rushed and we seemed to be walking at a fast pace to keep up with Ronan .
It would have been helpful to know to bring a packed lunch as there is no cafes and no lunch break , so one needs to eat some snacks whilst walking about .
Feel excellent for families with older children .

The excursion to Sachsenhausen was very interesting. I have learned quite a lot of new things about the person 1930-1950. Still it is difficult to understand to what we can do to each other, based on differences like ethnicity, political beliefs, etc. I did not know half of the cruelties which were performed there. Also it was interesting to learn how the camp functioned as example for other camps and that the bureau which made the regulations for all camps was situated there. Sachsenhausen therefor is historically more important than I had known.

Our guide, Chloe, had a very informative and effective way to show us all around. As soon as the group was complete at the train station in Berlin, she started sharing so even the waiting time was used to gain knowledge.

Chloe demonstrated to have a big personal interest in the topic and was not just “playing a record”. Most questions of the groups could be answered and others triggered her to look into later. I appreciated that a lot. Not bluffing, but being honest and open to learn.

Note that of the 6 hours quite some time is used for going back and forth to the camp, over 2 hours easily. We saw a lot of groups walking from the train to the camp, which takes 20 minutes each. Our guide knew the bus schedule and we were lucky to catch a bus both ways. This helped us to stay at the camp about 30 minutes longer.

We had a Fantastic guided walking tour to a very interesting and sober facility. The experience begins at the railway station and then You travel with a guide to Sachsenhausen. Please make sure you take food and drink with you as it’s a long day without refreshments.

This was excellent tour and Maria did a wonderful job presenting a terrible time in German history and how Germany is proactively dealing with so it doesn't happen again. There is a lot of walking so be aware of this and wear comfortable shoes and bring a backpack with lunch and drinks.

Our guide was Julian, he not only gave us a comprehensive tour of the concentration camp, but gave a very good explanation of the reasons behind it.
This is not a tour for children, but should be compulsory for all adults.
There were twenty or so on our tour, but Julian still managed to make himself understood clearly.

Taylor took us to Sachenhausen concentration camp and from start to finish, he looked after us all making sure we were all ok. He was very friendly and approachable and extremely knowledgeable in the history of the camp and relevant events. Well worth booking the tour if you visit Berlin.

My husband and I were glad that we booked a tour with a guide. It is such a hard subject to discuss, and we really appreciated our tour guide Phil's insights and knowledge. He did a great job explaining what everything was, and also explaining why the camp can still be visited today. I would recommend this tour to anyone thinking about visiting the camp.

Our tour guide (12 Sept 2018) was Phil, a very pleasant history graduate from Ireland - extremely knowledgeable and full of interesting and relevant facts about the World Wars, the rise of the Nazi party and Adolf Hitler. His insight proved to be invaluable during the tour of the Camp as it provided great context for everything we saw that day. The camp itself is an eye opener, but Phil's commentary really helped us understand the ghastly events that took place there.

The pick up point for this tour was from Hackescher Markt station, a very convenient stop in central Berlin. From here we took a couple of trains to reach Oranienburg, a town about 40 mins from Berlin. From there it was a 10 min walk to the Camp.

The camp has bathroom facilities and a small shop, but nowhere to get snacks etc - so you'll need to bring your own. Our tour took around 4 hours, although you could easily spend twice that long if you wanted to really get into the detail of all the exhibits and buildings. Take comfortable footwear. It was also quite windy when we went, so dress suitably, especially from Sept onwards.

All in all - one of the highlights of our visit to Berlin. Great historical value, great perspective from Phil.

Booked this through Viator. It was a long day but worth it. Very detailed info provided by our tour guide Phil who is obviously passionate about history. Depressing to see the actual site where the terror happened but we knew what we signed up for.

Taylor provided an extremely informative narrative as we explored what is obviously a confronting experience. There is too much information on display to take it all in if you guide yourself, so I would highly recommend joining an Insider Tour. The cost is in my opinion low for the service provided.
Taylor ensured that everyone knew exactly what was happening at all times and that we all got on the correct trains to reach our final destinations. This extra attention to detail was appreciated by all.

Our guide, Phil, was excellent. He provided much background information which really helped us understand how the Nazi's gained power and the appalling treatment handed out to inmates at the camp. Although many of the barracks had been taken down you could still sense how the camp was run, although the full horror of what took place there could never be imagined. The walk from the railway station (re-tracing the steps taken by inmates) taxed the leg muscles and after a further 4 hours walking around the camp is certainly not for those less able. For the return we caught the bus back which dropped us right outside the railway station.

This tour is worth every penny you will spend on it. I signed up to take the tour on August 30th with a friend of mine. As directed, I purchased the ABC zone ticket and met at the designated spot. After a short wait, the remainder of our group arrived and we embarked on the trip. At the train station, our guide asked if there was anyone interested in splitting off and joining another group, apparently there was another tour that needed a few more people. It was the same company so we made the change. I'm not sure how the other tour guide would have been, but I can't imagine her being any better than the guide we had. "Yan" was absolutely amazing. He is by far the best tour guide that I have ever had. After the 45 minute or so trip, we arrived to begin our walk to the camp. The weather was grey and rainy which only added to the ambiance and the overall experience. I don't think that I have ever had a guide so passionate about telling not only the story, but helping you to understand and imagine what it might have been like. We stopped various times during the walk for Yan to provide us with more information, he would randomly shout a few German words like "nine" "nine" as examples of what the camp workers might have endured, this only added to the overall experience. We walked throughout the camp but didn't really have to take it all in and read all the displays. It was a long tour so I understand the need to keep moving. What I learned about this tour is that, at least for this one, is that it is a walking tour. This is NOT a tour for slow walkers or for those that have difficulty walking or standing for long periods of time. This tour lasted approximately 6 hours, 4-5 of which was standing or walking. There really isn't anywhere to sit to rest, so be prepared for this. It is also important to wear good walking shoes and not flip flops or other type sandals. This isn't your typical tourist attraction where there is a gift shop at the end (fortunately) so bring water and a snack.

There was so much information, and very interesting - thank you to the walk guide Walid, who made sure all the group stayed together and made sure everyone was able to travel back to where ever needed after, and of course gave a very informative tour!

Phil, our tour guide is very knowledgeable and the tour was accompanied by lots of interesting facts and stories. I would definitely recommend it!

Even though it takes almost a whole day, it didn’t feel long because there was a lot to see and take in. Make sure you bring food and water, and put your walking shoes on!

We had a great tour with Phil. The camp is large and there is so much material. Phil provided the perfect overview, shared stories, kept us on schedule snd andwered any questions the group threw at him. Would suggest tour and especially Phil to any friends.

While in Berlin we felt that we owed it to ourselves to experience this bit of history, despite how upsetting it can be. Alicia was our tour guide who met us at the station, and was incredibly helpful in getting us to the camp. Once we were there, Alicia was incredible in giving information in a way that while not being too heavy, still affected you in a deep way. It’s such a tough subject but she made it incredibly interesting, as well as pointing out parts of the history of the memorial that I wouldn’t have thought of without her there.
