I cannot recommend Alicia and her tour enough, you learn and feel the gravity of the location so much more with the tour. Do yourselves a favour and do this tour, because all it takes for evil to triumph is for good men to do nothing. This location is as relevant to today as it was in the past.

Walid took us on a wonderful and insightful tour of Sachsenhausen. He was extremely knowledgeable and well educated on the camp. He made sure we were made aware of particular exhibits at the camp before we entered the exhibitions. This was a great help as there was so much to take in. It was so refreshing to see someone really enjoy their job and honestly care about everyone’s experiences. Thank you. a day full of history and a great experience. A must do in Berlin.

A comprehensive and informative tour. Our guide Taylor was fantastic- very knowledgeable and passionate about making sure that guests understood the significance and history of the concentration camp.
A huge thank you to our guide, Ronin, who was so knowledgeable about this subject and made the experience very real. A great day to reflect on our past!

Start with the tour guide- Chloe. She was the best tour guide I've had for any purpose. She brought everything full circle, knew her stuff, and answered the questions that popped up in my mind before I ever needed to ask them. She adapted the tour to avoid the crowds (necessary in a location like this), helped keep us out of the heat, and fielded every question that we threw her way.

This tour was a roughly 35-minute train ride from Berlin and didn't take up too much of the afternoon. Wear comfortable shoes!

The tour takes you through the outer gates where most of the Third Reich's concentration camps were coordinated and planned. From that small museum, you move to the outer houses used by the SS and their families. Then, the tour of the main camp - which is as good as everyone else indicates.

Trust the other reviews. This is an educational and powerful trip. It's one place where I do not recommend going it along - get a tour group. Most of the buildings or exhibits here will not be self-explanatory, and you will want the human details to make it all hit home.

This was a great tour. Our guide was Nikolai who had a great knowledge of the history involved. The tour was well organised. It’s useful to read all the joining instructions, and make sure you have the correct train ticket before you meet the group.
Sachsenhausen is a very overwhelming and somber experience. But well worth the visit.
This tour involved a lot of walking, you need to have a reasonable level of fitness to make the walk from the station to the memorial, and then around the memorial and back again. It was pretty tiring in the heat, and the facilities at the memorial are basic. There is no place to buy water or food there, so go prepared. Overall a very long day, but a moving experience. Highly recommend.

My other half and I did this tour with our excellent guide Julian from Canada. Straight from the beginning he was giving us the history of the camp and how it came about. It was 32 degrees and he managed to find shade whenever we stopped. The tour starts and ends in the same place and our guide gave us any information we needed with regards to travel and best places to visit. Overall very pleased and would recommend. Bring extra water if you don't want to drink from a tap. They don't sell any at the concentration camp.
Really good for history buffs. Tour guides were really helpful and friendly. Make sure to bring food and drink with you

We recently travelled through Europe with a group of 9 high school students. On July 15, 2018, as part of our study in Berlin, we took this walking tour through Insider Tours. Our guide, Pip, was phenomenal at relaying the history of the camp and WWII in Nazi Germany in a very succinct manner. She was very knowledgeable, and the students were very engaged in her presentation of the history and explanation of what went on at this camp. We were part of a large group, but Pip handled it very well. Thanks Pip!
Excellent tour, and the tour guise was even better. Walid was so nice, a great conversationalist, and extremely knowledgeable.

Phil was a fantastic guide for our tour of Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp. He was very knowledgeable and answered everyone's questions. It was a very hot day and he was considerate of everyone's needs. He guided everyone on to the train and provided great context to everything that we saw.

20th July me and my partner went on a guided tour done by TAYLOR.
The tour itself was such a humbling experience.
The tour managed to touch on the history of the camp and also the many years that camps were ran for.
It’s full of mixed emotions but I’m glad I had the opportunity to take the time out to learn about human history.
Taylor was our Tour guide and he did a brilliant job of getting us all there and back safely as well as providing us with a well detailed and efficient tour. We definitely got our money’s worth and learned a lot.

My son and I were on this tour on July 16th and we are glad that we took a day away from the city to learn more about this camp and lots more of the history of the area. While it was a hot day and there was a good deal of walking it was a very informative tour and our guide was very good and respectful of the subject matter.

My son and I booked this tour with Insider tours. Our tour guide was Mike who was fantastic. Incredibly informative about all aspects of sachenhausen, brilliant historian. Lots of walking, it was haunting to to be there. An absolute must see.

Went on this tour with Walid. He was excellent, very knowledgeable and informative, and helped all of us make sure we had good plans for the rest of the day and our trip. The trip itself is a lot of walking no matter which tour company you use to get there - you take the train, followed by a 15-20 minute walk to the site, followed by a walk around the site.

We were a group of 4 who joined the Sachsenhausen concentration tour on an incredibly hot day. John, our host was both professional and informative.
It was clear that he had a passion for his tour, and, despite the difficult topic, he made the tour a very enjoyable one.
Even when we were confronted by the most terrible of stories of the poor inmates in the concentration camp, John was able to ensure that the group got great value from the long tour.
The weather was challenging as it was extremely hot, however, John made sure that we had suitable rest breaks.
We thoroughly recommend this tour and would like to thank John for his hosting skills.
Waleeeed is the best! He made the trip VERY special. His sensitivity and knowledge was incredible - and he managed to bring the group together superbly. Bravo! I cannot recommend it enough.

We had only three days for our first ever trip to Berlin along with our 19 year-old grandson and wanted to see the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp Memorial. It is important that people visit this site as witnesses to man's inhumanity to man. You cannot possibly take all of this in on your own. Insider Tours was highly recommended to us and did not disappoint. Our English-speaking guide, Chloe, was very well informed and made this trip very worthwhile and a great value. We are in our 70s and were fine with the amount of walking that was involved.

Bring bottled water, snacks and your camera. Also rain gear if the weather calls for it.

Thank you Chloe for an outstanding tour.

The visit to the concentration camp was the single most impactful activity I did during my 6 days in Berlin. I did this tour with Brian Bell, and he was an excellent tour guide. His explanations wear clear, informative, and insightful. He was very friendly and made the trip enjoyable even though the subject matter is so heavy.

The camp was presented in such a way that a person could visualize just how it was during the time that it was operational. The buildings that are standing show the conditions that people were subjected to during their time in the camp. The history of the camp is documented within the main building. Our guide was Michael from InsiderTour. His knowledge of the camp and its history was amazing. Michael conducted the tour very professionally yet never rushed while inside the camp. I would recommend this tour to anyone who has an interest in 20th century history of Germany.

This is the second time I have done a tour of the Sachenhausen Concentration Camp and first time doing it with this company. Taylor was extremely informative but also kept the tour light enough so we did not leave feeling depressed. He covers all of the facts and shares remarkable stories and goes much more in depth than other tours I have done in the past. Highly recommend this tour for anyone interested in learning the hard truth of Concentration Camps.

We took the tour of Sachsenhausen concentration camp with Insider Tour and found the experience truly fascinating and eye-opening. Our guide was a man named Nickolai who did a tremendous job of taking us through the chilling history of this place. It makes a real difference when the guide is evidently passionate about the subject as well as knowledgeable; this is what really stood out about Nickolai. He was personable, intelligent, funny, kind and interesting.

In addition to this, he went above and beyond to speak to everybody and ensure that every person got to and from the camp safe, seeing to it that everybody knew where they were going and directing us to where we needed to be.

I would highly recommend choosing Insider Tour for this trip if you are visiting Berlin. It is an experience I will never forget.

We were very fortunate to join The Insider Tour with guide Maria for this fascinating tour. She was extremely knowledgeable about the Sachsenhausen and offered many details and anecdotes to paint the painful picture of this part of world history. She also made sure everyone was accounted for and knew where they were going upon our return to Berlin.

We met our guide Jamie outside the Zoologischer Garten station. There is a choice of 2 departure points so wherever you stay you shouldn't be to far from one of them. You need to buy an ABC ticket to travel to the camp. Your guide travels with you so you don't have to worry about losing your way. There is about a 15/20 min walk to & from the camp however there is a bus that you can catch if you're not up to the walk I leaned so much from our guide Jamie. He gave us so much information & delivered it with respect & clear empathy for the victims. I really don't think that we would have learned a fraction of what we did if we chosen to go by ourselves..

Me and a friend went along to do this tour from Berlin. The tour guide called JJ was very friendly and very knowledgeable he helped us with everything including getting back to the hostal after the tour had finished. The tour was very good and very interesting I would definitely recommend if your in Berlin

My dad and I visited Berlin to soak up the history of WW2 and the Sachsenhausen tour was the highlight of our trip. We were most impressed with Chloe our tour guide who held a fountain of knowledge on the subject area. Our tour experience was made all the more enjoyable by her friendly and relaxed approach. Thank you Chloe!!

My boyfriend and I just returned from a 6 hour tour with Mike around Sachenhausen. From the minute we arrived at the meeting point Mike was a wealth of information. He was extremely enthusiastic and passionate and had us hanging on to his every word. There is no way you could visit without a tour guide like Mike and get a true sense of the horrors that took place at this concentration camp and others. Not only was Mike a fantastic tour guide but on the journey back he also took the time to answer any general questions regarding Berlin itself. Every opportunity to share knowledge he took, thank you Mike!!!! Couldn’t recommend enough
it was a great tour with a great tour guide please do this tour to realy feel what happened in the concentration camps

My sister and I spent the day with our very informative guide Sadie. She is a history major from Britain and focused on the effects of these camps on Germany today. She is articulate and brings a very personal perspective (lives there with her family now) to a very difficult topic and to a country that is still struggling with the stigma of the events that happened during the war. Sadie helped us with our tickets and sorted us out on the way back so no one would be lost.

Really good tour, packed with information. Just a shame that it's not possible to get round everything in detail! Will need another trip back. Phil was great, really personable, very funny and incredibly knowledgeable; any questions that were asked he answered without hesitation. Learnt a LOT from him that we wouldn't have learnt if we went on our own. Phil was very helpful in terms if making sure we all knew how to get back to our each varying locations after the tour. Big shout out to Phil for supplying my ginger boyfriend with suncream and finding shade all day to prevent him from burning and us all melting. Would very much recommend!

What a day! if you're reading this just book it now!!! the whole thing was smooth from start to finish. Phil had so much knowledge of this tour. I like to think of myself as a bit of a history nut but Phil knew everything you needed to know, I learnt things I had no idea about. It is a long day but worth it. so make sure you take some lunch and plenty of water as it was 27 degrees when we went.

Had Josh as a tour guide. Very informative and sensitive to the topic. Ensured that we all got on and off the train at the right stops. It is a lot of walking. Gave us time to reflect on the history of the camp. We learned a lot. Would recommend this tour.

I am 19 years old & I was studying abroad in Berlin when my father came to visit me. He told me about how someone on his incoming flight told him that a tour of the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp was a must-see. I'll admit, I'm not the biggest fan of history - yet, this was the best history lesson I've ever received. Our tour guide, Chloe, was not only VERY knowledgeable and educated on the subject, but she was also very friendly and open to any questions you may have had. I knew little to nothing about World War II, the Nazis, etc. prior to this tour; however, Chloe taught my father and me all that there was to know in approximately 6 hours. I would recommend this tour to any person of any age, race, or nationality. It was definitely an eye-opener and it's not for the faint heart, but it is important for us to learn this history so we never repeat the same mistakes.

Thanks again Chloe. :)

Our tour was lead by Phil who is from Ireland with background in HISTORY. I see that Phil really knows his stuff and still maintains his enthusiasm considering he had visited the concentration camp for more than 200 times (well, my 11 yo son asked). Coming to such site filled with sad stories, I feel that Phil did a great job in talking about the purposes of the camp establishment in a way that I think appropriate to give the timelines and background of events without overwhelming our emotions.
After the tour on the train ride back to Berlin, Phil gave directions and saw us getting off at the right stop. Berlin is such a city that took center place in many events of modern history in last century. I will recommend Insidertour to anyone who visits Berlin for the first time.

Sobering tour of the grounds of the concentration camp. Rowan, the tour guide, was a wealth of knowledge and was able to answer all questions. This a bucket list item if you are on vacation in Berlin. Thoroughly worth the small tour fee!

This was by far one of the best tours I have been on in relation to the camps, their purpose and how the camps fitted into the fabric of everyday life. Chloe was a extremely passionate team leader. Highly recommended.

You need to take your own water and a snack, and an ABC zone public transport return or day ticket for this guided walk - 6 hours including 2 hours travel time. Very good value Insider Tour, especially if you book online, although you can just turn up at the meeting point if you wish. Our guide, Jamie Sewell, was excellent, giving us information in a clear and incisive manner, helping us to understand what happened here in the terrible period of Germany's history 1933-45, and also afterwards during the Cold War. Both the Nazis and the DDR gave the world a lot of false information about what happened here. Sachsenhausen was the first German concentration camp, and the place where all the horrors were tried and tested first, and other concentration camps were designed. Jamie managed to tell us what happened in quite a lot of detail, bit by bit, in all the different locations, but somehow without overwhelming us; he is a very skilled, understanding and understandable communicator. I will never forget this place.

This was a fascinating day tour. The history of the camp was brought alive by our tour guide Phil. He was extremely knowledgeable and brought the timelines together in an informative and sensitive way. He was able to include and respond to everyone's needs and questions on the tour. Thank you for a fascinating day.

Mike our guide was incredible. Not only did he have an extreme amount of knowledge of the Nazi era of the camp but he shared an experience his wife had of the camp during it's Soviet era. He managed to keep the tone light on the way to and from the camp but kept the tone somber and right for the actual tour. Definitely worth the 5 hours we had. My only criticism would be the lack of a bathroom break; he did pack a whole heap in so I understand but the camp doesn't have many toilets and I had to wait as it was full on the only 15 minute break we had! Highly, highly recommend though!

Our guide, Taylor, was the best. He made the tour one that should not be missed. From the initial meeting to meeting with each guest as we rode the train back to the city to be sure thy all knew how to get to their next destination. Thanks, Taylor--G'day mate!

Our guide, Phil, was SUPER knowledgable. He's an irishman that's been living in Berlin for about 4 years, and I think he studied history in university, which helped the tour! Any questions we had, he had answers- with specific dates. I really, really enjoyed this tour and would 100% recommend it.

We thought that Chris Taylor gave an intimate, heartfelt, personalized tour of Sachsenhausen. We were beyond surprised how he could make a tour of 22 seem so personal. He helped us purchase our train tickets, gave explicit instructions on what he was going to cover and at what time he would meet people who wanted to spend more time in given areas as we made our way through the site. He made a difficult subject matter a pleasure to learn about, he answered all questions wth sensitivity, and moved at a pace that was comfortable for all. I cannot recommend him more highly. He appealed to both my 17 year old daughter and me.

The Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp tour was an engaging, interesting, and emotional tour of the concentration camp. Our tour guide, Walid, was friendly, outgoing and talkative. He is an excellent, knowledgeable, and organized tour guide.
As our tour guide, Walid, treated the tour, my fellow travelers and myself with respect. During the entire tour he was open to questions and input from the tour group. We started our tour at Haseckermarkt then we took the train to the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp. Walid, gave us an overview of the history of the Third Reich and the camp’s function in the National Socialist regime.
One thing to keep in mind is that this requires a lot of walking during the entire tour for entire length of the tour. There is a 20-30 minute walk to the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp from the train station and the camp complex is large and spread out so there is a lot of walking between sections of the camp.
Walid, guided us through each section of the camp. He started with the construction of the camp and its development. He talked about its function in National Socialist centration camp system. The role of the camp in the Holocaust was also discussed. There are thousands of exhibits in Sachsenhausen so we covered each section as much possible. We were also give time to look at individual exhibits on our own.
Walid, displayed an in-depth knowledge of the camp and its history. He also gave us detailed accounts of the treatment and suffering of prisoners in the camp.
This tour is very educational and emotional. I feel that it is one of the most impactful tours I have done in Berlin. To me the tour is worth the time and effort needed to get to the camp. I highly recommend this tour to anyone interested in the subject and for those that want a better understanding of this period of German history, the Holocaust, World War II and the world history as a whole.

Traveler Type - Family of Five (mom, dad, son (18), son (16) and daughter (14).

Overall Feedback - Absolutely worth the 6 hours of time (10am to 4pm). Tour guide (Mike Stack) was a difference maker. History geek? Check - he majored in European history. Bored easily? Check - Mike was informative enough for the geek, but colorful enough to keep everyone interested. On a Time Schedule? Mike kept us right on time...to the minute (no kidding). So you can schedule your late afternoon / evening with no worries.

A Few Specifics - 1) Check-In via the West Berlin option in front of the McDonald's was worry-free. Mike even helped us purchase our train tickets. 2) Two trains and a bus seems like a bad comedy, but Mike did a good job keeping 24 of us straight-away during our transit to the Camp, 3) Bring food / water (we brought protein bars and a few bottle waters) and 4) There is a decent amount of walking. Be prepared with good walking shoes.

What an amazing experience. You learn a lot. TJ

On Monday we went on this amazing tour with Jamie. The organisation of the trip was superb...and so easy! Jamie was attentive to everyone in the party and considerate of everyone's needs. He had a wealth of information to share and was truly passionate about the history of Sachsenhausen; sensitively painting a vivid picture of the truly horrific events, which happened at the camp during the war. Although emotionally disturbing, it was an experience which we would highly recommend. Thank you very much Jamie. From The Preece family, Manchester.

You’ll realise that every human needs to visit places like this once in their lives
Go with a guide, there’s masses of info to read & these passionate guides will help you understand what atrocity occurred where in the camp eg looking at the poles where the SS strung up prisoners until their shoulders dislocated

This occurred in Europe a few years ago, visit it!
Ronan was a fantastic guide - the depth of his knowledge is amazing! He made us feel very at ease with heavy content. The tour itself is quite harrowing but very worthwhile.

Our guide Maria was very attentive and resourceful. Throughout the whole tour she paid attention to the overall atmosphere, she changed the route so that all the tours in the camp wouldn’t get overlapped with each other. The tour was emotional, but it was very much needed.

It was such a wonderful eye-opening experience. Our group guide Alicia was so knowledgeable and gave us incredible information that we wouldn’t have known otherwise. I would recommend to anyone traveling in Berlin. An emotional and incredible experience.
I participated to the camp tour with Chloè. She made the tour emotional and informative. Excellent guide, highly recommended!

Our guide Pippa me us at the station and advised on tickets/trains etc.

It was a sobering experience. Very bleak and thought provoking. The camp has been well preserved and the notices and artefacts very informative and presented in good English. Unfortunately our trip around the camp was subject to tour time restraints - understandable as it was a longish tour from a to b. I would really have liked to stay and read all the info and immerse myself in the 'experience' more - I will at some point make my way back under my own steam.

Pippa was very knowledgeable and presented all the information very concisely. It's not really appropriate to describe it as an 'enjoyable' experience but it's certainly something that I have wanted to do for many years and I am pleased and thankful that I made the trip.

Pippa ended the tour with a very heartfelt and thought provoking short speech.

Thank you Pippa,

Our tour guide Chloe was brilliant. She had a real passion and knowledge of Sachsenhausen that was second to none.

Everything was explained in an easy to understand way so you don’t have to be a major history buff to enjoy this tour. Truly a harrowing place to visit but it is important that we don’t forget the horrors of the past so that they may never be repeated.

Special shout out to Chloe for battling against public transport issues and still getting us to the camp in a timely manner. 10/10 - loved this tour.

It was a pleasure meeting Chloe, our tour guide. From the very start, she was very friendly and as accommodating as possible. She was well versed in the topic. You can tell she took considerable time doing her research. She spoke in laymen’s terms so all could understand. She was open to answer any questions or comments we had which was an added plus. Although (not due to her control) we had quite the adventure getting there, it was well worth it in the end for those that are visiting Berlin. Whether you are a history buff or just looking for something to do, this is a MUST see. The experience was mind-blowing and I will never forget it. “Two thumbs up!”
We had Ronan as our tour guide who was absolutely fantastic. He was so knowledgable and answered all of our questions. We would fully recommend this tour and our guide to others.

Very hard choosing words to describe this tour as it’s very humbling and sad to learn of the facts and events that had happened here. Mike our guide was outstanding from the start with his well timed trains to his compassion in the way he spoke and his knowledge was superb. Least we forget .

The trip was easy and great. The meeting point was not complicated to find and the trip was soft enough for preparing what we were about to see. Pipi (sorry if I am spelling it wrong) was great, with a great humor she made the trip interesting no matter where. Getting there, she gave us the right amount of history and also shared her thoughts with us. Which made us think actively and not only soaking up everything like a sponge. I still thinking about some of her points...

For me it is a MUST DO for all of those who like to get in touch with history and think by themselves and not only about what others say... to have our own experience is essential.

The Insider Tour of Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp with Phil from Dublin was absolutely excellent. He had the right mix of facts and anecdotes. Wrap up very, very warm: it’s all outdoors. I have spoken to so many people about the tour and highly recommend it. You will return to Berlin (30/40 minutes on the train) with a fresh pair of eyes and interesting knowledge about the history, which is simply brutal and terrible. Not exactly a ‘holiday’ activity but so worthwhile and one of the best walking tours I’ve ever done. Phil was very memorable in his speaking and is clearly a born guide who enjoys sharing information and experiences.

The cost was €17 plus a train ticket for the Sachsenhausen tour. I booked in advance online.

Overall, I am very pleased with the service offered by Insider Tours in Berlin. I was particularly impressed with Phil and his style of guiding us around the concentration camp.

Absolutely fantastic insight into the horrors and history of the camp, we visited with our Guide Nickolai who was brilliant, Very knowledgable, full of interesting facts, eager to share his extensive knowledge
and answer any questions that popped up.

Nickolai was also extremely helpful on the journey home, organising us all with the best stops/connections to arrive at our destination.

The camp itself is something of a must, we've been going to Berlin for years and never visited. You have to get a guide, don't make the mistake of visiting yourself, you'll miss absolutely everything, the camps electronic guide seemed ok but this place demands a personal touch.

My husband and I went on the insider tour for Sachsenhausen at the beginning of January. Phil was our tour guide. He was incredible and very knowledgeable. The tour was very emotional, and very tiring. You almost get emotionally exhausted because of the content of the tour. However, we would highly recommend it.

The tour to Sachsenhausen was undertaken by Mike, who was incredibly knowledgable and made sure that everyone had plenty of opportunities to ask questions and enough time to take in the camp. It is an experience of great historical importance and it is not to be missed

The Sachsenhausen Tour was a great insight into WWII Germany as well as into the concentration camp itself. The site is great but be due to be prepared for the elements - there isn't heaps of shelter. Our tour guide Phil was really knowledgeable and made the whole experience enjoyable - from his knowledge of the Holocaust and Nazi Germany through to his recommendations and directions to places to see at the conclusion of our time with him, Phil provided a great experience.
I would definitely recommend this tour

My wife and I both wanted to take the opportunity of a trip to Berlin to visit a concentration camp, all be it that we weren't expecting it to be pleasant. Whilst I understand it is possible to tour the Sachsenhausen Memorial Site by yourself we felt that given the subject a guide would be essential for aiding our understanding. Our tour was lead by Jamie, and we reached the memorial site in approximately 1 hour after meeting the group (this involves two trains and a walk), and in total spent 6 hours with the guide. Whilst it definitely wasn't a pleasant visit, it was informative and the subject matter was treated with all the respect it is due. The tour brings to light the horrors of what took place at concentration camps and helps you to understand it. I would highly recommend using Insider Tours for your visit to ensure it is as good as such a visit can possibly be. The price we paid was very good value (note an online discount is possible if booking direct on the company's own website).

Brain was our tour guide for a day trip to Sachenhausen Concentration camp. While the information was entirely sobering and heartbreaking, Brian did an outstanding job sharing the information with our group. Very Impressed with how smoothly the day was run and how much we learnt. Despite being in a group of 20 or so, Brian made it feel much more personal and was easily available to answer everyone’s questions. Highly recommend.

Jamie, an Archeologist by trade, offered an insightful education into the vicious Nazi war machine. To think any human being is capable of willingly committing such atrocities on another fellow human being is mind numbing, but as we repeatedly experience throughout history, propaganda and social economic conditions can lead to all manner of things. Concentration camps are not the answer. They started under the banner of fencing people in. Sound familiar, maybe a certain politician who thinks about building a wall/fence could if allowed end up fencing people in? Moving, thought provoking. Jamie added to the tour through his historical background. Well worth the cost.

It's difficult to say that this was a great experience, as the subject is not really something you actually can enjoy. However, our guide, Mike, made sure that he gave us as much information as possible and made sure that this was a very interesting and informative day.

He did not stick to some small facts about the camp, but started the day by explaining the most important events between WW1 and WW2 and how Hitler seized power. During the day, we visited the most important parts of the camp and we received an avalanche of information, with facts and stories about how life was at the camp and how the camp was used after WW2 ended. It's nice that he did not only talk about Sachsenhausen and it's role, but also touched other important events during and before the war.

At the end of the day, he was kind enough to give us some extra tips on what we could visit during the remainder of our stay in Berlin.

We would definitely recommend visiting Sachsenhausen with Insider Tour. Also, everything was neatly organised. We had to take 2 trains and a bus, but everything went perfectly fine. When we visit Berlin again in the future, we are definitely going to go on another tour with Insider Tour.

I was quite apprehensive about visiting Sachenhausen Concentration Camp so decided to book a tour and was grateful that I did. Our tour guide Jared not only had a wealth of knowledge about the events that took place at the camp, he also gave a round view of the circumstances leading up to the opening of concentration camps before and during the Nazi regime. I would highly recommend this tour should you wish to gain an understanding into the circumstances leading up to the concentration camp and also to remember the souls lost to the brutal regime of the Nazi and later the Soviet Union occupation of the camp.

We had Phil as our guide for the tour to the camp. He was excellent! His knowledge of German history leading up to the war and beyond was fantastic. Unless you are a history buff with vast knowledge of German history, you will miss a lot without a knowledgeable guide. They really are worth the expense.

We used the same company with Josh as our guide at Potsdam. He was equally good which is why we decided to book again for the tour to Sachsenhausen. Without the guides, you are just looking st "stuff."

The Sachsenhausen Tour guided by Taylor was a fantastic experience. Taylor is very knowledgeable and provided insight into the lives of those who were held and worked at this camp. I would definitely recommend this tour. Thank you Taylor for an exceptional experience.

Our participation in the Sachsenhausen Tour guided by Jared was an unexpected decision that ended up being a major highlight in our five day visit to the wonderful city of Berlin.

Jared is a gifted personality and was a treasure trove of information. His passion for knowledge and ability to communicate effectively was awesome!

My new wife and I walked away from the tour with an appreciation, not only for the victims of Hitler's Third Reich, but also the resiliency of the German people and their commitment to facing the past in an attempt to protect our world from further genocidal atrocities. What a way to spend our honeymoon. Thank you Jared!
Our guide Ciarán was brilliant. Very informative and educational tour- would highly recommend if travelling to Berlin.
A moving and enlightening experience. Our guide Jamie was really knowledgeable. Enjoyable doesn’t feel like the right description but it was definitely worth it
Such a heartbreaking place, but a memorial you must visit. So that history is not repeated. At place where the unthinkable happened.
We were led round by Jamie who was very knowledgeable and also took great care to ensure all the group stayed together including the trip on the public transport to and from Berlin
The information by Paul. Excellent knowledge with compassion in what was a difficult historic memoir for us all.

A very sobering but memorable tour. Our guide Paul was excellent, very knowledgeable, and looked after us well. He gave us a running history of the camp from its inception for a few political detainees, through to its liberation and the final tragic march of the remaining prisoners. The camp itself is very stark and most of it has been razed to the ground, but one can see the layout, the entrance arch, an original bunk house, a cell block, the prison wall, the gun positions, the torture posts, various execution sites, the 'infirmery' and the remains of the killing chambers and cremation ovens. It is all testament to the horrors that went on there. There are a couple of indoor exhibits which are very good but were very crowded when we went, and there wasn't enough time to read all the information.
On the need-to-knows : The trip involves a lot of walking, to and from the station and around the site, and the site itself is large and exposed with very little shelter from the weather, and few facilities.
Overall it is a very interesting insight into life in a concentration camp, and predictably, horrific.

A must do tour if your in Germany. After seeing Holocaust Museum in Washington DC this is a must while in Germany. This is the headquarters for all concentration camps and where everything was tried. It was not originally an extermination camp, but a work camp located in town. The Villas and houses of the SS officers are still lived in today. The main headquarters are the tax offices and the training facilities for SS officers now is for training police. Our tour guide Mike was extremely knowledgeable with all the history. You can not go wrong with Mike leading your tour. Mike is a walking encyclopedia of history. He made the time feel like 5 minutes. Not only did he give us a great tour he left us wanting more even though we were there for several hours. Never once did we feel rushed. Thanks Mike for a wonderful last day in Berlin.
Our guide Joanna gave a informative, respectful history. She made sure we all had the right train ticket and kept the group together. Her knowledge was first class. Highly recommended
Not enough time at all for visit. And on return long wait for return train . Time could well have been used at camp. Not clear why it was not
Joshua our tour guide was extremely knowledgeable and sensitively answered many questions. Would highly recommend!

We were guided by Martin an amazingly informed person who actually came from the area and had many personal stories to share. This is a very difficult but important place to visit. So many groups either by birth, religion, political views, or sexual preference were persecuted here. It is a tortured visit yet a necessary one because authoritarianism seems to b attractive once more. As an American I found this chilling for reasons an American can understand after Jan 6. Sadly we all have our stories and histories that evoke warnings and fear. I highly recommend this tour to all visiting Berlin. It serves as a cautionary warning going forward.
The tour guide was very knowledgeable and kept everyone rite with checking they had the proper train tickets and and breaks

This was a moving and highly informational tour. Cian was our guide and he was outstanding. Not only highly knowledgeable about WWI, WWII, and the camp but also overwhelmingly helpful. 5 stars for Cian.

Took the tour with a guide named Nikolai. Simply the best guide I’ve had anywhere. Yes he knew the history of the camp but he also knew how to personalize the experience of the camp. Everyone should do this tour and if you can get this man (from Chicago originally) as your guide - it was just wow. Changed my life in 3 hours.

Excellent guided tour from Chloe, very informative and Chloe certainly knew her subject. Chloe made sure we all had food and drinks for the day and the correct train tickets and even made sure we were all on the correct trains when going home.
Iguana was fantastic with great knowledge and she looked after us well. The tour gave us a real insite of the life in the camp.

Fascinating and interesting day touring one of the first concentration camps. Jamie, our tour guide, was extremely informative and interesting and we all learned much about the social, economic and political causes for the creation of the camps, in addition to the history of the camp itself. Our tour was impacted by a train functioning issue as well as a torrential downpour while at the camp. Jamie handled these challenges with calm and grace. A must do tour.
Our guide was a menace. He refused to put a mask on in the train and when confronted he refused and got in an awkward standoff-ish encounter. Overall decent knowledge of the camp though.
Excellent tour by Cian, an extremely knowledgeble tour guide, to the Sachenhausen concentration camp. May we never forget.

This was an excellent, very informative, and very moving tour of a German concentration camp. Our guide, Cian, was fantastic -- very knowledgeable, very personal, and very respectful of the serious nature of the site.

We felt this tour was just the right size -- enough of the historical site and information for us to get a real sense of the context and conditions, but not exhausting in time and not overwhelming and over-the-top with gruesomeness and horror.

Cian was a particularly great guide (and we have had our share of not great ones). He planned the tour with a great pace, allotting enough time of us to see everything while not rushing. He was very sensitive with the historical material, telling us the hard truths that need to be told but not dwelling there so much where everyone is just disgusted and depressed the whole day. We were particularly impressed and pleased at how he spent extra time during the ride back to Berlin talking to each family personally, helping with directions home or with advice on other things to do.

We booking through trip advisor. Our tour guide was ciaran. He was excellent. Great story of history before we entered the camp and this continued to the end. Well worth visiting here. Unbelievable the size of it.

Our tour guide, Gregor Berger deserves a shout out! He put the entire explanation in context of what was happening at the time and how hate doesn’t evolve overnight. It’s a process. People benefit from hate, people are murdered from hate. It’s an arduous day. If people endured suffering and got murdered, then we can honor their memories by showing up! Gregor has a masters degree in art history. He understands history. He made the day an excellent learning experience.

The guide was friendly and warm.
He ensured everyone was there before starting his explanations.
Certainly a place that required a guide.
The only thing is it all felt a bit hurried.

“Swedish” Maria is very knowledgeable about the topic, is very patient, and has a good attitude.
Please include in your tour information that travelers should get a 9-euro unlimited metro ticket (instead of an ABC zone ticket).
From the very beginning at the meeting point to the train ride back our tour guide walid was very helpful, informative and friendly, would highly recommend this tour again.
Chloe was a brilliant guide. Super polite, well informed and caring for the group. We definitely enjoyed our experience and can't recommend it more.

A sad yet must do in Berlin. Highly recommend Booking with tour guide Cian.
We booked a day in advance but it’s better to do the booking well in time.
The tour is so well worth it. Our guide was Ciarán and he did an amazing job. Couldn't have asked for a better guide. Highly recommended.
Jamie G was an excellent guide who ensured we got the most out of our time there. Really good tour overall!
Very well organised tour. Our tour guide Walid was excellent - he really knew his subject. He was interesting and articulate and managed to bring some lighter moments to a very dark subject.
Better communication from the trip. No acknowledgment of booking but still kindly took our money. No effort by the team to help
Rob Shaw was amazing and informative! Left there with so much knowledge and information! We lucked out with our guide!!

Very sobering and moving experience to hear about and walk the path of those who were imprisoned, suffered, executed, tortured, worked and died there. So hard to comprehend what it must have been like. Yet, Nickoli, our guide, was very informative and treated the subject matter with the respect and depth that it deserved. Highly recommend this experience to anyone.
Just a note: quite a lot of walking and very little stopping for those who aren’t expecting it. Worth it but wish I was told in the “what to expect”.

Martin was an excellent guide. Having lived and grown up in Oranienburg, where the camp is located, gave him an expansive knowledge of the area. It was an emotive and educational tour and well worth the visit and time.
Chris was an informative and engaging guide. Even though I’ve been to Sachenhausen before I didn’t do a guided tour - it is a completely different experience and one I’d recommend.
Although it was a LOT of walking (7km) Martin had amazing knowledge as an Oranienburg local. He has interviewed multiple survivors from the camp and was a wealth of knowledge.

We had Ioanna for our tour and she was extremely knowledgeable and friendly. The tour was jam packed with information but we were still given time to ask questions. We would definitely use this company again

Had a very somber but eye opening tour with Nickolai. The tour was filled with lots of history and definitely gave an over view of the camp with some interesting stories. Definitely need to have your walking shoes on and there is the option at the end of the tour to stay at the camp as there is still lots to experience.
Great tour, great experience. Martin was fantastic and gave us so much information. It really helped put everything into context. Highly recommend this and get Martin if you can.
Excellent tour with a really informative guide (Jamie). Would highly recommend if you’re interested in the surrounding history.

Martin’s sincere commitment to share the facts about this crucial and painful history was uplifting which goes some way to compensate for the sad and shocking nature of the experience. He is a superb guide and individual. Well done sir.
Guide was extremely passionate, helpful, and informative. Tour requires walking but it is not much if you are used to it. Bring food and water with you
Laura did a great job on this tour. You can tell she feels the terrible history that she is sharing. The grounds have changed a lot but you still get the history of all the horror that went in there.
Our guide Gregor was friendly and highly informative. He asked thought provoking questions. It was a memorable adventure.
Xavier was an amazing tour guide. He knew what to say and when to say it. It was an excellent experience and Sachsenhausen was very important to learn about.
Went here with a guided tour. Vast area of land and lots of walking on the flat required to get around it all. Shop, small cafe and toilets available.

The guide knew much of the history of the camp. We have visited a few concentration camps, but this was the first time with a quide. We think doing the tour with a guide gives you extra information. So we can recommend it.
The camp was sobering but worth going too. My only problem was how far we had to walk to get there. A shuttle bus or something would be nice. I would encourage anyone to take the tour if in the area.
Ioana was an incredible guide and knew everything about Sachsenhausen and the war in general. The tour was well run, interesting, and memorable. If you are in Berlin definitely make time for this!
Martin was an outstanding and articulate guide who made the tour very absorbing, educational and worthwhile. Much recommended
Our guide Gregor was excellent. His insight and knowledge were first rate. His engaging manner made the tour an informative and valuable experience. I would highly recommend this tour.
Horrible no communication ripped me off $200 twice worst ever no one use this guide please for your own good.
We had joana do our tour and she knew her stuff! Very friendly, approachable and knowledgeable about every part it!
No clear instructions given as to where to meet our guide, call centre unhelpful in resolving the issue, tour guide seemed impatient and rushed
Excellent learning experience. Ioana was amazing and knows so much history and the way she explained it makes it more interesting. Be prepared to walk a lot.
The guide was knowledgeable, attempted to keep us dry on a rainy day and made sure everyone was able to hear what he had to say.
What a fantastic tour, Mike was a brilliant, made the day. Hugely informative, interesting and engaging. Can’t recommend Insider Tours and Mike highly enough.

Maria was an excellent guide with a tremendous amount of knowledge regarding the Holocaust. More importantly she did not hold back in telling the truth behind the atrocities. I highly recommend this excursion as a must in your stay.

We did this tour with Viator tours and our tour guide was Marie who was absolutley brillant with her knowledge of history of the camp and area surrounding also showed us how to work the train system in Berlin which was a great saving compared to getting taxis everywhere would highly recommend 5*
The guide was superb and thorough in explaining the history and insights. And the tour itself is well planned out.

Jamie G was a fantastic tour guide. He was very friendly and was very informative which helped me to better understand the significance of what we saw. They also made travel much easier than if i went on my own.
Our guide Nick was amazing! He was very informative and even offered ideas on what to do after the tour. Highly recommend this tour for sure!
Amazing , sobering, and educational experience. We saw the open areas where buildings used to be, outlines of the foundations of buildings, as well as a couple of buildings still intact.
Very informative. If you prefer a guide to a headset this is a great choice. Be prepared to walk from the train to the camp.

My husband and I decided to visit Berlin earlier this year, and before I planned any of our itinerary I knew we had to visit the former concentration camp. I am extremely grateful that we were able to book with this group as our tour guide, Mike, was exceptional! He was extremely helpful in getting everyone from point a to b on the train, making sure we all had the proper tickets. From the moment we left as a group, Mike was engaging and made sure any and all of our questions were answered. He had a wealth of knowledge and was eager to share with all of us in a respectful manner.

The tour itself was a sobering experience to see first hand where these atrocities occurred. It was a rainy, cold day on the day we visited which felt extremely fitting for the locale.

Bring a snack and water and comfortable shoes as you will be walking a lot.

Thank you Mike for an unforgettable experience!

We took this tour August 7th. Our tour guide, Sebastian, was very knowledgeable, he spoke clearly and with the right volume for the group. He made the tour a memorable learning experience. While this a sobering place to visit he clearly explained the history. I wish I had high school teachers with his teaching ability. We highly recommend this tour and especially with this tour guide.

Really informative, respectful and interesting tour. Our tour guide Gabriela was great and was able to take us through everything with a lot of information. Would definitely recommend doing this tour with this company. If we had more time in Berlin we would have booked more tours with them.

Extremely well run tour led by Martin. As a genuine local he’s knowledge was fantastic and his English terrific. He was super accommodating, informative and thoughtful throughout the entire tour. Although a very sobering experience learning and understanding the history of the area, Martin kept the group interested, engaged and reflective the entire time.
(For Aussies - Don’t hold it against him he’s Richmond tigers supporter)

The tour was a long one but well worth it. There is so much to learn about the past. Our guide Martin was excellent. He was knowledgeable and very accommodating to all our questions.
I’m glad we brought some food as this is done in the middle of the day.

Whilst visiting Berlin, we felt compelled to visit this site. Sarah, our guide, was very informative and very helpful with getting the right train tickets etc. Very thought provoking and to me a necessity for our visit to Berlin (which is a really friendly city). I’m sure you could visit independently but I think a guide is essential to get the most out of the site (they do have audio guides for hire).
We have two young teens who were kept interested throughout, the only thing to consider is that it is a long day on your feet.

Martin our tour guide was extremely informed and could answer any question we had. His accent was easy to understand and he was very interactive with the whole group. I learnt a lot and would highly recommend this to anyone wanting to learn more about the history and timeline of Sachsenhausen and Germany before, during and after ww2.
Martin was an awesome guide, he was able to answer our questions and so much more! We learnt so much. 100% would recommend this tour.

Tour guide extremely knowledgeable, friendly and approachable. Would highly recommend this tour.

Point to note - you will require a packed lunch / drink and a travel card covering zones A, B and C.

Our tour guide was amazing. Gabriela was very polite, very informative and very respectful. The tour was not as long as I expected which was good because it was very cold. I learnt a lot and would definitely recommend it.

The eastern meeting point was a couple of minutes from our apartment so very convenient. We were met by our tour guide Gabriele who was very helpful from the start and informed us which train ticket we needed to buy
Throughout the journey to the memorial she stopped regularly to give us history of the area
Having previously visited the memorial on a school trip I had some knowledge of the camp but doing it this time with Gabi was so much better. She is very knowledgable and I left the memorial this time with so much extra information than previously

This was number one on my list when I came to Germany, and I’m so glad I went. The tour guide was incredibly knowledgeable, however sometimes I felt she moved to quickly from place to place (although I can’t really fault her, there’s so much ground and history to cover.) The site is well maintained and I appreciate that the museum and different exhibits are kept quite simple and to the point. It rained much of the day, but I didn’t really mind. It felt somewhat appropriate. Highly recommend.
Nickolai was very knowledgeable and passionate about everything on the tour. It was along day but we were warned up front that it would be so be prepared.

We generally could not have had a better guide, we were lucky enough to have Martin and he was so intresting, interactive and made the day a enjoyable day even thought it was an emotional, eye opening experience!
The trip so interesting to see and learn about! I highly recommend it to anyone! And if you are lucky enough to get Martin.. you couldn’t want more!!

Martin was very friendly and helpful in answering any questions. His knowledge of the camp and the local history was outstanding.

He really painted a very real picture in what happened at the camp and you able to create a clear picture in your mind of what life might have been like there.

It was a harrowing and eerie day and although it was a bit chilly (wrap up warm) we learnt a hell of a lot and was interested in every word Martin had to tell us .

Tour starts by meeting at the McDonald’s outside the zoo train station for if you’re in the west. Here you meet the guide redeem your ticket and buy a train pass. You then take the train the town and take a 20 min walk to the camp. The guide wil walk you round the camp there’s never actually any time to eat but we just ate a sandwich in-between walking to different points of the camp. Time went quite quickly so you don’t even realise you’ve been there all day as what the guide is saying is so interesting!

Fantastic tour would highly recommend

very knowledgeable tour guide who gave us a much richer experience than just visiting the site on our own would have done. As you can imagine It was very difficult in places listening to the awful things that happened here. However the need to learn lessons and honour those who died is a central theme to the exhibitions and one that makes this a valuable experience which I felt was really brought to life by having a tour guide.

You will need a ticket for use on the trains (Zone A B and C) comfortable shoes and water. There is a walk from the station to the camp as the buses are not too regular. You will be on your feet the whole time but there are opportunities for rest stops / comfort breaks.

An incredible experience with our tour guide Martin who had a vast knowledge of Sachenhausen and of all the things that went on here during the war. We went into the bunkers and section Z and had a look around the camp. It was a 6 hour tour in English but it could have easily been so much longer! An airy sad place but fascinating for those who enjoy learning about the war and the SS reign.

The tour was very interesting. The travel with train + walk took around 1.5h. Then we spent 2.5-3h at Sachsenhausen. The guide talked sometimes a bit too fast but with very good english. A lot of information and very well made exhibitions. The guide helped us to not get stuck too long at some places such that we could see most parts. A lot of walking and in total almost 6h so maybe a bit too tough for small children.
Our guide was knowledgeable and empathetic to the gravity of the topic and managed to communicate the information in a very appropriate manner. It was a very well worth while tour.

An essential site for the history of the rise of the Nazi party and their clinical destruction of opposition. Well preserved and utterly chilling. First time I’ve been in the watchtower by the front gates. Highly recommended educational experience
Had Sebastian for tour. He was excellent really made it enjoyable. Really brought things to life. Day flew in.

With all that’s going on in the world and particularly the UK, you only need to visit this concentration camp to realise the potential peril that could become with nationalistic rhetoric. This is a very sobering experience extremely difficult to comprehend! Difficult to describe the emotions, I suspect we will all deal with this differently.
A fascinating and poignant experience. Our tour guide Sebastian was very knowledgable and delivered information in an animated and compelling manner.

John was a great guide, he kept it really interesting and let us have a little wonder often so we could properly look at things. Always happy to answer any of our questions and was very knowledgeable! It was a very cold day though so wrap up warm in the winter!

What a day. An extremely worthwhile step into such a dark part of Germany’s history. Mike was a wealth of knowledge and used every moment to impart that knowledge with amazing factual details. He pulled us in with harrowing stories of those murdered, those attempting to just survive, those in denial, those who were rescued and the heroes who assisted them. I feel like I’m still processing but found today while devastatingly difficult, also encouraging as we know now to do better and learn from these horrible atrocities. An extremely worthwhile venture.

As a side note, Mike, thank you for taking the time to share “extras” like encouragement to check out the Otto Weidt museum (which we thoroughly appreciated) and the Rausch chocolate store and Resistance museum (on the agenda for tomorrow)

We are now looking into Insider tours in other cities because if they’re all this good, we are definitely hooked.

Our guide Taylor (Tyler?) from Australia was super knowledgeable, great speaker and managed our large group really well, couldn’t have been better.

I very much recommend this tour, it was mind blowing to walk on the same place that these monsters carried out their atrocities. The camp is huge and has tons of documents, photos and we could see the barracks, infirmary, camp prison and execution areas, among other things.

Bring comfortable shoes, food and water, and be ready to walk a lot.

From reading about Sachsenhausen beforehand we expected that there was little to see, but as it wasn't closest to Berlin we went on trip/tour. It was an outstanding learning experience for our entire family and our guide, Sebastian, was tremendous.
The whole experience was extremely informative and Julian certainly knows his stuff. 10/10 would recommend
Everithing was perfect. Very good guide with a lot of knowlege and disposition. The coordination was very easy. A highly recommended visit.
It was a very moving, interesting and thought provoking visit, our tour guide Ronan was brilliant, he had so much useful information , and was great at answering our questions.

Sebastian was very knowledgeable and passionate about the subject matter. Would recommend this tour.
I would advise anyone visiting to bring a packed lunch and wrap up warm!

Lucky we had a dry day to tour around this vast camp, learning all about the past &,how it worked etc
I suggest you wear comfy footwear as alot of walking to be done and take a drink & snack with you ,although there is a coffee shop but it is not that big ,

This is a very eye opening tour which I would highly recommend doing. We had Martin as our tour guide he was absolutely amazing and soo knowledgeable. Thanks Martin for being our guide from the kiwis.

Very interesting tour and our guide was brilliant
Quite a walk from the railway station
Still can’t believe how cruel people can be

Very moving experience. Our tour guide Sebastian was brilliant! The camp is almost completely reconstructed yet he done a wonderful job of describing what conditions would have been like at the time. Very knowledgable and passionate about the subject. He was very thoughtful of everyone on his tour and just a lovely guy! On the train back to Berlin he asked us what we were doing with the rest of our day, gave us directions on how to get there and even recommendations for restaurants/bars nearby. Definitely recommend!

We were met by Phil our tour guide outside the train station at am to pm. He kept us well informed all along the way to the camp, always checking if people were comfortable... When we got to the camp he provided us with a clear and concise picture of what the camp was like and the atrocities that happened there.... Definitely go and see, and if you are lucky you will get Phil as your guide.... Top marks to Phil...... Oh and Paul chloe from Kilsyth were very nice young couple.... Just ask chloe what a rest room is.... Lol

I took the Sachsenhausen Concentration camp tour with Sebastian, who spoke English very well. He was well versed in European history and ensured we have the proper historical context leading to the creation of this camp. It was a very informative tour that is recommend to anyone.

Martin, was one of the most outstanding guides we have ever had. Also, he is a terrific human being. He is dedicated to making sure the world is a better place and that the world does not forget the horrors. Hervorragende Anleitung.
The tour is long, all day really. Martin spend several hours longer than scheduled so that we would see and understand it all. The walk from the train station to the camp, as the prisoners took, was powerful and informative. Take this tour.

This was my first time to a concentration camp. You walk a lot during this tour, around 12,000 steps according to my iPhone. The tour guide,Sebastian, is fantastic! He really knows his history. Speaks perfect English and is very easy to understand. He keeps you engaged the entire tour.

Mike was a fantastic tour guide. Friendly and approachable and he really knew his stuff; all the way down to dates and years.

If you're looking for a good tour guide; Mike's your man!

Sarah, from Australia, was an excellent guide. She was professional, sensitive to contextual surroundings, knowledgeable, very kind and engaging. We learnt a lot about sachsenhausen. Thank you, Sarah.

A very interesting tour with nice and profosjonell guide. Provided a good historical foundation for how such an awful part of our history could arise. Also good and detailed description of how the conditions were in the camp.

The tour was well organized. the tour guide Sebastian Was very knowledgeable of the history of what happened in this place. He kept everybody’s attention and explained with detailed. Great tour highly recommend. Especially the guide Sebastian. ❤️
Very limited information about the place at the site. Pictures tell a soft story. The words are more honest. It doesn't give much of an impression of what the place was really like.

Excellent tour provided by Insider Tour - our guide 'Jan' was very friendly and provided a very insightful, highly knowledgable tour of the site. He looked after us from start to finish and ensured that we stayed together particular across the myriad of trains.

Room for improvements would be to provide a rough timetable (i.e when there would be opportunities for comfort breaks, snacking etc). Also, I would have liked more time in the camp, especially in the museum.

Advice: wear flat shoes and be prepared for lots of walking.

Overall, though a brilliant tour and should not be missed. Highly recommended!

Our tour guide Jan was incredibly knowledgeable and we learnt so much during this tour. It's a really tough and emotional place and part of our history but it's also important to be aware of it. Definitely recommend this tour if you're interested in learning. Jan made sure that we all knew what direction we needed to head in after the tour. Remember to take water, snacks and lunch as there isn't anything there.

An excellent day out with a knowledgeable and courteous guide,Jim. He added a wealth of context and information before, during and after the tour. He also made sure everyone got their connections back from the train station. Well worth the price.

My partner and I visited Berlin at the start of October for 3 nights and decided to spend one of our days visiting the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp Memorial. Absolutely incredible value for money - Our guide Julian was incredibly knowledgeable and insightful. Would highly recommend this tour to anyone.

We did this fantastic walking tour of sachenhausen concentration camp yesterday with an American guide called josh . He is very intelligent, articulate and clearly passionate about this role. The weather was cold , raining and as it was a public holiday - the train to and from was standing room only.

We had a large group which made it difficult . If your out the back you had difficulty in hearing Josh, so we basically stuck with the front section most of the day . I was impressed with his knowledge and how he gave you his opinions and supported it by facts when required .

The camp is well set out and even though only minimal buildings left in situ - josh ensured we all understood the ways of the world with this camp. The horrific death pit , gas chambers , execution rooms and crematorium was very sad to see . Poor poor people . The story is being told now and we all pray that this doesn’t ever happen in the future.

My only criticism would be that it is quite rushed and you definitely beed more time inside the camp to read the exhibits and experience it. Josh offered everyone the opportunity to stay back and finish the tour at your own Pace . I don’t believe anyone did on our tour .

Great value for money and I learnt a great deal about this horrible chapter in history , thoroughly recommend this company.

We went on the tour with Ronan with our 2 kids. Phenomenal experience. He's extraordinarily knowledgeable about the site, the history and the details. He kept the entire group engaged throughout. This tour was well worth it and I'm sure much better than the hand held devices people are using walking around the camp. Highly recommend it!

Ronan (Irish man, we think that’s his name!) was brilliant. So well versed in all the history and I could listen to him for hours. He was so easy to listen to and could answer any question thrown at him. His delivery was perfect for this type of tour. I have been on 2 insider tours and 1 with another company, and they haven’t come close to the tour guides from this company. Thank you!

An extremely interesting, emotional and enlightning tour with the best and proficient guide, Nikolai! Recommened this trip to everyone!
/Mariell

Was able to visit the ‘model’ concentration camp built 30 min train ride from the centre of Berlin and be immersed in a terrible side of history.

Josh, our tour guide, has an incredible breadth and depth of knowledge about the camp which he delivers in an engaging manner at 15 of the camps locations.

The tour starts in an easy to find place in Berlin Zoologischer Garten train station. You’ll see the crowd forming for this and various other tours. For the tour you need an ABC ticket but the tour guides can help you if required
Very informative and eye opening. Tour guide was helpful from meeting him at the train station in Berlin to getting back to start point in Berlin!

Definitely worth a visit. Very eye opening experience. Our guide, Taylor, was extremly well informed and beyond helpful with any questions or even transport advice for afterwards. Thanks again Taylor!

We had Taylor, a fellow Australian living in Germany, as our guide. The trip was extremely well organised. He took us on public transport but he was very knowledgeable and the system in Berlin is very user friendly. It was very sad subject matter but he was very informative and humorous when appropriate. We had enough time to see the main points but we covered it very efficiently. Had a fantastic day, would go again and thoroughly recommend.

Our guide was very knowledgeable and friendly. She escorted us from an easy to find meeting place and accompanied us on public transport to and from the site. My friend and I both really enjoyed the day. Thank you!

The visit to Sachsenhausen was well coordinated, education, and sobering. As a past employee of the camp, our guide Martin, was exceptionally well versed in the operations and passionate about what happened there. It was very moving and I highly recommend the tour.

Not everyone chooses a side trip to a concentration camp. Our tour guide Jim was fantastic. A good storyteller that knew how to give our large group a great experience - handling the trip with respect, perspective and knowledge.

Amazing tour! It is a lot of walking, but well worth every penny. Chloe is an amazing tour guide. She is knowledgeable and can answer all of your questions. She made this tour a great experience. She also made great recommendations on things to do while in Berlin. I would go on all the tours offered with Chloe if I could. Highly recommend the Sachsenhausen tour to anyone visiting Germany.

What should anyone expect? Pure evil by the Nazis.To see the many faces of innocent young men being starved, punished, hung, and shot deliberately for fun, religious, experimentation or political reasons is disturbing. This was a sad time in our world and we should all be willing to not let hate and evil happen again. Everyone should visit and hear the evil. Josh (Ohio) our tour guide was excellent and well knowledgeable on the holocaust and most of the other concentration camps. The details he gave was more than you would get from an audio tour.

Great way to spend one of your days when staying in Berlin! Our tour guide Julian made everybody feel comfortable as well as being very informative and interesting, with lots of further knowledge beyond what the tour required!
Excellent tour with guide Martin an extremley knowledgable local with perfect english. A sobering experience
Julian did a wonderful job guiding us through this tour. He was respectful and very knowledgeable. We highly recommend this tour.

Ok what can I say that hasn't been covered ?

Really didn't know what to expect when we started out on a visit here. I would say that every person should visit a place like this to make them realise the cruelness mankind can have if not kept in check.

The location of the camp is about a 20 minute walk from the town's train station but is well sign posted .

The tour guide -Stephen of Sandermans New Berlin guides was excellent . His knowledge of the camp just added to the whole experience.

The location has well presented information boards and wc's are available on site

As someone who teaches a History of the Holocaust class in an American university, I can tell you that Martin, our guide, knows his stuff very well. Rest assured you will learn the how and whys of Sachsenhausen and the concentration camp system. He was also very accommodating to my mother who required some walking assistance and was very inviting to everyone. Highly recommended!

Martin our tour guide is a very interesting and informed man. His depth of knowledge in his subject is amazing. The tour of Sachsenausen was both emotional and harrowing at times. A must if you visit Berlin.
Great tour with very professional local tour guide Martin who dished up this heavy material in an authentic and pleasant manner. Highly recommended!

On arrival, Taylor made sure that we were prepared for the day ahead logistically, checking we had food and the correct train tickets.
We then travelled as a group to the memorial where he gave us lots of information on the way , the same route as the prisoners would have taken.
Once we got to the site, it was really useful to have someone to explain the significance of the ruins and memorial objects and to give them context. He was very informative and knew so many facts.
On the return journey home he ensured everyone in the party knew how to get to their next destination.
Overall, brilliant!

To go or not to go while on your hols....he wanted to go as he loves history, I don't so I didn't want to ruin my holiday vibe. Selfish perhaps but that's how I felt. I decided I'd see what I felt like on the day....so after 3 lovely leisurely days in Berlin, I sacrificed my 4th and went along on tour.
Our guide was Julian, an extremely knowledgeable and likeable Canadian. Our group was 18 people.
So logistics involve meeting the group, getting a train and bus to Sachenhausen. Walking about 3km snd standing for a number of hours during the actual tour.. You need to bring food and drink with you as limited options to buy while there.
Then walk and train back to Berlin: 6 hours.

Experience: grim, bleak place. Not a fun day to spend BUT came away with really good understanding of what went on, the history that led to this, the other groups of people tortured as well as the Jews, the jaw dropping enormity of what people do to others. We had some interesting conversations as a group, Julian managed the group and the questions well, he was very passionate on the subject.
The experience has stayed with ne the last 5 days since coming home.
I think if youve 3 days or less in Berlin I wouldn't do unless it's a priority for you .
If you've any longer, then definately do.
Very good value for money.

We had a wonderful day with Sebastian - he is very knowledgeable and explained the history of how Germany progressed to the point where the Nazis came into power.
Additional time should be included to be able to review the exhibits.
A LOT of walking is required.
Note: additional transport costs are required for train travel to the Camp.
I had Pip doing our tour and she was great. Very accomodating and knowledgeable. I found the tour interesting mainly based off her stories because I didn't find the site itself very stimulating.

I definitely got more than what I expected out of this tour! Sebastian did a wonderful job of explaining the historical context that gave rise to Hitler and the Third Reich. This made it easier to understand how the atrocities in Sachsenhausen and other concentration camps could even happen.

My only suggestion is for us to have more time explorong the exhibits on our own. I wanted to check out the museum in the former camp kitchen but we had to continue on. In the end though, the duration and pace was just about right.
Did this tour today. Our guide Sebastian was so interesting and informative, so much to see here that time is an issue but Sebatians knowledge made up for this. I would highly reccommend this tour

Meet up instructions simple. Guide Sebastian was ace, really clear with travel instructions and very very knowlegeable. He put the trip into context commencing 200 years before the events which gave food for thought. We did the trip in 30 plus degrees heat and there was lots of walking so reasonable level of fitness required. Would absolutely recommend. For anyone thinking of taking teens, my 13 year old got lots out of the trip too xx

Our tour guide (lovely Irish dude sorry forgot his name) was very knowledgable about the camp and its history. Its a 6 hour tour but the time went by quite fast as there was lots to see as well. Not an easy tour based on the history but kudos to the guide for telling the stories as sensitively as he could. I would highly recommend the tour to anyone who hasn't been or if visiting Berlin for the list time.
Our experience was amazing. Our guide Julian was excellent. We learned a lot and it’s definitely a must to do when you are in Berlin.

Josh was an incredible tour guide. He was extremely informative and knowledgeable about the camp as well as all aspects of post and pre World War 2. He really sets the scene on the way to the camp discussing World War 1 and Hitlers rise to power. I highly recommend the tour, it was one of the best things we did whilst in Berlin.

I did this tour on on 25.8.19, really enjoyed it, the tour guide Khole was great. I definitely recommend this tour if you have time, it involves a lot of walking so make sure you’re prepared. If you have time after the tour and you’re not too tired you have the option of staying there longer. We didn’t get much time to go through all the written information and by the end of the tour I was exhausted, it didn’t help that the weather was so hot.
Very heavy and deep historical subject, but most certainly worth the visit. I would definitely go again.

This was a really great informative tour that I'm sure even those with a lot of knowledge of the time would be impressed with. It was probably the best thing I did whilst visiting Berlin. I came away from it quite moved with a fresh interest to learn more about this sad part of history. Our guide Chloe was attentive to the needs of the group and clearly passionate about what she was saying. She made sure everyone was comfortable throughout and also helped everyone individually with getting back to their accommodations and also suggested other good attractions to visit and things to do in Berlin.

What an amazing place. The tour was well delivered and really opened up the story of the camp and the gave a prelude to world war 2 and after. Very impressed. On a personal note it was incredibly sad and at times unbelievable what humans have done to one another repeatedly.
I cannot recommend this tour highly enough.

Our group from west was overbooked. We accepted to change guide. Our tour guide was skilled and had a good ability to tell the awful story of this camp. Great experiance. Unfortunately the guide was very eager to take shortcuts, it was more important to get on the bus than compleating the whole tour.
