Our tour guide was Julian. He was great, very informative, easy to listen to and very friendly. The experience itself was obviously very sad but incredibly interesting and something everyone needs to do in their lifetime to stop things like this from happening again. Thanks again Julian :)

Jakub was a very good guide. Explained well, at a good pace, and had carisma! Very much enjoyed him as our guide.

Thanks
We had Jakub as guide. Very informative and reflected tour with him. Also very helpful with other information about Berlin. An absolute joy for us.

I was a little nervous about the tour due to never doing anything similar before, but it was fantastic! The guide Ciaràn was fantastic, he was so down to earth and an all round lovely guy, he got to know the tour goers individually and gave fantastic accounts of everything that happened in Sachsenhausen. 10/10 would recommend to anyone visiting Berlin with an interest in German history!

This tour was no ordinary tour and our guide Jamie Jim was no ordinary guide. He took great care to deliver a thought provoking and clear presentation of such an inhuman act.he was thoughtful caring and brought us through an emotionally charged situation with great calm.full marks Jim
Great day ! Our tour guide,Pip, was awesome. Make sure to bring a lunch and good running shoes as there is alot of walking.

Our tour guide Maria was really informative. She made our tour enjoyable considering the camp we visited wasn't a pleasant place for those souls that lived there. She interacted with everyone & took care of the ones who didn't quite get the proper train tickets. Thank you Maria for moving the tour along when necessary yet keeping everyone interested.
The whole experience was so moving and the work put into providing you with a glimpse of this atrocity is amazing...

It was very informative and the guide was very knowledgeable. The walk from the train station to the concentration camp is about 20 minutes, you need to have comfortable shoes and be able to keep up with the group. It was so worth it!

Absolutely amazing tour of this camp given by our guide Mark Curtis. His passion for this could really be felt the whole way through the tour. It was the best tour I have ever done and I would highly recommend dedicating a day to this when visiting Berlin.
Our tour guide Chloe was very knowledgeable and took us through the important parts of sachsenhausen
Really good tour with a very knowledgeable tour guide (Ronan). Will definitely do the tour again if given the opportunity.

Our guide, Chloe, was so knowledgeable about the history of the era and the camp itself. You can watch shows on television or read about the Holocaust, but nothing compares to standing in a concentration camp with a good guide and seeing and hearing for yourself the horrors that were inflicted on other human beings.

Sachsenhausen is an example from the past of what can happen when evil is allowed to flourish. We forget the lessons of the past at our peril, particularly given the current state of politics in the world, and this tour and the camp provides a vivid reminder of the importance that we need to be ever vigilant.
Our tour guide, Josh, was extremely knowledgeable on the subject and was able to manage the balance of providing interesting information and insights into the horror of what happened here while providing some relief from the gravity of the subject.
Josh managed our group well and kept us engaged throughout the tour and the camp itself provides a fascinating insight of what happened here.
Thoroughly recommended.

Excellent tour. Our guide Nikolai was very passionate and well educated. He provides very interesting and informative commentary throughout the journey, in the fitted of so many who didn't survive, the camp.
Wear comfy shoes and bring lunch.

Very solemn and moving. Nikolai was an excellent tour guide. He helped us get the necessary train tickets the day of the tour to and from the camp. While walking from the train station to the camp, Nikolai reminded us how the prisoners were treated by the citizens as the were marched through the town to the camp. Most citizens laughed and spit on the prisoners while some caring people would slip pieces of bread to those destined to the hard inhuman conditions in the camp. Make sure you bring water and food as there is no time to stop for lunch. A must do on your trip to Berlin.

Sebastian was an excellent tour guide, very informative and keeps it exciting. Made sure everyone had an idea of what to do with the rest of their time after the tour and gave great tips on where to eat. 10/10 would recommend.

We a family of 5 with 3 teams went on this tour today. Sebastian met us at the West Berlin meeting point. Suggested we grab some water and food before we started. He is an amazing guide. Our tour guide Nikolai briskly moved us through a very full day at Sachenshausen. There is a lot to see and, as promised, he left us feeling like we hadn’t quite seen enough at each stop in order to visit some of the many places inside this vast concentration camp.

Our guide told stories en route of the history as well as the stories of individuals. From him we learned what happened at many different locations in the camp, and of a liberation that came too late for many. Sachenshausen is an especially significant camp because all 32 concentration camps were administered from here. It was a labor camp rather than a death camp, and housed several types (or classes) of prisoners.

It is a walking tour, and there is a lot of walking. Make sure you bring water and something to eat: there is so much to do that there are only two 10-minute breaks. You are outside most of the time, so dress for the weather. While they caution you about bringing your children into some places, there was nothing age-inappropriate for my 13 year old. The tour was conducted in a way that made it suitable for all ages. It starts in Berlin where it is a 20+ minute train ride (tour guide gets you on and off the train) to Orangienburg where your walk begins.

Some of the impactful places included the main gate, the pathology room, the walls with barbed wire and clear line of sight to the guard towers, Station Z where prisoners were killed en masse, the prison within the camp, and the Jewish barracks. The scale of careful planning and execution of genocide and propaganda is gut wrenching. I am thankful that the German people neither shy away from nor glorify the ugliness of this chapter. It seems to me a very effective way of ensuring it doesn’t happen again.

Sachsenhausen was stripped of wood by a desperate German population after the war so all wooden structures have been recreated. Also, the socialist government began demolishing Station Z before an outcry stopped them, so only the ruins of the gas chambers, execution chambers, and cremation ovens remain. This was a little disappointing to me simply because I had an opportunity to visit Bergen Belsen as a teenager, where it was incredibly impactful to visit the barracks, see the ovens and stand in the very shower where countless victims died.

Please visit a concentration camp. Sachenshausen would be a good choice, and I would definitely use this tour company again.

Our guide Beth from Orignal Berlin Walks was so informative and involved that the experience was an enrichment of the German culture. She covered all the aspects of the war. Answered all the questions in minute detail til the end of our train ride. Best guide ever. Would totally recommend.
The information given was really interesting and clear and The guide was always looking that everyone was together

My high school daughter and I were mesmerized by our guide Julian’s articulate, well-organized, insightful, and thorough tour to Sachsenhausen Memorial on Friday. He explained the historical context of the Camp and the events that happened there. He helped us understand the Memorial’s buildings and artifacts. The tour was detailed, easy to understand, and interesting (“never boring” my daughter says🙂). We highly recommend taking a tour to ease transport and increase information absorption. The Memorial (thanks to Julian) was worth spending day at in our week in Berlin.

This is a concentration camp I hadn't heard of on previous visits to Germany. When I heard about it I thought it would be worth a visit and I wasn't disappointed, it is very well done, even considering it is a work in progress with improvements being made as we speak. Very thought provoking, a very real piece of living history.

A good tour with a very knowledgeable guide (Julian). The camp itself has much to see and provides much opportunity for reflection. A note on the booking portal to mention that while the tour is all day, there is no lunch stop so taking your own refreshments is a must.

Mike was a fantastic guide. Incredibly informative and careful with such a sensitive subject.
He ensured that every member of the group was spoken to and listened to. Questions were encouraged. Everyone was included.

It was lovely to be met at the train station to be guided to Sachsenhausen and back.
A full day. Personal and great value. Highly recommend this tour.

This tour was not the heart breaking reality check i thought i was signing up for. Our tour guide Ronan was amazing and put a very practical perspective to the camp which turned this tour into a very educational and fascinating day. I would highly recommend even to people who do not want to go.

This was one of the best guided tours I have been on. Mike was incredibly knowledgeable and also really passionate about the 20th century history of Berlin. His stories, descriptions and facts brought the place to life and helped us to understand fully its awful history. He took us through the site with great respect and explained also its impact, as a memorial, on modern Germany. A big day but a really interesting one that will stay with me.
Carol, Melbourne

Last Saturday we took the tour to Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp. Being Israelis and Jewish this visit was the highlight of our trip to Berlin.
From the moment we met Ronan we understood he was the perfect guide to that horrible place. He was so sensitive, talented, gifted guide. He provided the whole group with details and historical accounts of the events.
We were the only participants who had a strong connection with the Holocaust and Ronan was the perfect teacher who “taught” and explained with details and sensitivity the process and the horrors of those darkest years.
We could not have a better guide, Ronan is an excellent historian, and did his best to try and help all the group through the long walks. He even helped us find the train to get back to Berlin and got off in the station where we had to take another train walking us to the right platform.
We felt that not only we had learnt a new lesson but met a wonderful person.
Thanks Ronan for having been our guide.
Ruben and Gabriela Yudelevich, Israel, April 2019
Our tour guide Sebastian was amazing! His knowledge of every aspect of Sachsenhausen was incredible. I highly recommend this tour for anyone

Visited here on a tour with Sebastien as our guide. The site is horrific, of course, but extremely well curated and an extremely educational visit. I can't speak highly enough of Sebastien; superb knowledge, passion for his work and very empathetic with his guests.

I fully recommend this visit, everyone who comes to Berlin should take this tour.

We had a Taylor as our guide and it was clear from the outset that he was extremely knowledgeable about this era. He impressed us with his ability to filter his presentation for the benefit of the tour. I highly recommend Taylor for any tour as his demeanor and communication skills are excellent.

Wow, what a great but heartbreaking experience, our tour guide nickolai did a fantastic job at making everyone feel part of the group and managing to keep us all together and helping us find which train to get us back. Comfy shoes and water are a must, also suncream if sunny we did come back sunburnt! And you do spend a lot of time outside, overall a very good trip, would highly recommend, keep up the good work nickolai :)

Very deep, emotional, eye opener. This visit should made compulsory for every high school student. It makes everything soooo real. Joshua (Josh) was our guide and he was awesome, incredibly passionate and knowledgeable. From the moment you leave the train station, he reminded us we were about to walk the same walk so many walked to their dead. He made us get into the situation, he gave us facts as we walked along to the camp. He made it all a stronger experience. Please take half a day on your visit to Belin to come here.

Had an excellent tour with our guide Nickolai! Easy to find in the morning, very knowledgeable guide, kept the group together and made sure we all knew our trains back.

Bring your comfy shoes and snacks as listed on the instructions!

This is one of those tours you have to do to see just what humanity can do. I am still not too sure how I feel about the whole experience, but very glad we went.

John, our guide, was outstanding and very passionate and interesting and takes his job seriously. It is had to be entertaining in such a place, but he had all the facts and was very good at communicating them.

The trip to the camp via the train was simple and the group was a good size to manage. Prepare yourself for a long walk and wrap up warm as this place is so cold and windswept - again just makes you realise what the people here must have suffered.

Once inside, this place gives you the shivers - so many people crammed into this place forced to work and live in such extreme conditions .... I am going to stop here - go and see it for your self.

Highly recommended - well organised and well worth it.

John our guide was excellent - very informative and fun to spend a day with
The camp itself was thought provoking and raised some questions about what you would do in the same situations
Hard to believe that people lived and worked so near to the camp
Approx 18 in our group - just the right amount of people - would recommend a visit

We took this tour with Taylor from Insider Tour. This tour exceeded my expectations and is a must see while visiting Germany. Taylor took us on a detailed walk throughout the Camp to explain what it was like in the camp. He gives a great lead into how Hitler came to power prior to arriving at the Camp. We took this tour with our 12 and 10 year old kids. They did just fine on this tour. Taylor took us form location to location and explained what would have happened in each building. What were the guards like, what was life like on the inside. My wife and I both had tears in our eyes at one point while Taylor was explaining what it was like. It is a very emotional tour, but I am so glad we took the time to go visit. Well worth the money and time to get a detail count of World History.

We loved our tour of Sachsenhausen with Yan! He was very knowledgeable and an excellent leader of our group. There is a lot of walking, not only to get to the camp, but once you are inside, but it was worth every step. It was a memorable part of our trip and we highly recommend Insider Tour and Yan!

Well worth every step. We have Rob Willis as our guide who was a great storyteller. Lots of walking to get to and from the Camp, when you are there things are moved along quite quickly to get through it all. It’s nice not to have to think twice and follow a guide who knows it all.

Sara is an amazing tour guide! She is very informed and passionate about history. We learned so much about Sachsenhausen and Nazi Germany. Really appreciated that Sara was able to meet us near Brandenburg Gate and direct group through public transit to the camp. It made transport simple and easy and allowed for more time to ask Sara questions.

I was lucky enough to go on this tour today with guide Sam Noble who I highly recommend to anyone who is looking for an engaging and knowledgeable tour guide.

His understanding of German history of this time period is astonishing and his eloquence and way of explaining things enables you to learn a ton!

He was able to field even the most detailed of questions and give us recommendations for further learning. One of the best tour guides I’ve ever had! And worthwhile experiences I’ve had visiting Berlin!

Our guide "JJ" was amazing! He knew everything and more about history during, before and after the Sachsenhausen concentration camp. He was very professional, friendly and looked after the group very well. Me and my 11 years old son did the tour and we loved it! I def recommend it!

We was met by our English guide(Well he was Irish) outside McDonald's facing the zoo. Directions and instructions for public transport for the zones we needed to travel to was easy to understand. The tour was very interesting and the knowledge of our guide made the experience all the better.
Our guide was very attentive to all members of the group and took the time to speak individually to people and helped us all on route home
Nikolai was a great guide. Clear, informative, engaging and approachable, and always respectful of the moral dimensions of the subject. And he looked after us very well. Highly recommended.

We had an awesome time on this tour. Our guide Nikolai was amazing, he taught us a lot and made us really understand what the camp was like. While it was cold and raining when we went he kept us inside the buildings as much as possible. He made sure we all knew where to go before and after the tour as well, helped each person get home as easily as he could. Would highly recommend this tour.

First, our tour guide Pip was wonderful. She was very informative and did a great job interacting with the group. Visiting Sachsenhausen was one of the most powerful and humbling experiences of my entire life. In my opinion it is absolutely vital to see and learn about this place. A must do in Berlin.

We’ve done a lot of guided tours in different parts of the world and know the value a good guide can bring.
In Nikolai from insider tours we found on of the best!
Clear, informative, interesting delivery of a very difficult site to cover.
We were a group of 20+ from all corners of the world.
He made sure each and everyone of us were with him the whole way from The meeting point in Berlin to Sachsenhausen and back to Berlin. Great service!
But most importantly he delivered a great tour

A very worthwhile visit with very good guide. It was a bit rushed as due to those wishing to pay on day we did not leave the station until 10.25. The journey by train takes 40+ minutes and there is a 20 minute walk at destination (not mentioned in advertising). The Concentration Camp Memorial is excellently presented and there are many and informative information boards in English throughout. The day was very moving and our guide was very good in describing the horror of the period 1936 to 1945.

My mother and I did the Sachsenhausen tour with Josh. It was an incredibly moving experience with the opportunity to see the camp first hand, visit the museums onsite and hear stories of the prisoners, SS and general sentiment of the time.

Our guide Josh was excellent. He knew so much about the camp, but also most importantly he explained the context and important issues of the periods before, during and after the war. He also provided a great balance of broad information and very human/personal stories.

All in all, a brilliantly informative tour of a period in history that should not be forgotten.

Nicolai was our tour guide and he was very knowledgeable and helpful (he made sure everyone got on the right subway home). The tour itself was a rare and eye opening experience. You're not going to get a chance to visit a part of human history like this very often so take it!

We read the various reviews and considered doing the tour on our own and saving the £15.00 each.
So glad we didn't .
Ronan our guide was great and well worth the tour cost for his great presentation and exceptional knowledge on what is let's face it a difficult subject matter.
Expect a fair bit of walking on the tour, some shocking facts and to come away feeling educated and much wiser on the subject and at the same time happy and blessed for the life we have

It's not something you can generally get enthusiastic about, but for me it's essential to visit at least one of these camps to recognise how horrific these places were. This is apparently where the SS guards were trained for all the camps, so that may give you an idea of how horrific it was.

It's a bit of a trek to get to (about 40 mins by train from Berlin centre, then 20 minute walk), but absolutely worth it. Some of the site was bombed by the Russians at the end of the war, but there is still plenty to see. I highly recommend the audio tour, which is very informative and excellently done.

Most memorable moment? I went on a freezing cold November day, cloudy and miserable with a coat that really wasn't warm enough. I listed to the audio explaining how prisoners would be forced to stand in place outside for hours on end. I was freezing, wearing three layers of modern clothing, never mind if I was wearing thin prisoner clothes, starving and exhausted, with people being beaten and killed around me.

The human capacity for cruelty and the will to survive is perfectly illustrated at this site.

We had our trip with Ronan who was extremely informative and you could tell he was passionate about what he was talking about. We walked around for the whole day and he knew every answer to every question, It was a long day with a lot of tough information to take in but was well worth it.

Free entrance. We took the audio guide €3/person. Easy to use and different languages. Speechless. Ypu can feel the prisoners around. It’s the most amazing and emotional experience . We were in shock the rest of our day. This visit makes anyone realise how cruel humans really were.

Chloe took us around the concentration camp - she was extremely knowledgeable, helpful and charismatic. We learned so much and felt the gravity of the prisoners and the political sphere that encompassed German/European culture and hardship at the time. Would recommend to anyone traveling to Germany.

Tour guide (Ronan) was funny and generally an awesome guy. Even kept his cool with a red coated woman running after him 😂 lovely bloke and amazing historical tour with lots of info! (Great for any videographers)

honestly speechless, you walking in and you feel someone’s home. It’s the most amazing experience yet so emotional. We were left star struck for rest of the day. I would highly recommend booking a tour guide who would provide a variety of information which makes the visit just as outstanding. Overall I would say it sets history and makes anyone realise how cruel humans really were. Honestly no comment on how horrific it was

Josh was an exceptional tour guide during our visit to the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp.

He really understands how to engage the crowd, providing intriguing information about the different areas of the camp, as well as the lead up to it on the train.

This was an amazing tour! Brian our tour guide for the day was very informative and fun! Any questions we had about anything he was able to answer. It was 3 hours that went by in a blink of an eye. Brian made sure we were all understanding everything and helped each one of us get back to where we needed to go at the end of the day! It was a great experience and would deffinatley go on another tour with Brian!

This was without doubt one of the highlights of our visit to Berlin. The logistical organisation of the tour was flawless, and our tour guide Josh provided insightful and thought provoking commentary throughout the museum tour - around 3 hours at the camp in self. The way in which Josh shared the personal stories of individual prisoners held at the camp was especially moving, sharing both the horrors they faced, as well as the inspirational stories of camaraderie that existed between the prisoners. This really was an outstanding tour and I would recommend anyone visiting Berlin with a day to spare to take the time to visit Sachsenhausen with Insider Tours.

We had one of the most fascinating days with our guide Josh at Sachsenhausen yesterday. The tour was in depth and covered all major aspects of the camp, even covering relevant topics outside of the camp. Josh was very insightful and friendly, a truly lovely chap who answered any questions anyone had. He also recommended the best vegan restaurant (called 1990, thank you Josh, it did not disappoint!) for us to go for dinner. Overall, we’d recommend this tour to anyone we knew. Thanks again!

We did two tours in two days. The Sachsenhausen tour with Nikolai and the best of Berlin tour with Chloe.

Both tours were jam packed with information and I really felt like we learnt a lot. The tour guides are fun, personable and full of knowledge.

I found this the perfect way to explore the city and learn about its history and such a reasonable price too!

Would definitely recommend to anyone wanting to soak in the culture of this incredible city.

Our tour guide an American expat living in Berlin was so knowledgable about Sacsenhausen and Nazism in general. He asked for questions and really tailored the tour to the questions and interests of the group. He also did an amazing job talking about the horrors of the camps and talking about some of the more inspiring moments of the camp. Overall an amazing tour and would recommend it.

Ronan was our guide on this tour out to the concentration camp. He was extremely knowledgable - trying to keep us warm on our cold day out there, and always having time for questions. This is a tour that is not to be missed, even if you only have a few days in Berlin. Using a guide ensured that we heard stories and the background on the various buildings as we toured the camp.

He ensured that we knew how to use the train system and could also make it to the where we needed to, after the tour. (not in a rush to finish the tour)

Really interesting place, well worth the visit. The freezing temperatures really made us all think what the prisoners here had to endure . Our tour guide Ronan was very friendly and informative. He gave us time to look around but also kept the group moving through the site. He was happy to answer any questions and really knew his stuff.
There's a 10/15 minute walk at pace from the train station to the site so I'd recommend anyone with walking issues informs their guide as there is the option of a short bus journey instead.

Our tour guide Nickolai was really informative and had taken his time to ensure everyone was up to speed.

I would definitely do an insider tour again, superior value for money too.

It was a cold drizzly day but well worth the trip. Nickolai was amazing. Very informative made the day very interesting. Thanks. Hard to believe people can treat people like that. We had read about it now we have seen it. Very sad.

Our guide Ronan was excellent. He was very informative and helpful. It was great that the tour guides pick you up and help you get to the destination, it took a lot of stress off. I would definitely do tours with this group again but I would wear a warmer coat!

Alicia our guide was very passionate about Sachsenhausen and gave us a lot of intensely sobering and and sometimes shocking information. She conducted the tour at a fast pace which meant there wasn't very much time for reflection. But we were a large group and Alicia managed us masterfully. It was a bitterly cold and rainy day which made the camp even more desolate than it would have been otherwise and warmest clothes are absolutely essential at this time of year. My son and I failed to understand we needed to bring a packed lunch with us which could perhaps be made explicit in the confirmation paperwork.

My fiancé and I only had 2 days to spend in Berlin during our travels and I’m glad one of them was spent on this tour.
As someone who is very interested in WWII, the entire place was interesting and was the same for my fiancé who isn’t interested in the war at all.
Our guide for the day Alissa was fantastic, full of knowledge and always willing to explain this more in depth and answer any questions.

Would highly recommend to everyone!
Our tour guide was called Mike, and he really knew everything. We had an amazing tour for 6 hours, and he kept it interesting the whole time. Really recommend doing this tour!

Really pleased we booked this 6 hour trip through Insider tours and Ronan our guide was brilliant so knowledgeable and nothing was too much bother for him he even went out of his way to ensure we got on the right platform fir our way home 😊 We learnt so much about the history walked from the exact train station that the POW did. although you know what went on it just brings it all to reality and it was really not that long ago such awful atrocities. Wear comfortable shoes bring a snack and water and wear clothes suitable for the weather! Thanks Ronan you were excellent.

We had a very nice guide (JJ) and the the overall expirance was very nice! JJ had good knowledge on the history and alot of interesting stories. The tour felt a bit rushed at times though. We would have liked a little more time exploring the exhibits.

In Berlin for a few days with my family and we took the Sachsenhausen Tour with Chloe.
On a cold January day , Chloe looked after all the participants from the meeting point in Berlin , while travelling and at the camp. The delivery of her content was excellent and respectful. A very informative and educational visit and I'm glad we took the opportunity to go on this tour.
Chloe also gave us some really good local guidance on the way back and her restaurant recommendation worked out perfectly.

Beth was our guide. We met at the meeting point before all traveling to Sachsenhausen by train. The experience is sobering and made all the more relevant by Beth who has done postgraduate study on Nazi politics and how it shaped the thinking of the German people. I learned so much about how these atrocities were sanctioned at the time. Highly recommend this tour.

A great tour that had all the information we could need. Despite the freezing weather Chloe kept us engaged and moving with great information that was really relevant. The concentration camp was awful but a very historical experience and by having Chloe meant that we understood each element of the visit clearly.
We used our Berlin pass for the tour and the signing up and meeting process was really simple.
Great tour and a very informative and enjoyable day!
Thanks to Insider Tours and Chloe for a great tour.

We had a lovely day from beginning to end with Campbell on our trip to Sachsenhausen. He was witty, extremely knowledgable about the camp and German history, and did a great job laying out the day and our schedule and transport. Despite cold and rainy weather, Campbell kept us all engaged and did his best to explain things inside as much as possible to keep us dry and warm. The camp complex is quite large, and having a guide is a real asset to be able to really soak up and contemplate the horrors that took place there without worrying about navigating. Campbell answered any and all questions we had and gave a much appreciated concluding message about taking the time to visit places like Sachsenhausen lest we forget history that can all too easily repeat itself.
Thankful it is open for all to see and never forget. Many original things are gone because the Russians have removed it when they used it afterward when they delivered the place from the Nazi's.

Recently had a tour by Casaer. He was brilliant and so informative. He gave us a detailed tour and knew what he was talking about. He then told us how to get home and ensured we had a good time. The tour was thought provoking and a real insight to life during that time. The camp was very busy on the day but we were still able to see everything and hear Casaer over the noise and people.

We went on a tour of the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp. 2 of the group had visited before but that was no issue as the tour guide Mike made it incredibly interesting and fresh, explaining the context of the camp and its' implications. History is clearly his passion and his knowledge is extensive.

A bonus is that Mike takes you from Central Berlin to the camp and back, so you can't get lost.

An excellent experience from start to finish. Would go again and thoroughly recommend to all. The best and most interesting example of Berlin's history in my opinion.

P.S. Mike also recommended a fab burger place to go after (the Bird) which was delicious.

This is an experience not to be missed if visiting Berlin. Our tour guide, Mike, was enthusiastic and extremely knowledgeable on the subject at hand. We met him at the East meeting point and he kept track of our group, on the two trains to get to Sachenhausen and also returning to our starting point. It was a cold day and there is a lot of walking outside, yet there were some heated buildings with exhibits as well. Mike presented this tour in meticulous detail and he clearly loved doing it!!

Our tour guide Pip was extremely knowledgeable and did a fantastic job of making an otherwise sad and serious topic interesting and enjoyable. She spoke very clearly and was able to answer all of our questions very well. I would definitely recommend taking this tour, especially if you are lucky enough to get Pip as your guide!
Our tour guide Pip was very knowledgeable, taking us on a well organised, informative and thought provoking tour.

I've never done anything like this before so I started the tour of the memorial with some trepidation. I needn't have worried because we had an exceptional tour guide . With an amazing amount of knowledge she walked us through a fascinating, respectful and educational journey of the memorial and while you can't gloss over the atrocities that occurred at Sachsenhausen it's something that I would heartily recommend. Ask for Pip !
Our guide, Nicklolai, was excellent. He was friendly and knowledgeable. The tour was informative and moving. Would recommend to all who have an interest in this period in history.
Did both the Sachsenhausen camp and Berlin walking tour with Mike. He gave us the best experience you could have on a tour. Extremely welcoming and knowledgeable.

The camp was very emotional & very informative. Our guide was superb with his in depth detail of the historical facts of the build up to the camps introduction & background to the politics of the day. Educational & thought provoking. Would definitely recommend a visit.

First time in Berlin Germany. We decided to take this tour on a cold day in December me n my wife, I thought is going to be a boring tour but I was WRONG... our tour guy Nickolai was very informative about the concentration camp he give us a lot information about the history of concentration camp. I can’t wait to go back to Berlin next year on the summer, and this tour it will be one my top list. Thanks for all the information, I had a good time even if it was really cold day.

A couple days ago a friend and I went on this tour with Campbell as our guide. Definitely recommend this tour, especially if you are looking for a detailed history of how concentration camps had a role in the war and how the local community around this time behaved. Also definitely recommend Campbell- he’s approachable, great with engaging the group, and top notch with knowledge on the history behind Sachsenhausen.

Our fabulous guide Campbell took us to Sachsenhausen. He was really knowledgeable about all aspects of the camp and the events leading up to its establishment. The tour reminds us this time in history must never be repeated and to extend tolerance and understanding to those who are different from us. A sobering experience from which we all learnt lots. Campbell was fabulous really helpful and engaging.

Alicia was our guide. We traveled out to Oranienburg by train, and then walked to the Sachsenhausen camp (maybe 20 Minutes walking). Alicia kept everyone well informed as we traveled so we could all keep together, and every time we had a few moments to wait (like for train), she used the time to provide us with lots of history and information about the political developments in Germany and the world in the first half of the 20th century and what historically led up to events. Our tour of the camp was at a good pace, and Alicia was fantastic at answering questions. A very informative, yet sobering tour. Oh, Alicia was great about helping each of us on the tour find our way back to where we wanted to go in Berlin at the end of the tour.
Our tour guide Pip was simply excellent, very helpful and knowledgeable and had a great insight into the dark history and background
My first time visiting a memorial like this - tour made even more fulfilling because we had a great guide. If you go ask for Brian Bell from insider tours.

The tour-guide Ronan was very professional and had a very in-depth knowledge of the camp and the time periods of when the camp operated.
He answered all questions willingly and went above and beyond to take us to the camp and back to Berlin on the German public transport.

Even though it was freezing cold, my boyfriend and I had a wonderful experience. I highly recommend this tour!

Had the pleasure of following Alicia around Sachsenhausen concentration camp. She was very friendly and was always approachable. The camp itself is a sombre experience, and with Alicia explaining the ins and outs, it was a real eye opener into what prisoners experienced. She was very knowledgeable and knew all the relevant and interesting stories, and delivered them in a way that captured the mood and moment. It was a fantastic tour - a homage, really. Highly recommended.

Went on the tour today. Were met by Brian at the West Berlin stop at the Zoo train station. He was very helpful and asked people to buy food, water, helped locate toilets at MacDonalds and buy the ABC train tickets. He went with us by train to meet Maria and her group where the two groups combined and Brian left. We took the train to Oranienburg which took 45 minutes. Another 25 minutes walk from the station to the camp. There was a 5-10 minutes break for a toilet break upon reaching the camp. Maria was very knowledgable. Positives are that the guide was knowledgeable. Negatives are that the tour felt very rushed with only 2 toilet breaks and a 10 minute break for lunch. We were not given sufficient time to look around the exhibition in the kitchen and the special cells. There is scope to spend 5-10 minutes less in some other places and give a little bit more time in the few buildings that actually remain. The low score is because at the end of the tour Maria just ran into the reception building of the camp and disappeared. We had to make our own way back to the train station in a strange place and then to Berlin. This was of real concern to me as I was on my own .It clearly states in the info provided while booking that the tour concludes at Berlin. We were all rushing and following other tourists ahead of us. The other Spanish speaking group from the same company travelled back with his group and was advising the group on where to eat, shop, answering their questions. Very disappointing and unprofessional and a big let down at the end of a very sombre day.
Only go for this tour if you are really interested in the history around nazi Germany etc. Please dress comfortably, good shoes as you will be walking for at least 4-5 hours. Please bring your food and drinks as well.
Very interesting activity, if a little sobering. Unfortunately the bus from the train station was full and our party had to walk approx 1/2 mile to the camp, but well worth it.

If you come to Berlin, this trip is a must. This is a reputable and highly professional company. I have taken several tours with them and this was the best. Brian Bell was our guide, he was knowledgeable, professional and made the day worth every second.

This is a sad day, but well worth it as this is a piece of history that needs to be well understood and seen in person to fully grasp.

Come with comfortable shoes and lunch. There is a fair amount of walking. Don't miss this opportunity if you come to Berlin.

On a city break with my partner and we decided while we were over here we would go and see Sachsenhausen as the war is something we both take an interest in. We were a bit unsure whether or not to go alone or to go with a tour as we like to take our time looking at things and exploring. But aren’t we glad we went with insider tours!
Chloe, our tour guide, was unbelievable. The knowledge she has and information she was telling us was so interesting and she put everything into perspective for us to help us understand. Chloe wasn’t only knowledgeable but passionate. You could tell how interested she was herself which had such a good effect on the group. I would definitely recommend going as a tour as Chloe was so organised with how to get there and back, as it is quite far out of the centre of Berlin and you definitely won’t have the same experience or gain the same information you do with a tour guide.

After learning about the holocaust in history at school as well as the Communist rule of Berlin during the Cold War I was really interested in visiting a concentration camp. I felt that it was an important thing for me to actually be there and visit the site that had learnt so much about. The tour was absolutely brilliantly informative and we learnt the stories of both individuals as well as the general population of the camp. Following this tour I am now keen to visit other sites including Auschwitz in the near future to broaden my knowledge further.

We always wanted to visit a concentration camp but we did not want to visit Auschwitz (a bit too much out of the way).
For us in Berlin this was the perfect opportunity. Ronan was very knowledgeable and answered all the questions we had.
He also gave us a very interesting insight on why the concentration camps were created.

Luigi

I've never understood how things like this could happen but Taylor our guide did an excellent job of setting the historical context and was able to give us the facts in a way that was informative and unbiased. We couldn't have asked for a better guide. I learned so much from him. It's obviously very distressing in parts but so important that we remember. Everyone should do this tour.

To say that this was an amazing trip feels wrong however it was an extremely informative and enlightening visit.
The organisation was excellent from start to finish as we met our guide, Taylor, at the meeting point on the East side of Berlin. Following in the footsteps of prisoners as they would have journeyed to Sachsenhausen we took the train then walked from the station to the camp. Taylor's knowledge was exceptional and his manner ensured that everyone fully understood the context of the era and therefore got the most out of the day.
The memorial and museum depict life in the camp and there is so much to see, read and absorb that you cannot do it all justice in the three and a half hours we were there BUT with our excellent guide we got the most out of it.
It is a walking tour so make sure you wear comfortable footwear and wrap up warm!!
This is a very well done and mentored tour, and very humbling. Great guide too. Really recommend this.

This tour was one of our highlights of our visit to Berlin. Our guide Taylor was fantastic. He gave us a great download of the history of the rise of Nazism without overloading us. So when we arrived in Sachsenhausen we had the historical context to make the tour more relevant and interesting.
The tour was really inspiring and humbling at the same time. It made many of us pause to reflect on the massive impact this camp had in Germany.
Even though it was a sobering experience, we really appreciated the visit and would recommend it to others.

My husband and I went with Jan K to see Sachsenhausen. This is a trip everyone should be required to take. With Jan's help in understanding the history and human condition that made such evil and horror possible, I walked away feeling I had experienced one of the most profound days of my life. Was it a fun tour? No. But it should not be fun. Instead, Jan helped us process the horror so that we walked away wanting to do more to make sure such a thing never again happens.

Our trip to Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp went really well. Trip was well-planned and interesting. Our tour guide Yan was amazing guide, who told the information in the engaging way. Would recommend this to a friend.

Our day trip to visit Sachsenhausen Camp was made incredibly easy and we were given enormous amounts of information throughout the entire day trip not just while at the camp! Mike was an incredible guide who had an enormous amount of knowledge that he shared with us all continuously. No question went unanswered. He definitely enhanced our experience! We would recommend this tour with Mike to others!

Hands down the best tour guide I've ever had. The Sachsenhausen tour is six hours and with Mike, you're engaged the entire time. He provides a very detailed background of what you're about to encounter on the way to the camp (about a 45-minute train ride) and has this tour down to an art. Once you're in the camp, Mike's guidance is unlike any other I've experienced. For all of the six hours, Mike shares his incredible intelligence of the camp/time period with the highest passion. Any question you have along the way will be answered.

You won't get a fraction out of visiting the camp on your own, so figure out when Mike is leading and book this tour if you plan on going. You won't be disappointed. Arrive at the meeting spot on time as the tour will leave as scheduled on the dot.

Done this tour today with our Texan guide Brian Bell. It was fantastic, really interesting and informative. Brian was charismatic and held everyone’s attention for the whole trip. Would definitely recommend it!

I would highly recommend the trip to Sachsenhausen. It was very informative and we had a very good tour guide who was very knowledgeable.

We met our tour guide Nickolai just outside of the Zoo train station where we were taken on the train to Oranienberg and from there a short walk to Sachsenhausen.

lt was very tiring and emotional, but it was a visit that we were glad we did whilst visiting Berlin.

I was extremely impressed with Brian, our tour guide for the Sachenhausen tour. His explanations of what went on in the camp, and also the historical events that lead up to that point, were very well explained and easy to follow. Brian allowed time for everyone to ask questions and even took time to sit with each member of the party on the return train journey home to recommend places to see in Berlin. I found the tour educational and thought-provoking. Would highly recommend.

A great way to experience the Sachenhausen concentration camp. The tour guide was very knowledgable and engaged in the tour. The only downside was that there was too little time to stroll around in the exhibition, the first part of the tour took too much time so the end of the tour felt a bit rushed.
Very knowledgeable. Very passionate. Well run tour company. Very personable, professional. Julien was a great guide. High quality tour. Low price.
Had a very interesting day and took so much in. Mike was very good at his job and I would recommend doing any of the tours with him. So much history in such a short period of time.

Taylor led the tour I was on in September 2018. He was very knowledgeable about the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp and passionate about remembering the tremendous sacrifices the prisoners went through, as well as those who freed the camp. Taylor especially was helpful after the tour to get us on the right train back to Berlin. It was a lot of walking, but very much worth the trip. The tour was reasonable in cost, and sobering to visit where so many suffered and died.

Mike, our tour leader’s unbelievable knowledge and enthusiastic delivery really made a awful subject matter very interesting straightforward to understand. The camp has to be seen to be believed. I left the tour feeling a lot wiser and knowing a lot more about the camp, nazis and Berlin’s wider history! 100% recommended.

Our guide (Pip) today gave us a fantastic tour with an impressive depth of information that really helped contextualise everything we were seeing. Beyond just the facts, she also presented a few different ideas and concepts that really made you think about the significance of what you were seeing and hearing. Well worth the money.

I did the walk tour with Taylor and was glad that I did take the time to it. It was an eye opener and Taylor was a geat guide with lots of information to download.

This is an enlightening experience not to be missed.

An enlightening experience of the atrocities of the nazi era. It’s a full day tour beginning at your selected train station start point where the tour guides take full responsibility for getting you sorted with your train ticket and also how to get home at the end of the day.. our tour guide was Ronan who was brilliant. His knowledge was excellent, invited questions from the group and kept us all fully informed and delivered the tour in a respectful and entertaining way. Take some food for your lunch and water plus some comfortable shoes.

John did an amazing job escorting us from central Berlin to the tour location and explained in great detail about a very somber topic. Tour ended about 4pm with enough time to explore Berlin after. There was a lot of walking so I wouldn’t recommend for people who can’t stand/walk for long periods of time.

Extremely chilling experience but a must for all to do. Our tour guide, Michael Dempsey, was a fountain of knowledge and kept the tour interesting throughout. Of all the things I did during my weekend in Berlin this was by far my favourite.

Toured with George. He was very informed and very passionate about the topic and it’s relevance to today. The tour had a brisk pace. You will have time at the end to self tour if you left your guide know and are confident on taking the train alone. Not a happy place but important to see if you have never visited a concentration camp before.
Easy Train ride, very informative tour , the pace of tour was easy , time went by quickly , great value for money , highly recommend.
Cesar was a wealth of knowledge. He provided much background on the history of Germany and what lead up to the atrocities committed in the concentration camps. I would recommend this tour to anyone.

Can I just say a huge thank you to Michael the tour guide for giving us a great tour today. His knowledge was incredibly detailed but moreover he explained the grotesque actions of the nazis with a gentle respect that was both kind and compassionate. The pace of the tour was perfect and Michael really cared for our needs as a group. Thanks again and good luck!

Initially unsure about length of tour (6 hours) but in the end, we could have spent longer there! We were well looked after by Taylor, from initial meeting at the train station, ensuring we had snacks for lunch, and the right travel ticket, to him giving an interesting and informative narrative as we travelled to Sachsenhausen, and while we were walking round the camp, to finally ensuring that everyone got back okay. Good value for money, and having a Tour Guide and going as a group much more enjoyable than just by yourself using an audio-guide.

I went on the Sachenhausen tour with my girlfriend, my mum, and her boyfriend today and must say I was very impressed 😊 our tour guide, Chloe, was very informative, and happy to answer any questions. She even gave us a few tips for some nice places to have dinner this evening and made some markings on my map of Berlin for us to help us find them. I have come away from the tour feeling educated, thank you Chloe :)

Absolutely worth the 45 mins train ride + 15 mins walk to visit this memorial. Josh was the perfect guide : very knowledgeable and efficient.
Purchase your train ticket ABC one day before going to the meeting spot (automic machine next to the meeting spot) and bring food with you for lunch onsite.
We went on the group tour to the concentration camp and we were engaged the whole tome thanks to our guides delivery and organisation. Would definitely recommend!
Fantastic tour. Really well informed guide called Pip. She was brilliant and helped us make sense of it all. Thanks so much.

This tour went very well - from both a logistics and subject matter standpoint. In our West Berlin originating tour, we travelled from the western city out to the suburbs to Oranienburg /Sachsenhausen, one of the first concentration camps and the administrative headquarters for the Nazi concentration camp network. Later, the site continued service as a camp during the Soviet occupation and later the DDR.

Chloe was able to manage a large group of international tourists to and through the site. There is a lot of difficult content to drive through and net out, which she was able to do for the diverse audience. The site is fairly large and presents lots of topics and themes -- Chloe's guided tour helped us manage to see and understand it all in one day.

I highly recommend this tour.

Cannot say enough about this trip. We met Ronan at the meeting point. He helped us purchase our subway tickets and was extremely pleasant the entire day. He was VERY knowledgeable about the camp and history. Clearly passionate about German history. A very thorough tour and very informative, provided a lot of insight as to what really happened at this camp. I cannot imagine visiting this camp without a guide. It is a must!
Wear comfortable shoes, bring sunscreen, water and snacks. We traveled on a very hot day, there is not a drop of shade there. So be prepared.
Ronan has the rip timed precisely and we were able to easily catch bus and subway home. Thanks for a great experience!

This tour was engaging and full of information from start to finish! Chloe did a phenomenal job presenting the information and explaining the true gravity and seriousness of the places we visited. She connected to each member of the tour group and was able to answer questions not only about the camp but Berlin as well. A+ tour!!!

A very comprehensive visit to the Concentration Camp. It should be longer since there is so much to view and understand. The tour guide kept emphasizing that the camp included political prisoners, others in addition to Jewish people. I wondered if he was trying to minimize the numbers of Jewish prisoners.
The name of the guide was Campbell.
We had a fantastic tour guide during our trip to Sachsenhausen concentration camp. Chloe was so knowledgable and helpful. We would highly recommend this very moving and poignant tour.

We did the Sachsenhausen day tour wth Pip. She was an excellent and knowledgeable guide, and helped us really understand the experiences of the people who were imprisoned at Sachsenhausen as well as the history and political atmosphere of the time. I would definitely recommend going with a tour as it helps you learn much more than if I had visited on my own. Worth it!

Our tour guide was Taylor. Taylor was an excellent guide who made his points with clarity and conviction - he is obviously well versed in the camp's history. I personally loved the end note by him which offered a moment of reflection on the entire experience. The tour was well paced, with nicely summarised information delivered in a truly thought-provoking manner.

We were given this camp to visit on recommendation and it was a fascinating place to visit free to get in although we booked a guided tour and were given some very interesting facts. Would highly recommend this tour

It's very difficult to find the appropriate words to describe this tour. Our Guide Campbel was excellent. His knowledge was superb and he was able to covey the story of the camp in a sensitive but factual way. He was happy to discuss any questions we had and answered everything we wanted to know. His closing speech at the end was very poignant.
Whilst we were apprehensive about how we would feel about our visit we were all incredibly pleased we went and feel it was an important subject to learn more about.
I would recommend this tour.

Our tour guide (went by "Pim") was very knowledgeable and did a great job educating us on this camp. She spent a good amount of time connecting the camp to other events at that time to give context. Overall, a very sobering experience. Definitely worth doing, especially if you haven't been to a concentration camp.

There is a lot of walking in this tour, so be prepared. I'd estimate close to 5 miles. It is possible to cut out about 2 miles by taking a taxi from the Oranienburg train station to the camp and back after the tour. Our tour guide offered that as an option, however no one took a taxi in our group.
Excellent groupr tour guide Nickolai, very Detail, with knowledg on high Level. From first to last minute very helpfull and kind.

Our guide was fantastic, we chose one of the English speaking tour guides from outside McDonalds at the Zooilogical Gardens, we took the Sbahn with our guide, and when we arrived it was a short walk to the camp. From the minute we walked through the gates we felt the heaviness in the air, you can only begin to imagine what those poor people went through, at the hands of evil. The story needs to be told, those lives who perished there cannot be forgotten.

Make sure you pack water and food, wear good shoes, and be prepared to spend your entire day on this tour. There is not much to buy out there, nor is there any time to spend buying it.

Departure is at 10am, very easy to find the guide and your tour.

You will need a Berlin ABC train ticket for the day, which costs about 4 euros. You can buy this at the train station.

If you are unsure how to purchase a ticket, your guide will show you how and will show you how to validate it.

Train trip to Sachsenhausen is ~40-45 minutes. Bus to the camp takes 5-10min, walking ~20mins.

The day is packed with information, multiple stops and a lot of walking in what was a massive concentration camp.

Please beware that some parts of the tour are quite confronting. Not appropriate for young children.

The tour concludes at about 1500-1515. The train back to Berlin is generally faster (~25 mins). The guide will show you exactly where to get off.

Overall a fascinating day, quite sombre and a tad depressing, but a very important part of modern history. A must do for anyone visiting Berlin. The tour itself is, in my opinion, the only way to experience it.

We had Taylor as our guide. He is very experienced and you can tell he is very passionate about that part of German history. He took good care of the group and illustrated in clear and lively terms the life of those requiring protected custody in the camp. Highly recommended joining a tour than self-tour!

Can a concentration camp visit be enjoyable? Well, it certainly can be moving and informative, in no small measure to our tour guide, Brian. He balanced the content of the unemotional numbers of such a place with human stories and a context of how this all arose. Also emphasised that this is living history. This was first camp built especially for purpose of containment and murder, a prototype for larger concentration and extermination camps. One of the interesting aspects was how the East Germans presented their view through their prism. Soviets also used this camp as internment place with many casualties. The whole tour is a reminder to the inhumanity of man, but does end on note of hope that future generations do not forget. Highly recommended.

It was eyeopening and once in a lifetime experience. Very nice because it's located near Berlin, you just need to have ticket zone A-C to get here. From the station, you can walk for 20 min or take a bus to get to the camp.
This camp is originally made by the Soviet for their war prisoner, so inside you will find the camp museum when in Soviet regime. By paying 4euro you will get an audio guide, I recommend you to use this. Some of the building is still there with all facilities such as toilet bedding and drawers.

My partner and I visited Sachsenhausen with Ronan. Whilst it was obviously a delicate subject matter, the tour was carried out very respectfully and Ronan was a grand guide. He had vast knowledge on the site and this era in history. Questions were encouraged and answered enthusiastically and in depth, just what you would want from a guide. We were so impressed with the tour we came back on our final day for another tour, again with Ronan leading us through the city centre giving us even more of his knowledge and experience of Berlin. We would both thoroughly recommend both this tour and Ronan as a guide. Thanks a million.

Perhaps the word great isn't the best way of describing a tour around such a sobering historical site. But the information provided and the depth of knowledge from our tour guide Mike was second to none. Definitely one of the best tours I've been on. Every question was answered with enthusiasm and a genuine interest in educating people about the importance of this site and once the tour proper was over and we were heading home, Mike spent a good 15 minutes helping us with ideas for the rest of our trip, to make sure we got as much from our time in Berlin as possible. Highly recommended!

Brian was are tour guide and did a great job taking us through this tour. He has a great understanding of the data but most important, presented the information in impartial and respectful way.

Watchout for older Travelers: a lot of walking and more of an eat on the go type tour.
Best tour in Berlim so far, Chloe knew so much about the camp. A very important place to visit to help us not forget what happened and avoid it in the future.

This tour covers the concentration camp at Oranienberg just outside Berlin. Taylor was an excellent guide; he’s very knowledgeable and has a lovely style of presenting what is some pretty confronting subject matter.

When My partner asked me to do the 6 hour tour of Sachsenhausen I was very hesitant but I must say I am very pleased that we did. I never knew a lot about the atrocities and events that occurred in this camp other than from watching a few movies and reading history books that I skimmed over as a kid. I always thought that forgetting the past or blocking it out was far easier than actually knowing what some humans were capable of during these times. It wasn’t until I spent 4 hours walking around this concentration camp with a small group of people from various parts of the world and a tour guide who had more knowledge about the history of this camp than any history book I have read that I truely understood what pain and suffering those that were sent there went through. Having someone as articulate, knowledgeable and compassionate as our tour guide Jamie made the tour something that I will always remember. For those that are interested in the history of this camp the wars that led to these types of camps being built then I thoroughly recommend that if you can book in with Jamie from Inside Tours you will not be disappointed.

We had Mike as our tour guide last month and he was the best tour guide that we've ever had! He was very knowledgeable, friendly and provided lots of clear information. He seemed passionate and set his voice at the right tone, appropriate for the trip. We would definitely recommend this tour with Mike!

Lucy and Ben

Guide was Campbell whose knowledge and enthusiasm helped sustain us through a hot day's walking around the camp. Recommend this trip. Apologies to Campbell for losing you on the return from Oriander. We rushed off the bus up the first set of stairs and onto the slow train back to Berlin. Your tip will have to wait for the next trip! My daughter forbade me from taking any photographs in the camp and, on reflection, I agree with her. Checking into Sachsenhausen on Facebook with a selfie in front of the ovens is missing the point.
This tour was so informative and Taylor knew so much about this camp He really got us to understand how it all took place. Excellent tour really worth a visit

An exceptional tour and something that is simply a must if you are touring Berlin.
Our guide, Rob Shaw was terrific and not only knew his subject matter inside out, he delivered that knowledge in a manner that truly allowed each individual the opportunity to explore and understand the reasons why such abhorrent acts were committed by once ‘normal’ people.
Although the site and general subject matter is naturally disturbing, Rob taught us the reasons why honouring and remembering the suffering of these men, women and children is so important for today’s and future generations.
My wife and I also attended the half day Berlin walking tour the day before, which was also excellent and is where we met Rob. Highly recommend both tours and specifically recommend Rob.

Paul & Rachel

Our guide Taylor was so knowledgeable and understanding. I really felt that he went out of his way to ensure everyone heard what he was saying and was always saying if people had any more questions just to ask. It was an extremely hot day and everyone was exhausted by the end of the it and he made sure that everyone knew where they were going and what train stop to get off on and was just all round a nice guy! Would definitely recommend this tour!

Just wanted to say what a gem of a tour guide Brian Bell was on our walking tour of Sachsenhausen. He was friendly, sensitive, so well informed and gave us perspectives and thought-starters that went well beyond the regular tour guide purview. Highly recommended. Thanks Brian.

Joined this tour to visit The Sachsenhausen concentration camp. Yan was our guide and he gave us a very insightful tour of the camp. Visiting it was sad to think how other humans could inflict such pain n do such murderous things to fellow human beings. We enjoyed the trip tremendously. It's a long walk and not for the faint hearted.

The Insider Tour led by Yan made this an incredibly memorable experience. Yan is one of the most professional, helpful and courteous guides in the business. He explained the history of this awful place with detailed precision, passion and moreover with sensitivity.His knowledge of not only the camp but of the historic background is expert in nature and moreover understandable. It was a truly moving experience and one we shall never forget ! Thank you Yan. Rob and Jan

We, my son and I have participated the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp Tour with Taylor as our guide. He has been an exellent guide (pretty clear voice) with so much interesting knowledge and respect about the history of all you can see during the tour. He told us we should walk te same way as de victims who are brought to the camp. It was a bit creepy to realise what these people has to deal with during the walk. When we arrived at the camp he had extra information about this part of history wich you (I) never learned at school. He let you feel the past if you are in it. After the tour he leads us to your next destination. It was a very nice experience. Thank you Taylor for making our first visit to Berlin such a success.
Have a nice summer. Dennis and Tineke from The Netherlands

Having been in Berlin before we were looking at other activities and found out about this company on TripAdvisor. We decided to book the tour to the concentration camp as our first visit. Our tour guide was Josh and he was superb. He was interested in all of the group and spent time speaking with all of us. He was very informative and more than happy to answer any of our questions despite most likely having being asked them all before. Whilst on the tour he gave an insight into the workings of the camp and the people in them, who would be placed there and the reasons behind their incarceration. He allowed us time to look at the displays, giving us time to think about the conditions people were living under. It is always disturbing when reminded of the cruelty that individuals can inflict on others for their own gain. Enjoyable would be the wrong word to use in describing this tour but it is something that people should see at least once and Josh made it a very worthwhile experience

I've been traveling around Europe and signing up for every war-related tour out there, including Aushwitz and Dachau. This was the best one yet. Why? First, our tour guide Mike was fantastic. If you can somehow request him, I highly recommend it. He's an experienced historian with a great voice and perfect energy level. He kept things lively throughout while displaying the proper respect for the somber subject matter at all times (no canned jokes here). And as a bonus, he took us to the camp administration building (unique to his tour) which was fascinating, happily solicited and answered questions, gave Berlin-related recommendations to anyone who asked, and even helped people get home faster by asking where they were staying. He literally catered to 20 individual people. Amazing! Second, the camp itself was very interesting. I knew little about it going in yet found myself researching it further that same night. A great experience. Five enthusiastic stars!

Went with my daughter. Taylor was our guide and was excellent. Very knowledgeable and always made sure there was the opportunity to talk or ask questions. Looked after everyone very well. Highly recommended

So this is not a trip that is fun in any way. You are visiting a very sombre space and though they keep reminding you that you can spend many hours here, I doubt I could spend any more time here. The history weighs heavy as does the extraordinary evidence gathered and meticulously displayed. There are remnants of terrible times, sometimes worse, and you are constantly reminded of what human beings can do to each other.

The only element that made today’s tour bearable was BRIAN. If you can, specifically request the tour he will lead and I guarantee you it will be the experience of a lifetime. He constantly reminds you not of what has happened but what could if we are not careful of the future. As a student and later teacher of History and of this period and space specifically, it was rewarding to learn more.

Go to Sachsenhausen for lessons on what human beings can do to each other. Go with Brian to understand what we could do in the future.

(PS: I couldn’t being myself to take any pictures).

Last week I took this tour in Berlin with Insider Tour Walks in English. The guide
was Julian who proved to be excellent. The tour left from Hackescher Markt at 10:00.
We went by train to Oranienburg and then walked over to the camp. Julian has a vast knowledge of the events leading up to and following the building and use of this place as a prison/death camp. It was a hot day and he made sure to lead us into shady areas before speaking. Despite the horrific nature of the information, Julian managed to finish the day on an upbeat and positive note. I highly recommend this tour.

After taking in the historical tours and vists around Berlin, I found that the tour to Sachsenhausen is the final and most compelling piece of the jigsaw to the events leading up to and throughout the Second World War.
The tour sets exactly the right tone between fully communicating the realities of the jconcentration camp, but without being too horrific. If ever there is an experience to promote tolerance between all races, this is it.
The tour does involve train and bus trips to get to the town where Sachsenhausen is located, which is not included in the excursion price (Berlin ABC day ticket €7.70) and you do also need to take your own food and drink. Our English guide Mike Dempsey was simply excellent, very informative and always able to put into context.
An unmissable excursion, which was excellent value.

I absolutely loved this tour! It was a unreal experience. I highly recommend Michael, he was a great guide throughout the whole trip. He really cared about the group and new everything. He also helped me find my next stop after the tour was over!

This tour was excellent in every way. There weren’t too many people on the tour so we felt that we received good, attentive service from the extremely knowledgeable guide. The meeting point and the train journey was well managed. I found it particularly poignant to walk from the station to the camp as the poor prisoners would have done. I have previously visited other concentration camps but this one really affected me. The tour was excellent and extremely informative. Well worth a visit

Taylor our tour guide was like we say in Icelandic Algjör meistari very knowledgeable about the camp and history.He made the day really memorable and i highly recommend this trip.

Kveðja frá Íslandi.

We visited Sachsenhausen today with Jamie as our guide.

We met them in West Berlin at the train
Station where everybody was organised into groups. Jamie was friendly and ensured everybody had the correct tickets for the train and made sure we had food and drink for the day.

Jamie was incredibly knowledgable and passionate about the subject and gave us lots of information in a sensitive and evidence based manner. It was a really hot day (33 degrees!) and he timed his information talks/information nicely so we could stand in the shade. Jamie also spoke to us all on the train to give us the opportunities to ask him questions and to give us any tips on other places to visit.

I am incredibly impressed with the tour and even more so with Jamie. This is definitely value for money and totally worth it!!!

Thank you very much
Very interesting day out with a brilliant tour guide Mike very nice guy who knows his stuff and very interesting to talk to. Would recommend to anyone who wants to go

Me and my wife had an awesome day visiting Sachsenhausen Cincentration Camp museum with our wonderful guide Brian, a Texan now living in Berlin and involved in the theatre industry.

He was vastly knowledgeable and passionate about the subjects and atrocities concerning the Nazi's and the area in and around the camp, while also coming accross as a funny easy going guy who would take time to answer any questions you have.

I would highly recommend thus tour.

Campbell, our tour guid, is knowledgeable and very helpful. He taught us good history lesson about Nazi time , and how things deteriorated. Campbell showed us dark side of human nature and whether it is still happening in modern days. The camp is barren, everything is minimum, no souvenir shop, no cafe, no water fountain, no soft drink machine, no modern technology. We could imagine how miserable it would be like in the camp. Campbell did take good care of us during the 6 hour trip, and gave us recommendations to restaurants and other places of Berlin. Much appreciated.

Met at 10am and made our way by train with our Italian tour guide, Daniele. Great command of English and he was well read and informative about the camp. It’s a very different camp from Auschwitz: dreadfully sad but, for me, not as emotive. Nevertheless, it’s well worth a visit. It’s very hot and long. Take water and a sandwich. Would recommend. Grazie tanto, Daniele.

I went with my brother in a group of around 15. The site itself is well preserved and there is tons of text, interactives and exhibits to learn about what happened. Interesting angle to also talk about how the history is remembered because there is a lot of old East Berlin monuments there as well. Our tour guide was Brian, and I thought he did an amazing job, really tied together the history and meaning. He provided a lot of context without minimizing the tragedy.

We booked on trip advisor, which had a very reasonable price, I was in a group with 3 friends and we were assigned Taylor as a tour guide, he was passionate and very knowledgable on the concentration camp, I would highly recommend booking a tour guide then listening to the headset tour that is offered as there is so much to get around. Taylor got us around all the important aspects of the camp in 3 hours and helped us on our journeys from Berlin to our hostel. 1000% recommend this tour if your in Berlin and Taylor as a your guide :)

We will be looking to book another walking tour again and hopefully with Taylor

I am so glad I had the opportunity to visit this concentration camp, especially with a guide. Pip was my guide and she did an amazing job of giving us information about everything we saw. She also gave us a big picture idea about how different aspects of the camp related to the larger picture of the Nazis and Germany. While it was a somber experience, I am glad I went as I learned so much and was able to pay my respects to those who were held and killed in this particular concentration camp.

We returned to Berlin around 4:30, still allowing time to see the city after the tour ended.

Highly recommend this tour.

Our guide Chloe paid close attention to every member attending and was clearly knowledgeable about the topics she discussed. The tour itself was definitely worth it, although I am not sure why they don't make people simply meet in the main train station. We almost lost some people on the way there, and to organize two groups seemed a little unnecessary to me.
However, overall a good experience and definitely worth the visit to learn more about the horrors of the Holocaust.
One of the most haunting and impactful tours I have ever taken. Our tour guide John was fantastic. A must do when coming to Berlin.

We were very lucky to have Brian Bell as our guide. He told an amazing story, explained all aspects of the camp and answered questions without hesitation.

This is a very emotional but necessary tour as we should all be made aware of the horrific suffering these poor people endured. It is upsetting but very humbling.

Well worth a day in our privileged lives!!

I took the tour to Sachsenhausen concentration camp. The tour was well-paced and very interesting. Our guide, Chloe, was interactive and very knowledgeable and filled us with details that we otherwise wouldn't have known had we gone ourselves. I highly recommend this trip to anyone visiting Berlin.

Our tour guide, Brian Bell, did an excellent tour; he managed to condense as much factual information into the 6 hour tour and was very helpful with all of the group's questions. Would highly recommend for anyone who would like to understand more about the horrific time period that was the Holocaust. (On a side note, he also made sure that we all knew where we were going at the end of the tour and gave us recommendations for whatever we wanted)

This was the most meaningful tour that I have taken. Brian, our guide, was very well informed, passionate and provided valuable insights into the days when the camp was functional. One can imagine the agony of those imprisoned in the camp, their hopelessness, the extreme cruelty and indignity they went through. An extremely insightful, sobering and memorable visit. Simply amazing!

Taylor was our guide to Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp, a short train trip from Berlin. The destination itself was fascinating, but Taylor made it an even more memorable experience.
