He was very knowledgeable, gave a very clear and concise insight into the historical period and the events which led up to the creation of these camps. He was passionate about his topic, while at the same time being fair and even-handed - and also keen to have us understand that this type of abhorrent event could be repeated unless people are aware of, and prepared to resist, the erosion of democratic institutions. He was also very well organised. Highly recommended. Bill Versteegh

We had a fantastic time with our very in depth guide Ronan. It was very apparent that he was interested in the subject matter. He managed a group of 20 tourists very well and worked us through all the areas and history of the camp.

The camp tour is amazing and I am happy that I took the tour from Insider tour. Our guide Campbell was very knowledgeable and organized. We took a train from Berlin for this tour. The walk is long for this one but its worth the effort.

Even though it is upsetting to think about and indeed find out more about what happened there, it's a very important part of history, and in my opinion a must-see. You will learn new things even if you feel you know a lot about World War 2. The (double-decker!) train journey there and back takes no time at all, and even though the trip is about 3 hours, it's worth it for everything you learn about, and to give you time to have a look at the exhibits in the remaining buildings. It's a surreal experience to realise you are literally standing where prisoners once stood. We went on a fairly hot, sunny day, which although perhaps lessening the severity of the atmosphere of the place, hits home to you how bad conditions could get for those imprisoned there. Seeing the homes around the camp is disturbing, knowing people live within such close proximity. Our guide Chloe was great, she had an effective way of explaining the history of what happened there, as well as what led up to its development, keeping everyone hooked, and encouraging reflection. She was very friendly throughout the trip, ensuring everyone made it to their next destinations once we got back to the meeting point after the tour. For what you pay, the trip is definitely worth it. I would recommend wearing comfortable footwear, there is a LOT of walking, and taking food and drink- it feels strange to do this at a concentration camp, but you will need it. You are also free to take photos if you wish.

This is one of the smaller camps but nevertheless all of the horrors you associate with such camps were perpetrated here. The tour also included the building from where the entire concentration camp network was run. Made all the more disquieting by its tranquil charm.
We went by train so be prepared to walk further than you may think (about 20 minutes from the station plus walking around the camp itself), and be sure to take some lunch and drink as there isn't time to stop for lunch.

Our guide Chloe was very informative and insightful and kept the tour moving at a decent pace but with short breaks to rest and recover . It would be very easy to linger because there is a lot to take in. Chloe gave us the option to stay at the end to spend more time at the camp rather than return with the group if we wished. This wasn't a problem as getting back to the station and catching the train was easy. Chloe also ensured that every member of our group got to the relevant station and departure point. She was very good.

This tour wasn't just about Sachsenhausen, we got great historical perspective on the Nazi Germany buildup leading to Sachsenhausen's development plus an overview of how the property's been used afterwards, and a glimmer of how in the balance its future lies, now that the generation of camp victims and workers is nearly depleted. My uncle and aunt were visiting Berlin from Wisconsin, it was such a meaningful experience for us touring Sachsenhausen together. Our guide Josh was tremendously knowledgable, personable, entertaining and a very conscientious tour leader. He had tons of relevant book and movie recommendations; and gave us great tips for transportation and further sightseeing on the train ride back to Berlin.

This was a very sombre but worthwhile experience. We travelled by train and undertook a three hour guided tour of the camp which provided a very informative and thorough overview of what took place therin. Audio guides are available for self guided tours, but having a tour guide gave me the opportunity to ask additional questions - special thanks to our guide JJ for answering them - and I'd recommend anyone wanting to visit the camp, to sign up for a guided tour.

I am glad I had a rental car to come here as it is less than an hour from Berlin. This marks the first visit to a concentration camp and I am glad that I came. The most reflecting part of this visit was to see the execution trench, and to see the crematorium with what it seems to be actual residue from its victims. It is amazing to think that there are some people in this world that proclaims this never happened, in spite of undeniable and insurmountable amount of evidence for anyone to see that has half a brain. A must see for anyone that has never been to a concentration camp from this dark era of humanity.

Although this day visit was harrowing, we are really glad it was part of our trip. You can get an audio tour in your chosen language for 3 euros each and you get a map included. The information was very detailed and informative, it really gave you a sense of what it was like in the camp. Wouldn’t say we ‘enjoyed’ hearing about all the awful things that happened here, but we definitely learnt a lot.

We had Brian as a tour guide! He was great! Full of information, really comfortable asking him questions etc . Before the tour I thought it was going to be like a school excursion but it was nothing like it! Seriously recommend, it was an eye opening day and I learnt so much more by having the tour guide than I would of walking around on my own! Every room was explained and Brian had stories to go along with it

First time visitor to a concentration camp and I am so glad I did it. Our guide Josh was fantastic and so informative, I learned so much history from him that I didn't know before hand. Even though it is not a happy thing to learn about it is so important to know and a must at least one time in your life. Well worth doing for everyone. Highly recommend.
Chloe was an excellent guide giving a thought provoking and well rounded insight into the events and lives caught up in this harrowing time and place. Thoroughly recommended.

Would thoroughly recommend this tour. Chloë our guide was extremely informative,friendly and even helped with directions of getting home and to the airport. The tour itself was very informative and well worth the small fee

Alecia from walks in English was our tour guide, she really shared the deep, intense history of the concentration camp with us! She really has great knowledge of the happenings and history of the camp. The tour itself is very emotional, but I would recommend it to anyone who has an interest in the history of Germany.

The reviews on trip advisor made me book this tour because of the comments on the guides and my experience is totally in line with everyone else. Josh was friendly, exceptionally knowledgeable, and open to any and all questions that we had. He really made this an experience, keeping the tone right from the station to the camp and back again.
No matter how hard people may find it, I think this is a must-do to learn about such recent and terrible history, and this tour is an excellent way to learn about it.

On Monday 9th April we (8 girlfriends and I) had an absolutely amazing and fascinating Sachsenhausen tour by Chloe. She told everything very interesting with much knowledge. it was not boring at all (although 6 hours seemed very long in advance!) Keep up the good work, Chloe and thanks again for a very interesting experience from the 9 Dutch women.

Ronan is an outstanding communicator. He brought this tour to life by explaining how the Nazi regime impacted on the everyday life of inmates in Sachenhausen in straightforward terms. Clearly a highly educated individual he also loves his subject and is able to impart his vast knowledge effortlessly. We are so lucky to have been on his tour and would highly recommend. Very pleasant and helpful during fascinating tour.

We had Mike for our tour and he was brilliant. He was really knowledgeable, showed us lots of photos on the train and on the tour. It was really well organised and easy to get to the concentration camp. It was a short train journey, about half an hour to the camp and then we spent 3 hours walking around the camp, which was fascinating. We would definitely recommend it!

Quality! 100% recommend. Our first ever walking talking tour. It was brilliant. Our guide Brian was full of information and knowledge. Very helpful and polite. Also kept checking up on us regular. The tour itself was worthwhile.

Thank you Brian for making this grim experience slightly better.

N&D (UK).

We did this tour 2 weeks ago with Chloe and it was well worth the 6 hours (including travel time) . Chloe has a passion f r and a deep interest in history which was evident as she guided us around and filled us in on the history of Geramany from around the perios of the 20's 30s and 40s and her love of Berlin is also very clear. We had a good day. A trip to theconcentratin camp provided us with ample information and is well worth spending your time on. Bring water and a packed lunch with you if you are going. There is a small cafe just outside the camp but we did not visit it. Travel to and from is relativley simple and with the asistance of our lovely friendly guide we were all given advice on which train or bus to take to return to our destinations .

I took my 12 & 13 yo kids on the Insider Tour of Sachsenhausen. Mike, the guide, made the day interesting and appropriate for all of us. There is a lot to see at the camp but we came away with an understanding of the camp’s history from the 1930s to the present day. I am glad I didn’t attempt this day trip on my own. It was worth having someone that knew the journey and the camp to guide us at every point. I highly recommend Mike and Insider Tours tour of Sachsenhausen. Great value for money.

This tour is definitely something everyone needs to experience at least once in their life. Our tour guide Campbell made it a million times easier to get through some of the provokative places of the camp. He was extremely informative, friendly and passionate, and made sure everyone was on the same page. He went beyond just statistics and facts and added individual stories which made it a lot more interesting and real- so you attempt to understand what the actual victims of war went through. Would highly recommend.

Thought provoking, moving and at times shocking tour of this concentration camp.
Our guide Campbell was clear speaking and well organised.
Thoroughly recommended!

Our tour guide was Warren (Darren), the Irish guy. He was very knowledgable about the topic as it is what he is passionate about. He made sure all we all knew where we were going, so that no one stayed behind. He stopped along the way to introduce the Nazi era. He made sure he everyone understood what he was saying and was open to questions and comments. He told the history from an unbiased point of view leaving the information to our interpretation and conclusions. He delivered the information in such a way that made you feel you were there, maybe sitting in a college class, being immersed in all this history. He was wonderful.

Our group of teachers went to this site too late in the day to have a guided tour. However, the people at the front desk were very helpful and saw to it that we knew where to go and had a walk-around self-guided tour thingy (can't think of what to call it) and where we should go first. It was a meaningful experience and we learned a lot about what happened here those many years ago. Great experience!

Tour guide Ronan went above and beyond giving a fantastic guide and even helped us find a bar to get the 1 litre beers!! (We asked for this information..), an absolute gentleman! Fantastic tour! Dublin thanks you

Our tour guide Darren made this experience for us! He went above and beyond with an in-depth insight into the history of concentration camps across Europe and also for Sachenhausen. His knowledge is amplified by the fact he is doing a PhD in this area and it really shows with the quality of information you receive.

The perspective he approached with the concentration camps and their purpose made for an immensely enjoyable, insightful and worthwhile day.

Mike was a great tour guide, very knowledgeable! Kept the group engaged through the visit, really good at time keeping as well! The camp was a very moving experience would recommend. Would recommend mike as a tour guide to all my friends.

We could not have had a better guide than Phil. He was truly an expert who’s obvious passion for the subject added so much to our visit. The tour itself was well organised, easy to follow and definitely the highlight of our trip to Berlin. Well done Phil!

Found all necessary information clearly presented on website whilst planning this trip. Very well organised tour from meeting the team outside Zoologischer Garten station and throughout the entire visit. Our guide Brian Bell absolutely made the day. His knowledge and presentation of a dark subject was done with respect and care for his group. Despite very cold weather adults and teenagers found the visit both fascinating and thought provoking. Brian looked after us superbly including making sure everyone was happy with their onward travel arrangements at the end of the trip. His insight was essential in making this an experience we will all always remember. We felt very lucky to have had him as our guide. Vielen dank Brian Bell.

From the very beginning of the tour we felt welcomed to Mike’s team. Throughout the 45 minute train ride there we were given great background information to help us understand the context of the camp. Mike was always conscious of the needs of the group members and handled difficult topics with sensitivity. VIsiting the camp and hearing the stories of those in the camp was a profoundly moving experience and will lead to much further thought. Following the tour Mike made sure each of us knew where we were going next and pointed us on our way

A terrific tour and Jamie was the reason why. Very informative a pleasure to be with for 6 hours. He was very attentive to all on the tour and made sure we were accounted for. This tour was very informative and told the story that the world should never forget. A must tour when in Berlin. The train ride was easy.

Despite the very cold temperatures this was an awesome day. Our gratitude goes to Mike, who with an abundence of knowledgle was able to share the key points of the German history in order for us to fully appreciate the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp. Mike inspired the whole group with his passion and knowledge of the WWII era and went above and beyond as a tour guide, ensuring that everyones needs were met. We left this tour with a wider understanding and memories to last a life time. What an incredible tour, Thank you Mike! Highly recommended!

First of all mike was an awesome guide , completely in love with his job , so passionate, so kind . A human being with so much knowledge is a gift to appreciate
He will do everything so the tour can be perfect for you
I think one of the reasons this tour was a success was because of him .
Delicate and specially sad subjects are treated during this whole tour , that’s why a sensitive guide is needed to explain to you the saddest place in earth .
The camp is the one with most ancient ORIGINAL buildings , and one of the biggest .
As reminded , this is not a “ happy tour “ is a tour to acknowledge from a more close angle what really happened during those terrible years so we can not repeat the same mistake again .
Experience full of knowledge totally worth it if coming to Berlin
Only stayed 3 days in Berlin and I don’t regret a second

It was a well organised tour with our guide Mike meeting us at the station and making sure we all were sorted and knew what we needed and had everything. Easy going Kiwi who had great knowledge of everything with the history as well as some wonderful German insults thrown his way. The tour itself was interesting and well orgainsed being able to see everything at a reasonable pace. I would highly recommend doing this tour as well as this company (Insider Tour) as it was just spot on for what you need. On top of the tour itself when we were on the train back Mike took the time to make sure we all knew where to go or what to see and do/ eat or drink for the remainder of the trip. I thought this added touch was a class act. John Jerome the other guide out that day also made sure that me and my partner knew how to get back to the airport when we departed. All round a well run company.

HIGHLY RECOMMEND! I only had 2 full days in Berlin which made it tough to decide whether to do this tour or explore the city. SO happy with the decision of choosing to go on this tour because it is most definitely an experience I will never forget. Our tour guide, Mike, was the best! Super kind guy who went up and above his job as a tour guide by really taking care of the group and making sure we were getting the most of our time. His intelligence combined with his passion for sharing his knowledge made it an unforgettable experience.

Brian bell was amazing and really brought this sombre tour to life. our kids were fascinated and the way he crafted the the day made it very interesting. highly recommend this fantastic tour with high remarks to Brian bell who made it better.

We booked this tour over the internet. Well worth doing. We checked arrangements the day before and were given clear instructions in English. The day was very well organised and MIKE our tour guide was very knowledgeable and extremely passionate about the site and its history. We would recommend this tour to anyone but be sure to dress up warm if you are going in Winter: The site is very open. Remember to take a packed lunch as there was no time to stop at the cafe.

The tour to Sachsenhausen concentration camp should definitely be on your To Do list whilst in Berlin. Mike Stack was our tour guide and he is absolutely phenomenal. Mike, is very knowledgeable about the history and the camp. He was able to answer all our questions in detail and made the tour interesting. Mike gets you to think about things in a unique way and has left a lasting impression on all of us who attended the tour. There are many tour guides out there, but Mike is different in the sense, that he went the extra mile for us all, we learned so much from the tour and this tour has touched each one us. Thank you.

This is hands down the best tour I have ever been on.

Mike was friendly, welcoming and highly knowledgeable, not just about Sachsenhausen and the holocaust, but about the overall history of Berlin. He is so forthcoming with information and more than happy to have a conversation or answer any questions you might have.
I learnt far more about Berlin on this tour about than I would have otherwise, and have a greater love and appreciation for the city.

Couldn't recommend enough.

My friend and I LOVED our experiences today seeing the camp. Mike our tour guide was very knowledgeable and entertaining. He definitely made the trip so much more educational and worth while. This is a must do trip if you are in Berlin for a couple of days. Highly recommend!
Amazing experience. Our guide - Mike - was excellent, so knowledgeable and passionate about everything he showed us and told us about. This is a must when you visit Berlin. Thank for a great day out.

We did 2 tours with Insider Tours over the course of our city break in Berlin. Mike really went above and beyond in giving advice and tips on our visit to Berlin. He was extremely knowledgeable and handled extremely difficult subject matter with tact and sensitivity. Would definitely use again.

tour guide Josh very helpful very friendly helped with train ticket
good knowledge of tour
very cold bring warm clothing [February]
good value for money

We recently had our first visit to Berlin, our tour guide was Josh and he was just fantastic. His knowledge, stories and passion he had for his tour was shown through his delivery.
Would recommend to anyone who loves history and just wants to know more.
Just a quick tip, take your coats its absolutely freezing.
Nickolai proved to be an excellent guide. Friendly, fun and full of information regarding the camp. Would not hesitate to recommend Nickolai for this activity.
A very bleak day at the concentration camp, however the tour was superbly organised and the commentary was absolutely amazing. Michael really knows his stuff......thanks for an informative day!

Our tour guide Nickolai was extremely well educated on all subjects of the tour and delivered the tour brilliantly with a strong respect for the sombre subject matter and towards those who suffered in the camp. The camp itself is an eerie yet interesting experience which everyone should take the time to discover as a dark, yet crucial part in human history which should not be forgotten.
The tour is a must do when visiting Berlin. Its a full day's activity and for a very good price. You will leave with a much greater. Understanding of the horrors of the holocaust and respect for those who went through it.

Thanks so much to Taylor (our guide) from insider tour company for looking after a bunch of Liverpudlians so handsomely. We wanted to visit, but like most felt apprehensive about visiting Sachenhausen. The whole day was emotional, but had to be done. We arrived on a bitterly cold day and still cant imagine how awful it was when the camp was in use. Taylor was so knowledgeable about the camp and gave an amazing insight into the atrocities and conditions of the camp, which we have all taken away with us. Such s kind caring, helpful guide.

Nickolai was our tour guide. Very Good all round tour - promptly run, well organised, competitive price (17 euros each). Nickolai gave a good well rounded presentation on the context, relevant history and extracts of day to day life in the camp - also Nickolai was very informative and helpful in guiding us towards other attractions and nightlife in Berlin. There is a lot to 'take on board' after you visit Sachenhausen and the tour covers a lot of ground - however if you need further time to contemplate what you have seen you may want to consider the option taking some time after the tour and then making your own way back to Berlin (its a 20 minute train journey from Berlin and a 15 minute (easy) walk from the camp to the local train station

What an impressive day tour! Hosted by Insider tours that took care of us from beginning 10.00 am until about 15.30 pm. Where most tours directly get into the concentrationkamp, our guide "Amazing" Mike (a.k.a. J.D.), started at the headquarter building where all the Camps throughout Europe were controlled. Mike made this day perfect by clear explanation, his hospitality and appropriate humor concerning the subject of the trip. No question was too much. On our trip it was windy, snowing and freezing cold, but was the perfect setting to get a good feel what it meant for the people then. Not only stories about WW2 but also about the Sovjet period came across. A must do when visiting Berlin.

While Sachsenhausen is a tough venue, our well organised and knowledgeable tour guide, Jamie, gave us an excellent day. The day was very cold but Jamie was flexible and got us into warmer or sheltered places where he could. The journey was well explained and help given. You do need the extra zone tickets whether you leave from East or West Berlin meeting points. Be prepared with all the food and drink for the day already purchased, arrive with a coffee in hand. It's a full day from 10am - 4:30pm, from meeting point to getting off the train at the end. Jamie also gave us help for where we wanted to go next, talking to everyone individually.

An emotional and tiring tour of Sachsenhausen made all the better by our fabulous guide Alicia. I would highly recommend this tour the guides and organization were top notch from the moment we arrived at the meeting point.

Me and my partner did this tour with Nickolai today. We could not of wished for a better guide. We arrived at the East Berlin station at half 9 and he was already there. He made sure we had the right train tickets, told us where we could get dinner from. (very important you have dinner with you or there is nowhere to purchase any) He was extremely knowledgeable and took the time to explain everything to us, answered any questions I had, ensured everybody was together before starting a talk. He even made sure everybody knew where they was going on the trains back, took the time to speak to every group to tell them which stops to get off at depending on where they were staying. He was a fantastic guide from start to finish! Thank you Nickolai!

Highly recommended tour.

If you are after a single-day walking tour with a knowledgeable tour guide, this is the tour for you.

Our guide - Nickolai - was brilliant, both in herding us to the different locations and providing information and anecdote to bring the location to life.

If you are looking to take your time and really absorb everything the camp has to offer - you might need to stay back from the tour afterwards and make your own way back to Berlin. The tour is just that - a tour - and moves quite fast. Couple with the site itself being massive and we did miss a few things.

Overall though - excellent.

Went on this tour not knowing what to expect,but was really glad we took the time to book it.
Mick our guide was absolutely superb in his ability to convey the message across as to what a terrible time ‘this was in history
His knowledge was fantastic and his enthusiasm brilliant
Well worth the money

I did this tour with my two friends in January and found it really educational. Our tour guide Mike made the tour even better. He was helpful, friendly and really made a good impression. The tour was so easy to find and the day flew. I would recommend the insider tour to anyone of any age (we are 19). A overall great experience.

My husband, two adult son’s and myself took part in ‘The Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp Tour from Berlin’. This was a tour we ‘questioned’ prior to making a booking based on our understanding of this part of history.
Mike from Insider Tour’s did a fanstastic job in describing the living conditions at Sachsenhausen and delivered an insight into the psychology of both prisoners and the SS. Mike’s knowledge on this era of history was excellent. Member’s of our group asked questions during the course of our tour and Mike was well informed to answer all inquiries. We all (family) agreed at the end of the tour that whilst it may not be a ‘pleasant activity’ compared to other tours on offer, it is a tour that must be experienced by all.
We also appreciated Mike’s information on how to make the correct public transport ticket purchase for our family!
I would highly recommend this tour.
Taylor was a fantastic guide, who really knew his stuff and was very helpful and accomodating to everyone on our tour. The highlight of our trip to Berlin

Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp is one of the places everybody has to visit. And if you do go with Insider Tour, make sure you get in Campbell's group. This place is not about facts or figures, a tour guide who read a few Wikipedia entries simply won't do, you need someone who understands the relevance and context. Campbell is a historian, he's great in providing context and helping you understand the important things about Sachsenhausen.

Taylor is great, I enjoy the tour a lot. I would be impossible to cover all the exhibits without Taylor’s highlight. His extensive knowledge about history helped so much in explaining not only the camp but the overall context. One of the best tour I have ever been to.

We had an excellent guide - Phil. It is not an easy place to visit but he made it so interesting and presented an insight into just how many people knew that these atrocities were taking place but did not act to stop them because of the fear of reprisals. The tour was very well organised and Phil was very helpful with travel arrangements. Phil also relayed information that he had gained from previous visitors who had personal family stories to tell. I would thoroughly recommend that you book this tour.
Our guide Taylor was brilliant. He was extremely knowledgeable and very friendly. Would definitely recommend doing this tour if you are in berlin. Shocking to see and hear what went on there.

A tour of a concentration camp can't possibly be described as pleasant. However, our guide Taylor made the outing to Sachsenhausen a very interesting, engaging and respectful experience. I highly recommend both the tour and Taylor as a guide!

This isn't the first time I've been to a place like this, having visited Bergen/Belsen a few years ago.

I think I got a lot more from this visit, though. Taylor was a first-class and compassionate guide, regularly making sure his 'teams' were in tow. He had a deep knowledge of Sachsenhausen's history and told it with a real fervour.

I would definitely recommend this tour to anyone interested in going. As deep and disturbing as the subject matter is, I also felt that it's great to have the history and circumstances of the holocaust delivered to oneself first-hand and this tour was perfect in that regard.
A easy way to adventure into more of the history of Nazi Germany with an excellent guide (Wouter). Highly recommend it. Be sure to wear comfortable shoes and pack food / water.

Alicia has a master's degree in Jewish history and she was just the perfect guide for this tour and replied to every single question anyone had with precise details. Thank you again and good luck with your book soon to be published

Was really looking forward to this tour and it didn't disappoint. The tour guide, Taylor, was outstanding in his knowledge and approach to the sensitive yet important nature of this tour. Everything was run very professionally, right from the initial train ride right up to making sure everyone was advised how to get to where they were going afterwards. The tour itself is around 6 hours in total so great value for money. It was a day I will never forget. Would highly recommend.

Taylor was a great guide, he was very knowledgable about everything from WWI onwards and all the atrocities of what happened at the camp. It snowed while we were there, which made us realise the depths of what the prisoners incarcerated there went through without proper winter clothing. A definite must see if you are in Berlin.

Taylor made the day such an interesting experience and highlighted for me the difference between a 'concentration camp' such as Sachsenhausen and a 'death camp' such as Auschwitz. His historical knowledge of the events that led up to WWII was phenomenal yet he only gave us enough information at each stop to keep us interested rather an overload of facts.It was a fascinating and educational day.
It was bitterly cold the day we visited which in a way added to the 'reality' of the horrors of being incarcerated in such a place in the depth of winter with no proper clothes or footwear, but for us as 'visitors' it would have been nice if there had been somewhere indoors to eat our 'snack lunch' (or whatever anyone had brought with them) and have a hot drink. There was no prior information that indicated it was a 25 minute walk from the station to the camp before walking within the camp itself which was quite extensive-and a 25 minute walk back to the station! Fortunately, everyone in our group was fit enough to cope with this but it would have been a struggle or a big disappointment for anyone who couldn't manage.

What an absolutely fantastic day!! Taylor our guide was brilliant from the start. Helpful and informative. We were a little disorganised having failed to purchase an ABC travel ticket but he helped us so smoothly and easily we were never made to feel an inconvenience. We did the tour with our two teenage children and also our baby son so had a pushchair with us which Taylor accommodated well, directing us to easier options as available - elevators, wider paths, ramps etc. The tour was moving and educational with Taylor pointing out the salient facts and making things seem interesting. The best bit for me was at the end both of our teenagers agreed with us that it was a great day, they were glad they had been, learned a lot and “enjoyed” the day (if that is the appropriate word for a tour of such a sensitive nature. Fantastic for the whole family. We would recommend this tour to anyone visiting Berlin.

This tour with Jamie was a great learning experience. Despite being bitterly cold, Jamie's recount of the events here and during the Holocaust kept me engaged for the entire tour. I highly recommend this tour.

Having previously enjoyed their excellent Famous Insider Tour giving a great introduction to Berlin we booked the Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp full day tour for our next visit.
Again we would highly recommend it.
The tour is well organised and good value for money (10% discount for booking online) with clear joining instructions (you need an ABC Zone Day Travel card (EUR7.70) and a packed lunch). Meeting point in East or West is easy to find.
Our guide, Ronan, was very good. Knowledgeable, clear, considerate and helpful.
Sachsenhausen is well worth a visit with much to learn about its history and the time. So much easy to visit with a guide than on your own because it is very spread out with various buildings and points of interest. Plus it is easier to catch the bus from the train station than walk to it following a map.
This was excellent value for money and I would highly recommend visiting Sachsenhausen and specifically with Insider Tours.

Several weeks ago, Insider Tour guide Brian Bell provided a memorable historical visit to Sachsenhausen Concentration Camp. Our small tour group met Brian in central Berlin before travelling out by train to Oranienburg. This took about 45 minutes. The camp is then a short 15-20 minute walk from the station. Brian set the historical context of the camp throughout the journey. Once at the camp Brian covered the nature camp and much of what happened to the people who were taken there. This is not easy history. However, Brian is an excellent tour guide and our visit was managed sensitively and comprehensively. The trip was steadily paced and full of insight throughout. Brian was considerate of everyone's needs. On our return to the city, Brian even ensured we all made our train transfers to various destinations across Berlin. I highly recommend this Insider Tour and specifically if you can take it with Brian Bell. Our family enjoyed his expert knowledge and warm demeanor.

Well organised with clear meeting place. The tour itself was very informative and emotional.
Guide was Pippa, very knowledgeable and helpful from the early offing right up to ensuring everyone knew which train to take home.

This tour wasn't just incredibly informative and enlightening, but necessary. This is a piece of human history that should never be forgotten, and should be understood as much as possible by any who visit. Our guide was Nikolai, who did a fantastic job!

My girlfriend and I decided to take an educational tour of the nearest concentration camp to Berlin. And our first find was Insider Tour. And an amazing find it was! Our guide Taylor knew his stuff! He helped us get to Oranienburg via train, gave us a walking tour heading up to the camp entrance, and has an aura about him that keeps you attentive and engaged in what he had to say. Being a very sensitive topic such as that of the horrors of the camp, he certainly spoke wholeheartedly of what occurred in this camp, as well as telling very good accounts of each building and monument in the camp we visited. We were also given breaks in between to take in our surroundings and read up on some memorial accounts. Finally, Taylor was very helpful at helping us get back to our destination after the trip was over. Hats off to you mate!

Also a special mention to the guides we met briefly at the station before our tour began. All friendly and helpful. Thank you all very much!
